News.title: Is Farage right to shut down the entire asylum system? VOTE NOW
News.content:
Next

REFORM’S Nigel Farage has pledged to shut down the entire asylum system if his party gets into power.

Under his plans, a “national security emergency” would be declared and all asylum tribunals would be suspended, along with legal refugee routes.



Legal resettlement routes would also be scrapped, including the Homes for Ukraine scheme.

The scheme, named “Restoring Justice”, would mean a stop to any new refugees settling in the UK.



It would also end grants of humanitarian protection – where asylum seekers who do not qualify as refugees but aren’t able to return to their home country due to safety concerns.

Farage also said he would deport 90,000 applicants immediately.

News.title: Moment stepdad has birthday dinner with student, 19, before he ‘murdered her at uni after developing sexual obsession’
News.content:
Next

THIS is the moment a “sexually fixated” stepdad had a birthday dinner with a student before he allegedly murdered her, a court heard.

Carla Georgescu, 19, was discovered dead on what would have been her 20th birthday at the University of Lancashire campus in Preston.



Jurors heard just days before the horror, she had spent the weekend shopping for presents with her mum Janina and watching TV together.

On February 1, Nathan Owens drove from the family home in Hartlepool and joined his wife and stepdaughter for meal at Kimji Korean restaurant.



Preston Crown Court was played footage that showed him and Carla left alone together at one point during the meal.

At the time, Owens had allegedly become “sexually fixated” with his stepdaughter and made a life-size effigy of her to fulfil his sexual fantasy.

Owens also allegedly manipulated innocent selfies of Carla into sexual images and had filmed himself having sex with her anime dolls and a stuffed cat she had bought him.

Following the meal, Owens and Janina were filmed dropping Carla back off at her accommodation, it was said.

Jurors heard just three days later, he drove through the night before parking up in his Ford Puma outside Carla’s university residence.

Footage allegedly showed him shrouding himself in a blanket before making his towards Ribble Hall to murder Carla.



The court was told he left 90 minutes later – “shielding” himself with an umbrella and wearing a face-mask and Carla’s trainers, while carrying two bags.

Jurors heard Owens returned home to Hartlepool where wife Janina said he was his “normal self”.

The mum told the court the couple later went for their regular walk at a nearby beach together and also shopping at an Asda store.



At the time, Carla’s body was lying slumped against a wardrobe door with injuries to her face and a belt tied around her, jurors heard.

Janina raised the alarm when her daughter failed to respond to her messages and phone calls.

After Carla was found on what would have been her 20th birthday, two officers went to the family home and told her she had been found hanged.

Janina told the court she was left “shaking” while Owens “started crying”.

He had hugged and comforted her, she said, but at that point he still didn’t reveal he had travelled to see Carla the day before, she said.



Janina told jurors it was only when she contacted a hospital mortuary and learned more details about her death that he admitted he had been at the flat.

The court heard Owens claimed Carla had wanted him to take incontinence pants to her and help her tidy her room but the prosecution say this was attempt to “cover his tracks”.

When asked by Mr Lumley if she had any reason to “doubt” Owen, Janina replied she didn’t because “it wasn’t inconsistent with his behaviour” and if Carla had wanted him to come he would have.

A post mortem also revealed Carla had been subjected to two heavy blows to her head, slash marks on her cheek and cuts and bruises to her mouth and nose.

Carla’s hands were covered in blood after she attempted to defend herself and she had sexual injuries, the court heard.



The jury was told sex toys and Owens’ DNA were found at the scene.

Mr Lumley said “some form of grievous sexual activity” had taken place which was “hardly surprising” given Owens’ sexual obsession with her.

Jurors were told was possibly driven by “sexual jealousy” after discovering his stepdaughter was due to meet up with a new lover.

Mr Lumley alleged in the months leading up to Carla’s murder, Owens had been collecting photos of her taken without her knowledge.

Owens had also allegedly filmed himself having sex with her dolls and toys – including one that was a life-sized “effigy” dressed in Carla’s nightie.



He was also said to have manipulated innocent selfies of Carla into sexual images which he viewed in the week before she died.

“The only possible reason for looking at those images is that Nathan Owens had a wholly improper and dangerously entrenched sexual obsession with his stepdaughter,” Mr Lumley told the court.

He continued: “Her death was the culmination, the end point, of weeks, months and perhaps years of a one-sided sexual obsession.

“And it was the beginning of a complex murder investigation, which led to his door in Hartlepool.

“For it was he who was sexually fixated on Carla and it was he, Nathan Owens, who had killed Carla.”



Jurors were told Carla – a second year psychology student at the University of Lancashire – was fit and well in the weeks before she died.

The prosecution also alleges Mr Owens removed Carla’s phone and laptop and dumped them on the drive between Preston and Hartlepool.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Owens denies charges of murder, intentional strangulation and grievous bodily harm with intent.

The trial continues.

News.title: Schoolboy, 14, ‘shoots headmaster, 53, & teacher, 37, after opening fire with hunting rifle’ at school in France
News.content:
GUN HORROR Schoolboy, 14, ‘shoots headmaster, 53, & teacher, 37, after opening fire with hunting rifle’ at school in France







Next

A SCHOOLBOY allegedly shot a headteacher after opening fire with a hunting rifle at a school in France.

The boy, 14, was arrested after the principal was wounded at Joseph-Lakanal secondary school in Aubagne, in southern France’s Bouches-du-Rhône department.

A teacher, 37, was also reportedly injured after allegedly being shot by the student on Monday.

The headteacher, 53, was hit in the right hip by a shotgun pellet, reports say.





An investigating source said: “A 37-year-old teacher was also hit in the thigh, as a bullet ricochet. At least four gunshots were heard.

“A 14-year-old teenager has been detained on suspicion of firing the shots. Emergency workers are at the scene.

At least four explosions were heard during the alleged attack, according to local reports.

Figherfighters scrambled to the scene and the two injured teachers were treated, according to sources close to the investigation.



The same sources said the teachers’ wounds are not life threatening.

Mayor Jean-Pierre Squillari confirmed to reporters: “No students were injured,” as worried parents gathered outside the gates.

A criminal investigation for “attempted murder” has been opened up for the suspected shooter, a local newspaper was told by prosecutors.

Édouard Geffray, the Minister of National Education called the alleged attack an “unacceptable act” which “once again demonstrates the rise of unbridled violence in our society.



He added: “A student is said to be the perpetrator. I am heading to the scene immediately with the Interior Minister, Laurent Nunez.

“In the face of this new attack, the National Education system will, as always, remain united and strong, around an educational community sorely tried.

“Faced with this new attack, the National Education system will, as always, stand united and strong, supporting an educational community that has been severely tested,” he wrote on X.

The shooting comes as violent protests have been raging through France for nearly two weeks as furious students hurl projectiles and clash with cops.

More than 71,000 took part in marches across the country last week, the French interior ministry said, including some 24,500 in Paris.



Protestors want the equivalent of at least £9billion put into the education system, to combat dilapidated classrooms and teacher shortages.

Graphic video posted online last week showed the aftermath of the accident near the Béhale high school in Lens, in the north of the country.

The ministry spokesperson warned that violence at the demos is ramping up.

He said there was “an increase in urban violence, on the fringes of the peaceful mobilisations of sixth form students, which has marred their legitimate expression”.

504 people were arrested and 48 police officers injured today alone.



Students from Lycees – the French equivalent of sixth form colleges, for pupils aged 15 – 18 – have been revolting for weeks, initially over conditions in schools.

A source close to the investigation, as well as the Bouches-du-Rhône prefecture, told BFMTV that the shootings had “no connection” with the student protests.

News.title: Tributes to teaching assistant who died in horror crash between two cars – as man, 22, arrested
News.content:
TRAGIC LOSS Tributes to teaching assistant who died in horror crash between two cars – as man, 22, arrested







Next

A TEACHING assistant killed in a horror smash involving two cars has been named as moving tributes flood in for her.

Rachel Spence, who worked at a local primary school, was pronounced dead at the scene after emergency services rushed to the crash.

The tragedy happened in Ashby Road, Hinckley, Leicestershire, shortly before 10.30pm last Monday – October 5.

A grey Hyundai i30 and a silver Vauxhall Agila were involved in the collision near the junction with Barrie Road.





Rachel, who was in her 60s, was driving the Vauxhall.

She was named in a letter to parents from Richmond Primary School, where she worked as a learning support assistant.

A 22-year-old man arrested in connection with the crash has since been released under investigation.

Cops say enquiries are continuing, with officers appealing for witnesses and dashcam footage.

A Facebook page dedicated to Hinckley has paid a touching tribute to the “long-serving” staff member at the school.

The post said: “Our thoughts go out to the family of Mrs Rachel Spence, a long-serving member of staff at Richmond Primary School in Hinckley who has sadly died following a crash on Ashby Road in Hinckley on Monday evening.”

Dozens of locals commented on the announcement expressing their condolences and shock at the news.

One person said: “Thoughts are with her family, friends and colleagues old and new at Richmond.”



Another added: “Sending love, light and healing to her family and friends.”

Somebody else said: “Sending heartfelt condolences to Mrs Spence’s family. My thoughts and prayers go out to you at this devastating time.”

“I had the pleasure of knowing Rachel, she was a lovely lady, thinking of her family at this very sad time,” another added.

One woman said: “Mrs Spence was such a wonderful lady and a loved member of teaching staff at Richmond.

“I knew her well, and I left Richmond in 2008. The amount of time that she was at Richmond shows how dedicated she was to her job and the children.



“I really am thinking of everyone affected by this, and my thoughts are with all that love Mrs Spence, as well as those at Richmond. Love, thoughts and prayers with you all.”

Detective Sergeant Kasie McMahon, from the Serious Collision Investigation Unit, called for witnesses to come forward.

She said: “This incident happened on a main road to and from the town centre in a residential area.

“I believe there will have been people who saw what happened and I’m appealing for witnesses or motorists with dashcam footage to come forward.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

She added: “Any footage or details about what happened that you can provide could help our investigation.”



Anyone with information can report it on the Leicestershire Police website, quoting reference 26*599500.

News.title: Inside sick web of ‘moral-free’ porn sites hosting horror hidden cam & drug rape vids…as paedos ‘mentor’ kids for abuse
News.content:
Next

A SICK porn network fuelled by perverts operating across social media apps, twisted “tutoring” rings and child gaming sites is spreading out of control – even after the closure of a notorious and stomach-churning “moral-free” site.

Among the thousands of horrifying videos uploaded to the Motherless site were those showing abusers sexually assaulting apparently drugged and unconscious victims, investigators have told The Sun.



Warped sex predators filmed and uploaded videos onto the site including dozens filmed in womens’ own homes or from hidden spy cams installed in public loos and changing rooms.

Some depicted women being drugged, abused or staged to look like murders. The horrifying clips of abuse were sent in by users all over the world.

Extensive investigations across the US and Europe uncovered spycam content and women being raped while drugged, eventually leading to Motherless being shut down in July.



Authorities raided multiple buildings across the Netherlands and seized the servers which hosted the depraved content, shutting the website down for good.

But now experts have told The Sun that copycat sites of Motherless are already active and “being built from the ground up”.

Lyn Kennedy, a campaigner for women’s charity Collective Shout, said: “It was basically a free-for-all, no age verification, showing some of the most extreme porn we’ve ever come across.”

Motherless described itself as offering “unusual and extreme fetish”.

Of the 20,000 videos on the site, those tagged “incest” were among the site’s most-viewed categories, according to analysis by CNN.



“They [videos] came from everywhere. No country was off limits.”

Chillingly, Lyn warns that the Motherless site was “a drop in the ocean of what’s out there”.

The campaigner added: “We believe there is at least one copycat up and running at the moment.”



Charity Collective Shout has been surveilling the new site, adding that “every day there is more and more content on it”.

It is unclear whether the porn page has been set up by the original hosts or “Motherless enthusiasts”, explained Lyn, but she added that it showed “a lot of similar content”.

The Sun has independently verified the existence of a second site but cannot confirm whether it contains child sexual abuse material or drug porn content.

Some footage on the former Motherless site was filmed inside public loos, changing rooms at swimming pools or inside clothing stores, according to Lyn.

Screenshots from the website, seen by The Sun, showed one video filmed inside a locker room gaining thousands of views.



Lyn said: “Hidden camera content was particularly disturbing – sometimes it was staged, other times genuine, captured in women’s changing rooms at swimming pools, women’s changing rooms in retail shops or public toilets.”

Some have secretly filmed their wives on cameras hidden in air fresheners and plugs inside their own homes.

Others prowl beaches in Brit holiday hotspots and capture bikini-clad women or topless bathers to post online.

Some paedophiles commission livestreams of child sexual abuse for as little as £20, according to the National Crime Agency (NCA).

The twisted video clips end up on user-generated sites like Motherless. One gallery of sexually explicit images was called “Candid teens beach”.



Investigators documented nearly 90,000 videos under the search term “young teen”.

Motherless became a “safe space” for rapists and paedophiles, according to Jon Taylor, an online safety expert and former Met police undercover investigator into child abuse.

Users from the site formed group chats on Telegram which acted as sick tutoring forums which investigators called “rape academies”.

Twisted messages show men asking how to drug their wives or boasting about raping women while they were unconscious.



Lyn explained that the forums “educate other men on how to drug, film and rape other women and circulate the content”.

Former investigator Jon said that it was almost inevitable that user-generated sites like Motherless would spiral into extreme pornography, adding that “child sex offenders are trying to go somewhere safe for them”.

Following a major investigation by German and Dutch authorities, multiple locations across Amsterdam, Rotterdam, and Steenbergen were raided and the servers seized. No arrests were made during the busts.

Europol investigators are now examining data on the seized servers to find evidence and arrest sex offenders, said Dutch authorities.

But the servers that hosted the content can deflect blame by pointing out that it was other users – not they themselves – who uploaded the criminal content.



One contributor ran what he sickeningly called a “porn mentorship programme” for teen girls, according to Lyn.

She said he stole photos from social media of children as young as 12 and stuck them into AI to generate them alongside an adult porn performer.

The disturbing images – verified by The Sun – created what Lyn called a “novel form of child exploitation”.

Experts have observed a sharp rise in AI child abuse images – with some sickening pics depicting toddlers as young as two years old.

More twisted AI abuse pictures were found in the first six months of 2026 than across the whole of 2025, according to an October report by the Internet Watch Foundation.



Sexual extortion for money has skyrocketed in recent years, according to the National Crime Agency.

And in 2024, Hungary was gripped by fear when it emerged that thousands of photos taken in the street had been uploaded onto Motherless.

Terrifying captions called on users to “hunt them down” alongside AI-generated videos of the women’s throats being slit.

One man, Peter C, posting under the username “Archie147, ” was charged with posting more than 3,900 photos to the site.



How to keep your child safe Online Safety expert Jon Taylor told The Sun how you can keep your child safe from child sex predators lurking online “As a parent what they’ve got to do really all the time is to be there and know what their child’s doing and what sites they’re on”, he said. The Internet Watch Foundation recommends the TALK method. Talk: Have open, calm, and non-judgmental conversations with your children about digital safety, online relationships, deepfakes, and consent.

Have open, calm, and non-judgmental conversations with your children about digital safety, online relationships, deepfakes, and consent. Agree: Set clear family ground rules regarding device usage, screen time, and where electronics can be used.

Set clear family ground rules regarding device usage, screen time, and where electronics can be used. Learn: Understand the apps, games, and platforms your children use, keeping up-to-date with emerging risks like AI tools and social networks.

Understand the apps, games, and platforms your children use, keeping up-to-date with emerging risks like AI tools and social networks. Know: Know how to use safety filters, parental controls, and privacy settings on all household devices and platforms. You can anonymously report suspected child abuse images and videos to the Internet Watch Foundation. Jon also recommended using apps like FaceCheck ID and Take It Down to sweep the web for any pornographic lookalikes and force sites to take them down. He said: “There’s far more that parents are able to do now than ever before. “Basically my advice to parents is get involved, have that corridor of communication. What is your child doing? “They need to understand what their child is doing and be there for them.”

With sites like Motherless, Jon Taylor believes the motive is financial, telling The Sun “it’s all about money”.

He added that trapping youngsters into a spiral of explicit sexual images is “very, very easy” and cops have a slim chance of catching the sick fiends.

Predators will adapt their tactics depending on the age of the child they are trying to entrap, according to Jon.

For children under the age of 12, the sex abuse videos will likely have been filmed by someone close to the child.

Jon said: “If they’re seven or eight, they probably won’t be online.



“So you’ve then got to go somewhere where somebody has access to a child that young, so you can share and have the images.”

He worked undercover on sites in which users could access mountains of child abuse material – but only if they too uploaded sick content.

The sick bond meant that both people were equally trapped inside the web of twisted abuse and could be relied on not to go to police.

For older children – in the young teens – the strategy changes.

For innocent children, being groomed is initially “enjoyable”, according to the former police investigator.



He said: “The grooming process is an enjoyable one.

“It’s not something that’s nasty to a child because they’re sitting there playing their games and somebody buying them treats.”

It turns dark when the abuser asks the child to turn his or her webcam on. Predators can then take a screenshot and use AI to do a face swap onto a pornographic image and threaten the child with the explicit photo.

Some children are then blackmailed into sending explicit photos – which can then be uploaded for thousands of strangers to view online.

Jon said the sextortion is so rampant that “if that child says no, the next one will say yes. There’s too many out there.”



While working at the Met Police he said his team conducted a sweep across London to see how many people were accessing child abuse material.

He said that in just a 30-minute window, investigators found more than 45,000 computers showing explicit pornographic material involving children.

Across a single eight-hour night in Hackney, East London, somewhere between 5,000-10,000 computers are showing child abuse material.

Jon confessed: “We don’t have enough police officers to do the work.”

Sickening websites can be easily found – but tracing where the videos have come from can take months of sleuthing. Users bounce the web IP address through the dark web dozens of times to scramble the code – making it almost impossible to track back to the original address.



Jon said: “It would take us many, many months to track just one person” adding that if they used the dark web it would be “impossible”.

To add to the difficulty, he said that in his 30 years in law enforcement, he “never had an informant” in this area because “you don’t come across this [child abuse material] by accident”.

Law enforcement can only focus on the top 10 offenders in any given region, according to ex-police officer Jon.

An average of 1,000 suspected paedophiles are arrested each month in the UK, according to a recent report from the NCA.

Online safety expert Jon Taylor’s advice to parents is to keep a careful eye over what sites your child is accessing – and to keep speaking to them over their online activity.



Sites like FaceCheckID and Take It Down can be used to remove harmful images off the internet.

If you ever come across child abuse material, report it to the police or, if you would like to remain anonymous, to the Internet Watch Foundation.

News.title: Shocking moment bus driver REVERSES on motorway before truck smashes into vehicle killing 11 & injuring 27
News.content:
Next

THIS is the shocking moment a bus driver reverses down a busy motorway – just moments before a deadly crash with a truck.

At least 11 people were killed and 27 more injured after the terrifying smash in western Turkey on Sunday morning.



Initially, investigators believed the horror unfolded after the packed coach slammed into the lorry.

But chilling footage from a camera on the Gebze-Orhangazi-Izmir highway has shone a light on how the devastating crash really played out.



The bus, reportedly taking tourists to hot springs in Denizli, can be seen travelling on the inside lane of the motorway when it suddenly comes to a stop feet before an entry slip road.

The vehicle then begins backing up towards a sharp right-hand bend, possibly in an attempt to come off the road via an exit it had just passed.



Several vehicles pass the stricken coach via the middle lane, but a large truck travelling around the corner appears to be unaware of the hazard ahead.

The two vehicles then violently collide and overturn, sending shards of debris flying across the tarmac.



Shocking images show the aftermath of the crash site, with both the coach and tow truck rolled onto their sides.

Ambulances, fire crew and police from Manisa province were immediately dispatched to the scene to assist the injured.

Of the 27 people hurt, 16 were rushed to hospital for further treatment.



That includes the driver of the bus, who was arrested by police after being discharged with minor injuries.

Authorities say the coach was carrying 34 passengers and three staff from the cities of Bursa and Izmir, while the truck was carrying one driver.

The nationalities of the victims currently remain unclear.

The governor of Manisa, Vahdettin Özkan, visited the scene to pay his respects to those who lost their lives.

“First of all, I offer my condolences to the families of our deceased citizens,” he said.



“Besides that, we have 34 passengers, three crew members, and the truck driver.

“In total, there are 11 fatalities and 27 injured. Of these injured, 16 were sent to hospitals with yellow code, nine with green code and one with red code.”

He added: “Currently, on-site investigations are continuing under the coordination of our Chief Public Prosecutor’s Office.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“We are experiencing in a painful way how vital it is to strictly adhere to traffic rules.”

Cops have launched a probe to investigate the full circumstances of the crash.

News.title: Hardest questions kids ask include ‘where do babies come from’ and why we die
News.content:
TRICKY ANSWERS Hardest questions kids ask include ‘where do babies come from’ and why we die







Next

A POLL of 1,000 mums and dads of children aged three to eight across the UK found they’ll have to answer an average of six tricky questions a day from their little one.

In fact, five-year-olds were found to be the most curious of all, with parents reporting their children asked more questions at this age than at any other point in their early childhood.



‘Why do we dream?’, ‘Why can’t animals talk?’ and ‘How does Santa get to every house in one night?’ are also among the other frequently posed abstract questions.

While 90 per cent enjoy their curiosity, the same percentage also admitted to secretly looking up the answer because they were unsure what to say.



And 24 per cent of the total questions asked will be too difficult for the average parent to answer.

The research was commissioned by the Mr Men Little Miss series to celebrate the 55th anniversary of Mr Tickle, which began when Roger Hargreaves turned his son’s question “What does a tickle look like?” into the iconic character.



His son, Adam Hargreaves, now the author of the iconic books and illustrator, said: “My father recognised children’s wonderful sense of curiosity and imagination and he explored these to create Mr Men Little Miss.

“While parents may not always have the answers to those impossible questions their children like to test them with, those everyday conversations play an important role in helping children to learn and stay curious.



“It’s lovely to see children embracing their personalities and finding fun in exploring life through asking questions as I did when I asked my dad what a tickle looked like.

“If you don’t ask, you won’t know!”

The study also found 48 per cent of parents believe their child asks more open-ended and imaginative questions as they get older.

For many, this shift became noticeable when their kid reached the age of six.

But 26 per cent ‘often’ give an answer to a question posed by their offspring which they’re not sure is correct.



For 39 per cent, their child asks a question which catches them off guard or makes them stop and think several times a week or more.

Almost four in 10 (43 per cent) usually stop what they’re doing to discuss the topic with them, while 37 per cent give them a brief answer and move on.

It also emerged 72 per cent are worried about their children losing their sense of wonder and curiosity as they grow older.

But almost all parents (95 per cent) think it’s important to encourage and nurture their children’s curious, imaginative way of thinking.

The study, carried out via OnePoll.com, found 57 per cent believe kids today are generally more curious than when they were a child.



And 34 per cent would be less confident in answering questions around life and death, while 24 per cent would struggle with questions around religion and beliefs.

The book series is hosting a gallery of children’s ‘big little questions’ for the anniversary, to remind families to take inspiration from the wonderful things children say before they’re forgotten.

A spokesperson for Sanrio, which owns the licensing rights for Mr Men and Little Miss, said: “Children today are full of big ideas and even bigger questions, and that natural curiosity is something worth celebrating.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“When they feel encouraged to ask questions, they’re not just learning facts, they’re developing confidence, creativity and a deeper understanding of the world around them.

“This is why we’re so excited to launch the Big Little Questions online gallery, to encourage mums and dads to treasure the imaginative things their kids say.”

"When they feel encouraged to ask questions, they're not just learning facts, they're developing confidence, creativity and a deeper understanding of the world around them.

"This is why we're so excited to launch the Big Little Questions online gallery, to encourage mums and dads to treasure the imaginative things their kids say."

TOP 20 QUESTIONS PARENTS FIND DIFFICULT TO ANSWER:

Where do babies come from? How does Santa get to every house in one night? What happens when we die? Why do we have to go to school? Why can't I stay up as late as you? Why do people get old? Why is the moon following us? Why do people have to go to work? Why do we dream? What happens to us before we're born? Why can't animals talk? Are there aliens in space? Why do grown-ups make the rules? Why is the sky blue? Can animals understand what we're saying? Where does the sun go at night? Why do some people look different from me? Why do bad things happen to good people? Do pets have feelings like humans do? How do birds know where to fly?

News.title: 'Tea tastes even better' with BBC Traitors star Hannah Fry's 'stirring' method
News.content:
'Tea tastes even better' with BBC Traitors star Hannah Fry's 'stirring' method

There is a scientific reason behind this why this 'erratic' way works

View 2 Images The professor recommends the 'erratic' stirring method for sugar to dissolve better (Image: Getty)

Hannah Fry has said that Brits may look "completely insane" when making their next cup of tea, as one 'erratic' method makes it taste better. The BBC Traitors star previously spoke about the exact method people should be following when mixing their brew.

‌



‌



A YouGov poll found that, on average, around a quarter of Brits (24%) take their usual cup of tea with added sugar. The findings indicate that of those who do put sugar in their tea, 14% use one teaspoon and 10% use two.

‌



Currently appearing in the latest series of the BBC's Celebrity Traitors, broadcaster and mathematician Professor Hannah Fry claims that those who make their tea this way could notice better taste from more dissolved sugar by following a simple scientific method.

‌



She claims that it is actually a "terrible idea" to stir your tea in a circle to get the added sugar to infuse quickly. Speaking on The Rest Is Science video podcast, which she hosts with American educator and Vsauce creator Michael Stevens, Hannah said: "The sugar will dissolve much better in a turbulent fluid.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

Hannah claims: "I stir tea like this. Just do an erratic shape with your teaspoon, you look completely insane." Stevens added: "This is what I do when I need to get salt to dissolve in pasta water."

‌



Generally speaking, tea will taste better if you follow Hannah's method. It prevents sugar from sinking and collecting at the bottom of your mug. This avoids the first few sips tasting more bitter than the very last, which will become a sickeningly sweet sludge.

When fully dissolved, the sucrose molecules in the sugar are evenly distributed throughout the entire mug. Every single sip will taste exactly how you intended it to from start to finish.

View 2 Images Doing this method makes you 'look completely insane' (Image: Getty)

Article continues below

What is the science behind this?

When you stir a teaspoon continuously in a smooth circle, you create a neat, predictable whirlpool. Instead of dissolving, the solid sugar crystals get swept up by the current and gather right in the middle at the bottom of the mug (similar to how tea leaves settle).

To dissolve sugar or mix milk efficiently, you want a turbulent flow. This almost chaotic movement is filled with tiny, unpredictable currents with greater force behind it than a gentle stir.

As the liquid collides with itself and with the solid sugar crystals from different angles. This tears the sugar crystals apart and mixes them into the hot water much quicker than a smooth whirlpool ever could.

News.title: Police launch Sutton Coldfield murder investigation after man stabbed to death outside pub
News.content:
Police launch Sutton Coldfield murder investigation after man stabbed to death outside pub

The incident took place at the Beggars Bush car park on Chester Road in Sutton Coldfield, with staff at the pub 'shaken' by the fatal stabbing

View 3 Images (Image: BPM MEDIA)

A man has been stabbed to death in the car park of a pub on the outskirts of Birmingham, with a murder investigation now underway.

‌



‌



The incident took place at the Beggars Bush car park on Chester Road in Sutton Coldfield just before 2am on Sunday. West Midlands Police said a man in his 20s was stabbed but, despite the best efforts of emergency services, he died at the scene.

‌



The force explained that a "large number of people" were at the pub, with Birmingham Live reporting tha there was a birthday party. A blue police tent was seen in place in the car park on Sunday as the car park remained cordoned off.

‌



View 3 Images A blue police tent was installed in the car park as forensic officers attended the scene (Image: BirminghamLive)

The perimeter of the cordon also included the nearby Sainsbury's Superstore, which was closed on Sunday morning. A statement from West Midlands Police reads: "We are reviewing CCTV and speaking to witnesses as we work to establish what happened.

‌



"It’s believed a large number of people had been at the venue for an event, and we’d appeal for anyone who was there or who has information about what had happened to come forward." Detective Chief Inspector Stacey Follows explained the investigation is at an early stage.

She said: "Our thoughts are with the man's family and friends today. We will continue to support them as our investigation progresses, and I'd urge anyone who saw what happened, or who has dashcam or CCTV to get in touch with us as soon as possible."

View 3 Images Officers at the scene on Sunday (Image: BirminghamLive)

Article continues below

A spokesperson for the pub, which is owned by Greene King, confirmed the pub remained closed yesterday and that the venue was "working closely" with the police. "We are supporting our franchisee and their team, who have been shaken by the incident, and our thoughts are with the family and friends of the victim," they said.

Anyone with information should call 101, quoting log 345.

News.title: State of Andrew and Sarah's relationship now - 'don't believe that poor Andy c***'
News.content:
State of Andrew and Sarah's relationship now - 'don't believe that poor Andy c***'

Few royal relationships have survived as much disgrace as Andrew Mountbatten Windsor and Sarah Ferguson. But now after years of unbreakable loyalty, the tide appears to have turned

View 4 Images Sarah and Andrew lived together long after their divorce (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Sarah Ferguson once bragged that she and Andrew Mountbatten Windsor were the 'happiest divorced couple in the world'.

‌



‌



But now their oddly close bond appears to be in tatters, with one source claiming that Sarah is not welcome at Andrew's new home on the King's Sandringham estate.

‌



It's a sharp turn of events to say the least. For 20 years, the former Duke and Duchess of York lived together at Royal Lodge - staying under the same roof long after their divorce.

‌



They seemed inseperable, often turning up to public events as a duo and supporting each other on the sidelines. "We have a great love, a great respect, a great understanding," Sarah said in a 2011 interview. "He's an extraordinary human being."

To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

View 4 Images The former couple are parents to Princesses Beatrice and Eugenie (Image: Daily Mirror)

‌



Fergie, 66, even hinted at the idea of remarriage. "He's still my handsome prince," she told a literature festival crowd in 2013. "He'll always be my handsome prince".

But the years since have been marred with scandal after scandal. And revelations from their years-long friendship with the late paedophile financer Jeffrey Epstein proved to be the final straw.

Andrew now lives at Marsh Farm, a five-bed farmhouse world's away from the sweeping estate of Royal Lodge. Sarah, meanwhile, is thought to be renting a six-bed gated property out in the Home Counties.

‌



But it seems unlikely they'll be paying each other visits, with a source telling The Times that Andrew has distanced himself from Sarah. "The red setter, as she's known, is not welcome at Marsh Farm," they said. "She's persona non grata as far as Andrew is concerned."

View 4 Images Sarah married her 'handsome prince' in 1986 (Image: Mirrorpix)

But Andrew is far from wallowing in his own company. The same source shared: "Don't believe all that poor Andy crap. He's having a very nice time, thank you very much. He goes out, he goes off shooting with friends, he sees his old chums who are very loyal to him. He's not sitting around feeling sorry for himself any more."

‌



That it was Andrew who chose to freeze Sarah out may come as a surprise to some. Earlier this year, ahead of her return to the UK following several months overseas, a source told the Daily Mail that it was Sarah who keen to carve out her own path away from her disgraced ex. She reportedly told friends: "When I come back, I am going to have to put some distance between myself and Andrew."

The former couple's old home has now come back under scrutiny after it was revealed that King Charles has been forced to settle an eyewatering £1.8million bill for renovations to Royal Lodge after Andrew was unable to pay.

View 4 Images Sarah is not welcome at Marsh Farm, according to a source (Image: UK Press via Getty Images)

‌



While the former prince had been eligible for £302,000 worth of compensation after his elder brother kicked him out prior to the expiration of the lease, he won't pocket a penny, following an independent assessment of damage and vital repairs to the historic estate, for which he'd been liable.

Andrew also recently won a High Court battle over police raids earlier this year at his homes on the Sandringham Estate and Royal Lodge. The late Queen Elizabeth II's middle son was arrested on February 19, his 66th birthday, by Thames Valley Police on suspicion of misconduct in public office and questioned for 12 hours. He has denied any wrongdoing and has not been charged with any offences.

Thames Valley Police has accepted that the search warrants it used were unlawful and have been quashed, the High Court heard at a hearing which Andrew did not attend. Mr Justice Hilliard stated that a "significant error was made" by police as well as an unnamed Old Bailey judge. The criminal investigation remains ongoing, and items seized by officers during the raids will remain with police as the legal challenge continues.

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

As for Fergie, she's kept a relatively low profile following her royal exile, although her spokesperson has recently poured cold water over reports that she is mere "days away" from a seven-figure book deal to "rescue her reputation".

Last month, a source told The Sun: "Sarah wants to set the record straight about everything and earn some money to resolve her financial issues. There has been a secret bidding war, and a deal is close to being secured. The notes are compelling, and the bidders are excited. Fergie is ever the optimist and believes she can be forgiven and welcomed back."

Article continues below

But Sarah's spokesperson said: "There have been no discussions, and she is not writing a personal memoir; it's not what she's going to do."

News.title: 'Zelensky's near-impossible dilemma as he fights war on two fronts against Kremlin and Trump treachery'
News.content:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky is being forced to fight a war on two fronts - against Kremlin attacks on his civilians and Donald Trump ’s depraved and inexplicable respect for Putin.

Trump’s baffling approach to Ukraine has broken out yet again into treachery, with a diesel deal with Putin, calling for Zelensky’s replacement and demanding Kyiv stop hitting Russia ’s oil refineries.

Washington is even threatening to stop the procurement system that provides Ukraine with weapons to press Kyiv to halt its deep strikes on Russian energy infrastructure.

And it is even, reportedly, threatening to withdraw intelligence sharing with Ukraine.

‌



To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

View 4 Images Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky faces a near-impossible dilemma (Image: PRESIDENT OF UKRAINE/APAImages/Shutterstock)

Kyiv defies Trump with massive drone barrage against Russian oil READ MORE :

It is creating a near-impossible dilemma for Zelensky- how to respond to Trump’s attempt to neuter his troops in defending against Putin’s war on Ukraine, whilst maintaining diplomacy.

Trump is basically ordering Ukraine to stop defending itself even as its civilians die daily from ballistic weapons strikes and drone attacks on homes throughout the country.

‌



This at a time when Ukraine, after months of steadily dismantling Russia’s ability to pay for its vile war on Ukraine, was gaining leverage, whittling down Moscow’s war machine.

It is difficult to imagine how Zelensky just about keeps his cool, merely calling the diesel deal a “gift” to the Russian President instead of saying it as it is - bloody and bullying cowardice.

The almost hidden hand of Putin keeps hovering over the chess board and making deadly moves against Kyiv, exerting deadly influence over Trump and undermining Ukraine.

It has edged precarious diplomatic tensions inside NATO towards a tipping point.

‌



View 4 Images US President Donald Trump's claim of an energy ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine lasted hours (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

There is no equivalence here - Putin is killing Zelensky’s civilians as Kyiv dismantles Moscow’s ability to fund its war on Ukraine for a year, steadfastly trying to avoid harming civilians.

Zelensky was forced to vaguely accept Trump’s crazy announcement of a fuel accord between Ukraine and Russia - but Putin ordered attacks on Ukraine within hours, hitting power plants and more civilian targets.

Trump’s approach is impossibly cruel, trying to force Ukraine to stop doing the one thing that was giving it leverage against Moscow’s war on it, hitting its energy infrastructure and taking the war to Russia.

‌



View 4 Images Firefighters battle blaze in Kharkiv after Russian attack (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

And he is forcing Zelensky to speak out against the American President - almost certainly leading to a weakening of his own country’s position and creating major challenges for the UK and the rest of the coalition against Russian aggression.

The US President, mired in a worsening Middle East crisis with his popularity waning daily and facing midterm demolition, is in trouble and he knows it.

And when cornered, bullies always lash out at what they perceive to be the weakest around them, in this case Ukraine, which is defending against the threat of oblivion.

‌



His ridiculous claim of an energy ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine lasted hours before Putin broke it, making Trump’s assertion look even more ludicrous than before.

But Trump has set the scene for continued attacks on Zelensky, continuing to dress up Ukraine’s defence against Russia as somehow being disobedient.

Zelensky has even offered to hold elections if Putin agrees to peace, perhaps knowing what the rest of the world apart from Trump knows - that the Russian leader will never stop the war. Unless he is toppled or forced to do so.

News.title: Yorkshire tiger attack - latest: Wildlife park to stay closed after man 'bowed' before fatal mauling
News.content:
Witnesses to the horror incident at Yorkshire Wildlife Park said the man who was mauled to death at the attraction's tiger enclosure appeared to 'bow down' to the animal

Yorkshire Wildlife Park has confirmed it will remain closed today while investigations continue after a man was mauled to death by a tiger over the weekend.

The park confirmed in a message to ticketholders this morning that "the park remains closed for the whole of Monday, the 12th October." They added that people who have bookings will be contacted in the coming days regarding them and apologised "for the late notice" and "any inconvenience caused."

Horrified witnesses to the fatal mauling of a man by a tiger at Yorkshire Wildlife Park say he appeared to "bow down" to the animal before he was attacked. Police and paramedics raced to the site, near Doncaster, at about 1.35pm on Saturday following reports that the man had jumped into the tiger enclosure.

A video circulating on Facebook shows the victim sat next to the tiger before being bitten and clawed at as he appeared to try and communicate with the animal. He was heard shouting: "Stop, stop, stop, stop, stop!"

Anthony Hunt, 22, was visiting the park and said: "It looked like a performance. He got down where everyone could see him in the main viewing area. He was on all fours, praying and bowing down to the tiger. It was like he was waiting for the tiger."

Park bosses said Altai, the tiger, is "safe and well" and will not be euthanised.

News.title: £30,000 tax-free allowance 'not risen since 1988' and 'should be £85,000' as 51,000 in UK affected in one month
News.content:
£30,000 tax-free allowance 'not risen since 1988' and 'should be £85,000' as 51,000 in UK affected in one month

It has remained unchanged for 38 years and one expert said it should now be £85,000

View 4 Images The limit hasn't changed for nearly four decades (Image: imageBROKER/Audtakorn Sutarmjam via Getty Images)

Employers in Great Britain notified 50,904 proposed redundancies in September 2026, the most in a month since October 2020, while the tax-free limit on redundancy pay has not changed since April 1988. September's total is up from 19,557 in August, Insolvency Service management information published on October 5 showed.

‌



‌



HR1 forms - the statutory advance notification document that UK employers must submit to the government via the Redundancy Payments Service on GOV.UK whenever they propose collective redundancies - rose only from 282 to 353, although the figures may be revised and not every proposal ends in dismissal. For those let go, only the first £30,000 of statutory and enhanced redundancy pay combined is usually tax-free. Pay in lieu of notice and holiday pay are taxed as pay.

‌



While Chancellor John Healey is set to deliver his first on October 28, experts said there was no suggestion the allowance would change.

‌



Redundancy tax-free limit hasn't changed since 1988

Kate Underwood, founder and chief people strategist at Southampton-based Kate Underwood HR & Training, said: "Is £30,000 still the right line? Only if your rent is still at 1988 prices. It hasn't moved in 38 years.

View 4 Images Kate Underwood (Image: Newspage)

"The limit is old enough to have been made redundant itself. Is it fair? Give a firm 25 years and you get a tax bill as a thank you. Join last year and you walk away clean.

‌



"Link it to salary and the fat cats get the biggest break. Link it to years served, then index it so nobody forgets it for another four decades.

"Now the numbers. Proposed redundancies leapt from 19,557 to 50,904, but HR1 forms only crept from 282 to 353. That's a few big players swinging the axe.

"Small firms cutting under 20 jobs don't file an HR1, so they don't even make the count. Meanwhile tribunal claims passed 50,000 last year, up 39%. For a small firm, defending one can cost more than the redundancy. So employers pay up and move on. A settlement agreement is quicker, cheaper, and nobody wastes a week in a tribunal waiting room. It's cheaper to pay than to prove you were right."

‌



'Should be £85,000'

Tony Redondo, founder of Newquay-based Cosmos Currency Exchange, said: "As Clarkson asked (last week): 'Why would you start a business in the UK today?' The £30,000 tax-free redundancy limit was set 38 years ago. Adjusted for inflation, it would top £85,000 now.

"Enhanced packages routinely breach £30,000, turning relief into a tax bill. A frozen cap amid rising job losses is fiscal drag by stealth. The Treasury gains, redundant workers’ pay. It's manifestly unfair.

"A long-serving employee is taxed on everything above £30,000, often pushed into higher bands, while a shorter-tenured colleague pays nothing. Penalising long service erodes vital transitional capital. Employers in collective consultation can soften the blow with pension sacrifice on the excess, shielding it from income tax and employer NICs; employees should consider it, provided liquidity needs are met."

‌



View 4 Images Nouran Moustafa (Image: Nouran Moustafa/Newspage)

Nouran Moustafa, practice principal and Independent Financial Adviser at Roxton Wealth, said: "A redundancy payment is not a windfall. It is financial runway while somebody rebuilds their income.

"That is why a £30,000 tax-free limit unchanged since 1988 deserves serious scrutiny. A long-serving employee receiving a larger package can exceed it relatively easily, even though the money may need to replace months of salary. I would not frame that as newer workers being treated 'better'.

‌



"The real problem is that the threshold has stood still while wages and living costs have moved enormously. For anyone receiving a sizeable package, the first instinct should not be to spend it.

"Work out how long it needs to support you, what is taxable and whether pension planning is appropriate. And if redundancy risk appears during a mortgage application, tell the adviser immediately. Losing a job is difficult enough. The tax system should not make the safety net feel 38 years out of date."

Eroded by inflation

Ross Lacey, director of Rayleigh-based Fairview Financial Management, said: "The limit set in 1988 has been eroded by inflation, and it creates a cliff-edge for long-serving employees whose packages go over £30,000. We specialise in working with people going through redundancy and there are often merits in having some or all of the excess paid into a pension rather than taken as cash.

‌



"This can help manage the immediate tax bill and improve retirement provision. As ever, a well-thought-out plan for what happens next is essential, so take advice before you sign a settlement agreement."

View 4 Images Stephen Perkins (Image: Newspage)

Stephen Perkins, Norwich mortgage broker and managing director of Norwich-based Yellow Brick Mortgages, said: "An at-risk redundancy letter can create a real problem during a mortgage application because lenders are assessing whether the income used to support the loan is likely to continue. The worst thing a borrower can do is stay silent and hope to complete before anything changes.

Article continues below

"Tell your broker and lender as soon as circumstances change so the case can be reassessed properly. That may mean a lower loan, a different lender or waiting until employment is clearer, but discovering the issue at the last minute risks a collapsed purchase and much bigger costs."

Shoppers who like the look of the pattern on John Lewis' jumper, but would prefer spending less, may be interested in Lidl's option
