News.title: Max Verstappen is back and Mercedes are already worried
News.content:
Kimi Antonelli, third: “It was a very tough race out there but really happy with a podium at the end, I managed to take advantage of the fight between Lewis and Lando. To take P3 is a great result from the team, very happy with that.”

He is told that he can clinch the title at the next race:

“Can I, really? Let’s not worry about that. Let’s try to do the best weekend possible and finish the job.”

Charles Leclerc, second: “We were quite strong at the beginning of the race and then we started degrading at the end of the first stint. I pushed a lot at the beginning of the last stint and then degraded a bit more than the others. I gave it all and I don’t regret anything.

“I don’t think there’s anything more we could do but be a bit more aggressive at the start. It’s true that we brought some small new parts to the car which maybe helped us to do a little step forward but it’s enough. Today I think we had a good pace overall.”

Max Verstappen, winner: “It’s taken a while but I think this race was very good. We had pace when we needed to have it on the soft tyre and the medium. Very happy to win here. You always try to do your best and luckily [the start] it was just good enough.

“I think the last few races have been really positive for us. It’s great to see and we have a lot of motivation in the team to try to deliver even more results... hopefully we can have a bit more fun until the end of the year.”

News.title: The cheats prosper: Man City thrash 10-man Liverpool
News.content:
Just when the Premier League and the world outside of east Manchester and Abu Dhabi needed Liverpool to step up, to strike back, to make a point, they faltered. Maybe it was unfair to expect them to do so, given the circumstances. But unfairness, lack of clarity and uncertainty are all prevailing moods in English football at present.

How we had rubbed our hands in anticipation of Manchester City having to play their first league fixture here at Anfield after being found guilty of industrial-scale fraud with 114 of the 115 financial charges being proven against them.

It felt apt that it was at the home of Liverpool, who, along with Arsenal, possess the strongest sense of grievance at having been denied trophies and glory by City’s cheating. As expected, there were banners everywhere at Anfield. “A generation of supporters cheated,” one read and it summed up the depth of the anger.

News.title: Three tasks to get your home ready for autumn, according to a professional cleaner
News.content:
When I was sweating away this summer, I never thought the weather would turn, but it’s almost time to crank up our radiators and crack out the big duvet.

They’re the tasks no one likes doing, but luckily for you, I’ve worked as a cleaner for more than a decade. I’ve discovered some shortcuts to make the hated jobs that bit easier.

Tip one: Keep your summer duvet fresh in storage

If, like me, you want to get your winter duvet out, your summer one needs to be cleaned and packed away to keep it fresh come spring.

Start by spot cleaning any stains. You can just use a standard household fabric stain remover for this. If you want to wash your duvet, most domestic washing machines aren’t big enough to fit a double, let alone a king or a super king. Your best bet is to take them down to the laundrette and follow the care instructions on the label.

News.title: Man Utd make worst start in 40 years after being hauled back by 10-man Spurs
News.content:
The Tottenham boss told Sky Sports: “I think we played very well against a great team. We had many chances to score in the first half. Three or four. The second half is normal to suffer against this quality. I am very happy because I have seen the right spirit and character.

“We suffered in the game but every situation of the game. I like the situation we were in with the red card. We need this situation. We have not accepted the defeat. We have to react in all ways we can. It is a bad way, it is not the right way. I kiss Bentancur in the dressing room. Football is character.

“We win the game if we play as a team. We didn’t win this game playing as a team. Every game like today, we will win many games.”

When asked about Solanke, he replied: “He is a good player for Tottenham. There for not too many strikers better than Solanke. Today he was captain because he deserved it, especially in this moment because he suffer because Tottenham didn’t score or win any games. He is a great guy, great player and we are behind him.

“We have to believe in ourselves and this football way. If we believe, improve and play as a team, we will score many goals and win many games. If we don’t play as a team, it is impossible.”

News.title: Guimaraes looks a £75m bargain as ‘super sub’ makes difference
News.content:
Before the game we talked about two things, the challenge ahead against a team that had not lost in the Premier League. They full deserved to be where they are and it was going to be really tough. The second was to restore our identity and be ourselves again.

We weren’t pleased with our performance against Brighton and we wanted to put it right. But the context is that this was a difficult one [opponent]. But we reacted in a way that was unique and made it so special.

[Leeds] are very well organised, very physical and very committed in everything that they do. They are a threat. They are incredible the way they attack the ball and set-pieces, with belief. They came close to punishing us. They have individual quality and they are in a good moment.

When you play at 12.30 at home and you go one-nil down there’s a lot to do. You have to restore a lot of things. Energy is one of them. We had an incredible response. The crowd changed. You could see it.

We brought a lot of leadership on [with his three subs]. We brought goal threat, to win duels, people who can play forward and penetrate against their high press.

The timing, movement and execution of it [the winning goal], yes, it was a beauty.

News.title: Resurgent Verstappen on fire in the Singapore smog
News.content:
Welcome to our live coverage for the sprint race for the 2026 Singapore Grand Prix from the Marina Bay Circuit. Given the way the championship standings are, it looks like Kimi Antonelli has one hand on the drivers’ title. That means that the most significant thing is the battle for individual race victories. That includes grands prix, but also sprint races, like we have today.

Formula One is very keen on sprint races, increasing their number significantly next year, but we have never had one in Singapore before. We will find out today whether there was good reason for it. I suppose the logic is that even a processional sprint race is better than a free practice session and that having two qualifying sessions on a street circuit such as this is exciting, too.

Still, although he might be strolling towards the championship, he and Mercedes are not the dominant force they were at the start of the season when he won five in a row having finished second in the opening race. In fact, in the last 10 grands prix, Antonelli has won three and Russell two. With Max Verstappen’s win in Malaysia last weekend it meant each of Red Bull, McLaren, Ferrari and Mercedes have won races this season.

It is Verstappen who is in strong form in an upgraded Red Bull, as he snuck pole position from George Russell by just over a tenth of a second. He was followed by Charles Leclerc in the Ferrari and then Oscar Piastri in the McLaren. Antonelli, in the upgraded Mercedes, found things more difficult, finishing down in seventh nearly 0.7sec off the pace.

Anyway, the sprint gets under way in about 30 minutes and we will be here for all the updates from that, as well as qualifying later today.

News.title: Majestic All Blacks copy Springbok playbook to dismantle Australia
News.content:
Good morning and welcome to our live coverage of this Bledisloe Cup Test as New Zealand host Australia at Eden Park in Auckland.

The All Blacks are enduring one of the toughest periods in their history, having suffered three successive Test defeats against South Africa in August and September, which saw the Springboks claim the inaugural Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry series tour. Dave Rennie’s men are under immense pressure to avoid a fourth consecutive Test defeat for the first time since 1998.

You could argue there’s never been a better opportunity for Australia to beat New Zealand at Eden Park. The Wallabies are enjoying a six-Test unbeaten run – their longest such streak since 2017, with five games in this rejuvenated period coming under new head coach Les Kiss. In their most recent outing, Australia secured an extraordinary 42-38 victory over a much-changed South Africa side in Perth, despite being reduced to 11 players at one point.

Australia will feel further encouraged due to several key absences for New Zealand, as Ardie Savea, Ruben Love, Richie Mo’unga, Caleb Clarke, Fehi Fineanganofo, Billy Proctor and Anton Lienert-Brown are all out injured. In a reshuffle for the All Blacks, Damian McKenzie will begin at fly-half for the first time in 2026. Other notable inclusions for the home side see all three Barrett brothers, Codie Taylor, Tupou Vaa’i, Cam Roigard and Will Jordan starting.

Meanwhile, the visitors are without the suspended Hunter Paisami, with Isaac Henry taking his place at centre. The likes of Ryan Lonergan, Len Ikitau, Harry Wilson, Ben Donaldson and Max Jorgensen, who were all key to the triumph against the Springboks, retain their starting spots.

All the statistics overwhelmingly favour New Zealand. The All Blacks have not lost any edition of the Bledisloe Cup since 2002, winning 51 series to Australia’s 12, and are unbeaten at Eden Park since 1994, when they lost to France. Australia are winless at Eden Park since 1986, tasting defeat there 30 times in 34 games, and have lost their last 11 Tests against New Zealand.

However, given the landscape heading into this historic rivalry between these two heavyweights, it genuinely feels like anything could happen.

Kick-off is at 7:10am.

Sports.title: When will Man City be punished? The timeline for sanctions – and what the Premier League could do
Sports.content:
Next

MANCHESTER CITY could face one of the largest disciplinary fallouts in English football history after being found guilty of breaking Premier League financial rules.

Following an independent commission’s verdict finding City guilty of over 100 breaches spanning nine seasons between 2009 and 2018, the eight-time Premier League champions have launched an appeal.



The club maintains its innocence, but when could any sanctions kick in, and what could they look like?

Here’s a full breakdown of the timeline, the rules, and the potential punishments facing Etihad bosses.



What sanctions could Man City face?

The Premier League rulebook gives the independent commission virtually unlimited scope when penalising member clubs.

Because Man City’s charges represent the largest financial breach case in top-flight history, the potential punishments range from heavy fines to banishment from the league itself.

But perhaps the biggest threat comes in the form of massive points deductions.

Unlike standard Profitability and Sustainability Rules (PSR) cases that previously resulted in single-digit penalties for Everton and Nottingham Forest, City’s breaches span nearly a decade.

Legal experts suggest any points punishment could be much harsher, potentially starting at 30 points, or being applied across consecutive seasons.

Then there is the option of complete expulsion from the Premier League.



The commission has the authority to recommend kicking City out of the top flight altogether, though full expulsion requires a 75% majority (15 of the 20 clubs) vote in favour.

Alongside sporting penalties, the panel can hand down unlimited financial fines and impose strict transfer embargoes, preventing City from registering any new players over multiple transfer windows.

While stripping past Premier League titles is theoretically possible under league governance rules, experts say this is far less likely due to logistical and historical complications.

What is the timeline for sanctions?

City officially lodged their appeal against the commission’s guilty verdict on October 1, 2026.

That triggered a formal appeal process, though exact dates remain subject to legal debate.



The appeal will be heard privately by a three-member, independent board.

Under Premier League regulations, the timeframe for the hearing process is set at roughly 12 weeks from the initial filing, followed by a maximum 30-day window for the board to deliver its final verdict.

Following that time-table would mean the hearing concluding, at the latest, on Christmas Day, and beginning on December 21.

As that would not happen for obvious reasons, the implication is the appeal being heard from December 14.

The commission would then have 30 days to produce its final verdict.



If proceedings stick to league guidelines, a judgement could arrive between January and March 2027.

But given the volume of legal documentation and City’s desire to challenge every detail, the case could easily stretch into late 2027 and beyond.

What happens next?

City’s legal team is preparing to present what CEO Ferran Soriano has described as “irrefutable evidence” to overturn the initial verdict.

But the appeal board primarily reviews whether the initial commission made clear errors of law or procedure.

That means City cannot simply re-try the case from the start, making a full overturn a much larger legal hurdle.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

For now, Manchester City remain fully active in domestic and European competition.

But with processes in motion, English football could be heading toward a judgement that could reshape the Premier League landscape.

It capped off a difficult few weeks for City after an independent commission found they had hid £900million in “sham” commercial deals.

Etihad chiefs have always denied any wrongdoing and vowed to prove their innocence after launching an appeal.

Sports.title: Tottenham touch down in Marbella after snatching Man Utd draw as De Zerbi reveals why he ‘kissed’ red-carded Bentancur
Sports.content:
Next

TOTTENHAM head to sun-soaked Marbella with their rebuild finally heating up.

Roberto De Zerbi‘s side may still have clouds to clear, but the temperature is rising after a fiery draw at Old Trafford.



It might have been difficult to lift the squad’s spirits had they lost in Manchester after dominating for long spells and spurning chance after chance.

But Dominic Solanke‘s stoppage-time equaliser perhaps sparked a turning point after 18 months of hell.



Reduced to ten-men and trailing, Spurs for the first time showed character and evidence that they might finally be developing a backbone after spending more than £300m on new signings.

Both managers were tasked with a ‘reset’ after the three-week international break, but only De Zerbi walked away with any trace of change.

On their trip to Marbs, the Italian said: “We are going because we have to build the team. We are a great group of players, but we are not a team yet.

“This weekend we showed more of what a team looks like. To be a team is to play for others, suffer together, attack together and defend together.”

Spurs, so often prone to crumbling after adversity, showed rare fight after Rodrigo Bentancur was sent off for headbutting Luke Shaw with 12 minutes remaining.

Having sunk his teeth into a ball and booted it along the touchline when Solanke’s touch flew past Senne Lammens, De Zerbi was so pleased with his side’s grit that he “kissed” Bentancur in the dressing room for bringing the passion.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

It wasn’t all good for Tottenham, of course. And the slate will not be wiped clean.

Without the late uplift of Solanke’s equaliser, it might have felt like a nightmare on repeat: another blistering start, floods of good chances thrown away, another slow fade of energy, another goal conceded.

Solanke, who missed several clear openings, said: “The mentality is something to build on. The character we showed after going a goal down and a man down was magnificent.

“There’s been times we go a goal down and do not react in the right way. It was great to get something from the game.”

With Micky van De Ven only fit for the bench, De Zerbi gave Solanke the armband in a show of faith after recent fan backlash.



Indeed Spurs often smell blood against United and remain without a Prem win this season, with three points from their opening six games, climbing to 18th in the table.

After splashing a quarter of a million on new players, that is nowhere near good enough.

But it is not far off to believe Spurs will finish above United this season, with Michael Carrick‘s side facing a near impossible task of a top-four finish.

The North Londoners, without European distractions that will surely plague United, showed a pattern of play and a system to build on in Spain this week.

De Zerbi added: “We will work together, stay together, to go for dinner together, to know each other better, because to be a team you have to know the teammates.



“We are still in a bad situation, we can’t accept staying in that situation. It’s not important the environment, the past, the last season.

“We can’t accept it, we can’t stay sad for the result. We have to react. We have to find ways to improve the result, to improve the table, to improve this club.”

The injured Pedro Porro and Xavi Simons were among the travelling party at Old Trafford ready to jet out for their warm weather break.

Spurs have eight days to recharge before hosting Prem newsboys Coventry City on Monday week.

De Zerbi has a number of new faces who are still adapting to their surroundings. That includes new signings Jan-Paul van Hecke, Andy Robertson, Sandro Tonali, Mateus Fernandes, Savio and Omar Marmoush.



On paper, the following home clashes against Crystal Palace and newsboys Ipswich Town offer a chance to turn up the heat.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

But Spurs have won just TWO games at the cursed Tottenham Hotspur Stadium since October 2025, with their last victory coming in the 1-0 defeat of Everton on the final day of last season.

And with tricky away days at Chelsea, Leeds and Sunderland thrown into the mix, the rebuild faces some serious tests once they return to late autumn weather in London.

Sports.title: Man Utd chiefs accept they fell short in transfer window with two new signings ‘a long way down the list’
Sports.content:
Next

MANCHESTER UNITED power brokers privately accept that they fell short in the transfer window.

United have won one of their first six Premier League games in what has been their worst start to a season in 40 years.



They were also ejected from the League Cup by Brighton in what was United’s first defeat at Old Trafford after leading by two goals since September 1976.

Supporters booed at three separate stages during Saturday’s 1-1 draw with Tottenham, who were bottom at kick-off.



Although pressure is mounting on head coach Michael Carrick, the hierarchy was not satisfied with the second phase of their squad rebuild.

United invested £225.2million to bring in Matheus Cunha, Bryan Mbeumo, Benjamin Sesko and Senne Lammens last year but this summer‘s spending dropped to £155m.

The £70m Carlos Baleba, who made his debut in the 1-1 draw with Tottenham on Saturday, was a long-term target but United insiders have admitted Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos were “a long way down the list”.

Elliot Anderson, Mateus Fernandes, Aurelien Tchouameni and Ederson were United’s preferred picks.

Tottenham blew United out of the water to buy Fernandes before adding the £100m Sandro Tonali to their midfield.

Anderson had settled on moving to City months before the move was completed in July.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Both Anderson and Tonali had key roles as ten-men City and Spurs secured positive results at Old Trafford.

United opted to bring in Tielemans after a £35m deal for Atalanta defensive midfielder Ederson collapsed.

Tielemans, 29, had a release clause for £35m and United proceeded with the transfer even though he is an attacking midfielder and was outside their preferred age bracket of 22-26 for targets.

Surprisingly, Tielemans is the only United player who has started in all eight of their games but that run seems certain to end this week, with United away at Atletico Madrid in the Champions League and Leeds United on Sunday.

Andrey Santos joined in a £50m deal from Chelsea but has played only 16 minutes in the Premier League since he started in the opening weekend defeat at Hull City.



Santos, 22, was considered an affordable target after United baulked at the hiked valuations of other Premier League midfielders.

There is particular regret at United that they had to withdraw from the Ederson move after a medical flagged a major issue with his knee.

Senior figures at United are also rueing the failure to add a left-back, having held exploratory talks with Newcastle defender Lewis Hall.



Hall, 22, was keen to sign for United but Newcastle took measures to prevent discussions from progressing and the England international signed a new contract last month.

Long-time United left-back Luke Shaw missed three games last month and Patrick Dorgu is out for a number of weeks after sustaining an injury on international duty.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Carrick played Dorgu as a winger before the window closed and he has since started at left-back.

Shaw, 31, has entered the final year of his contract and could be released after his 13th season at Old Trafford.

Sports.title: ‘Total FARCE’ – Piers Morgan slates celebrating Man City stars following win over Liverpool after ‘staggering cheating’
Sports.content:
Next

ARSENAL fan Piers Morgan has launched an online tirade against Manchester City after their thumping win over Liverpool.

City battered the 10-man Reds 3-0 in their first game since being found guilty of breaching more than 100 of the Premier League’s financial rules.



The inflatable bananas were out in force as a defiant City mob created a raucous atmosphere in the Anfield away end.

But Morgan, who has watched City pip Arsenal to major honours numerous times in recent years, was outraged.



He wrote on X: “Sorry, but this is a total farce.

“Manchester City players, and fans, celebrating wildly like nothing has happened – despite the club being exposed as the worst cheats in football history.



“What happens if they win the title again this season? That could ruin the Premier League.”

City, who have appealed their guilty verdict, face a range of punishments including points deductions, transfer bans, being stripped of trophies and even expulsion from the Prem.

Less than half an hour after his ‘farce’ message, Morgan’s rant continued.

He posted: “The Premier League has to act asap and announce City’s punishment. This cannot go on.”



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Eight minutes later, Morgan responded to a clip of Erling Haaland celebrating in front of the City supporters, writing: “Let’s see how smug he looks when City get relegated. As they should already have been.”

Oasis frontman and die-hard City fan Liam Gallagher was the next to get it after signing off an X-rated post with: “MCFC own football.”

Morgan responded: “No, MCFC bought football. Illegally.”

Later on Sunday, Morgan was back online.

He wrote: “Staggering sums, staggering cheating… yet today, we saw City’s players and fans celebrate like they’d been cleared, not guilty as charged.”



City and Arsenal are the pace-setters again this season, with the Blues leading by three points after six games.

But the title landscape could change dramatically if City are punished before the end of the campaign.

Under Prem rules, a hearing should be held within 12 weeks of City’s appeal, with a verdict handed down in the proceeding 30 days.

Liverpool round-up as Steven Gerrard hails a Reds star and Mohamed Salah continues his blistering start to life in Turkey

View 3 Images Steven Gerrard is delighted with one summer arrival in particular (Image: Getty Images)

Following the showdown with Manchester City, Liverpool's attention has shifted to the Champions League and Wednesday's trip to Austrian side LASK. The Reds got up and running in Europe with a comeback victory over Atletico Madrid thanks to goals from Dominik Szoboszlai and Alexis Mac Allister.

‌



‌



The match continues an important spell for Andoni Iraola's side, who face a tough trip to Brentford on Saturday. Iraola will be hoping to have Alexander Isak and Cody Gakpo back soon, after both missed the City game with injuries sustained on international duty.

‌



Looking further ahead, planning for the next couple of transfer windows will be well underway. They could be busy ones for the Reds, given the current imbalance within the squad and problems at left-back. Away from the City game, here's a round-up of the latest Liverpool news…

‌



FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Gerrard names Van Dijk successor

Steven Gerrard believes Liverpool have found a long-term replacement for Virgil van Dijk. With the Dutchman now in the latter stages of his career, the Reds will soon need to look to the future, possibly at the end of this season when the 35-year-old's contract expires.

Five Liverpool players facing tough chats as Andoni Iraola reveals his golden rule READ MORE :

But Gerrard believes they already have a defensive rock in their ranks in the shape of Jeremy Jacquet, who has impressed since arriving from Rennes. Gerrard told SPORTbible: "I love him, I've been very impressed with him from the opening pre-season friendlies.

‌



"I think he's got a composure and a fantastic profile and he can move. I think there's still a bit of rawness about him. But I think there’s another level which he can get to and I think he's going to be the perfect replacement for Virg in a year or two because he's really helped solidify that back four."

View 3 Images Jeremy Jacquet and Virgil van Dijk have struck up a promising partnership (Image: Getty Images)

Salah settles in

Mohamed Salah is rolling back the years at Trabzonspor, powering his new club to a flying start in Turkey. Nine years after joining Liverpool, the Egyptian icon mutually terminated his Anfield contract this summer.

‌



His fresh chapter started in chaos with an early Europa League exit and the resignation of manager Fatih Tekke. But that turbulence has quickly vanished.

View 3 Images Mohamed Salah has wasted little time in becoming Trabzonspor's talisman (Image: Anadolu via Getty Images)

Before the international break, Trabzonspor laid down a marker with a 4-0 thrashing of Galatasaray, which featured a Salah hat-trick, following it up with a slick 3-0 win over Samsunspor on Saturday.

Article continues below

Salah turned provider with an assist in the latest victory, bringing his blistering league tally to seven goals and three assists in just seven matches. According to Opta, the 34-year-old is the first player to reach 10 goal contributions in his first seven matches of a Turkish Super Lig season since 2014/15, when such records began.

Trabzonspor visit KPS Kuopio in the Conference League on Thursday before a home clash with Besiktas on October 19.

Sports.title: Man Utd news: JJ Gabriel left in transfer lurch as Michael Carrick told to change plans
Sports.content:
Man Utd news: JJ Gabriel left in transfer lurch as Michael Carrick told to change plans

Manchester United manager Michael Carrick has been told to tweak his plans amid the latest update regarding JJ Gabriel's future at Old Trafford

View 2 Images JJ Gabriel is yet to receive an offer from Bayern Munich despite being in talks with the German giants (Image: Getty)

Michael Carrick's Premier League return hasn't gone to plan after Manchester United suffered further hurt on Saturday. Ten-man Tottenham snatched a 1-1 draw at Old Trafford following Dominic Solanke's late equaliser.

‌



‌



The international break was viewed as an opportunity for United to hit the reset button and rediscover some of last season's form. In reality, the club is in the midst of its worst start to a league campaign in 40 years.

‌



Carrick & Co travel to Spain for a Champions League showdown against Atletico Madrid next up on Tuesday. Before that, Mirror Football takes a look through some of the latest headlines emerging from Old Trafford.

‌



FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Bayern leave Gabriel in limbo

The positive news for JJ Gabriel and his team is that Bayern Munich are interested in his services after reportedly entering talks to sign the player. The bad news is they're yet to receive an offer from the Bundesliga giants as the January transfer window edges closer.

Man Utd star reveals Michael Carrick demand was not met in Tottenham draw READ MORE :

That's according to Sky Sport in Germany, which has reported Die Roten want a commitment from the player first. However, that may be tricky in the current landscape amid speculation he favours a move to Spain, with Barcelona and Real Madrid also said to be interested.

‌



It's no secret Gabriel, who turned 16 this month, and his entourage are seeking a way to get him out of Old Trafford. United have reportedly rejected the teenager's request to be deregistered from the club so he can complete a move elsewhere.

Much will depend on whether Gabriel succeeds in obtaining a European Union passport so he can obtain an EU work permit. However, that isn't expected to be an issue, as he is pursuing a Cypriot passport and also has a chance of obtaining Irish credentials.

‌



United are said to be eager to hang on to their starlet despite a breakdown between the club and the player. This reportedly stems from Gabriel's team demanding a greater guarantee of first-team minutes that went ignored.

Carrick urged to change midfield

View 2 Images Gary Neville has urged former team-mate Michael Carrick to abandon using Youri Tielemans and Kobiie Mainoo as a midfield pivot (Image: Shaun Brooks - CameraSport, CameraSport via Getty Images)

Amid the fallout from Saturday's disappointing draw at home to Spurs, United icon Gary Neville has called for change. Specifically in midfield, where he believes the club has already "seen enough" of Kobbie Mainoo and Youri Tielemans as a midfield pivot.

‌



The engine-room duo were hardly the only players to endure unremarkable outings for United this past weekend. However, Neville would like to see other combinations trialled and hinted Carlos Baleba could be one answer after impressing off the bench.

Speaking on The Gary Neville Podcast , he said: "[The team is] not running enough, they're not showing enough tenacity, determination and fighting spirit. The boos tell you they are really despondent with what they are watching."

Neville continued: "Tielemans and Mainoo, I think we’ve seen enough of it now. Not calling time on it, that’s probably too drastic. But I’ve seen enough of it to think, ‘That’s not dynamic enough to play at this football club in the Premier League'.

‌



"They’re both good players, by the way. But sometimes they don’t knit together or suit together, when Baleba came on that looked like a lot more energy. But the rest of them will have to get a grip."

Mainoo lost possession five times at Old Trafford on Saturday, more than any other player on the park. Meanwhile, Tielemans completed just 81 per cent of his passes in what was a wasteful day at the office.

Baleba could be handed a more prominent role after overcoming an injury to make his club debut against Spurs. Fellow summer signing Andrey Santos was an unused substitute against Tottenham, as was Mason Mount.

Sports.title: Arsenal news: Mikel Arteta plots Liverpool hijack as Gunners near 'triple deal'
Sports.content:
Arsenal news: Mikel Arteta plots Liverpool hijack as Gunners near 'triple deal'

Arsenal are reportedly eyeing a bid for a highly-rated player who is being pursued by Liverpool

View 3 Images Mikel Arteta and Arsenal are reportedly plotting a transfer hijack (Image: Catherine Ivill - AMA, Getty Images)

Arsenal are making moves behind the scenes to strengthen their squad in a number of different ways. The Gunners returned to Premier League action on Saturday, defeating Leeds United 2-1 in a tense first game back since the three-week international break.

‌



‌



There were long stretches of anxiety for manager Mikel Arteta and the Emirates Stadium faithful, especially given their previous result was a 3-0 drubbing away at Brighton. However, the reigning Premier League champions are still in a good position after six matches as they look to retain their title, with only Manchester City ahead of them in the table.

‌



Arsenal are not resting on their laurels either, with the club actively pursuing transfer targets ahead of the January window. Internally, the Gunners hierarchy are also looking to keep hold of several key players in the long term by negotiating new deals.

‌



Here, Mirror Football brings you two of the latest developments involving the north Londoners.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Arsenal plot Liverpool hijack

View 3 Images Gilberto Mora is in high demand (Image: 2026 MB Media)

‌



Arsenal have reportedly made an opening bid for Liverpool target Gilberto Mora. The Mexican wonderkid turns 18 this week, meaning the Gunners are allowed to sign him in January.

Attacking midfielder Mora, who remains under contract with Club Tijuana until 2029, had been linked with Premier League rivals Liverpool in recent weeks. But Mexican publication El Provenir claims Arsenal have approached his current club over a potential transfer.

Arsenal are long-term admirers of the teenager, who impressed as he became Mexico’s youngest ever player at the World Cup earlier this year. He has already earned 13 caps for his nation and has been eyed by the likes of Real Madrid and Barcelona, according to reports.

‌



Mora is said to have a release clause of just £21.2million in his current contract, meaning the English champions can secure him for a relatively modest fee.

Gunners near 'triple deal'

View 3 Images Arsenal are close to agreeing contract extensions with Martin Odegaard and Declan Rice (Image: Getty )

Arsenal are close to finalising new contract extensions for three key players, according to a report. Having recently tied down manager Arteta until the summer of 2030, Gunners chiefs are now looking to follow that up with deals for midfield powerhouse Declan Rice, captain Martin Odegaard and defender Jurrien Timber.

Article continues below

It has been widely reported in recent weeks that Rice is on the verge of signing a bumper new deal that will take him close to Arsenal’s top earner, Bukayo Saka. Rice is currently on a reported £240,000-per-week deal, which expires in the summer of 2028.

TEAMtalk reports that skipper Odegaard has also been in discussions with the club for over a year, with both his and Timber’s contracts expected to be signed during the November international break and, at the latest, before the January window opens. It is claimed that the club are incredibly confident that the remaining details can be resolved in the coming weeks.

Sports.title: Liverpool's Virgil Van Dijk says when he will 'definitely comment' on Man City's guilt
Sports.content:
Liverpool's Virgil Van Dijk says when he will 'definitely comment' on Man City's guilt

Virgil van Dijk has confessed he will break his silence on Manchester City's guilty verdict once the appeal is done and dusted having lost out to them numerous times in his Liverpool career

View 2 Images Virgil van Dijk will speak out on Man City's recent verdict

Virgil van Dijk insists he will "definitely share his comments" on Manchester City's guilty verdict once the appeal process has ran its course.

‌



‌



The Premier League leaders were recently found guilty of breaching 114 financial rules by an independent commission, with a punishment now expected, the most severe of which being relegation or the stripping of titles.

‌



City continue to protest their innocence and have lodged an appeal, which will see the saga drag on further, years after it initially started. During the period of the breaches, which spanned from 2009 to 2018, Liverpool finished second once, that back in 2014.

‌



But the players City were able to sign during the time they were inflating their revenue formed part of the squad that took on Jurgen Klopp's Liverpool, pipping them to the title in 2019 and 2022. Those teams involved Van Dijk, who could have a far greater trophy cabinet had it not been for the Manchester outfit.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

When quizzed on City's recent guilty verdict the Dutch defender said: "The only thing I can say, because it’s ongoing, is that I have really enjoyed the rivalry.

‌



"But that is on the pitch, what has happened off the pitch is a totally different story. Because it’s still ongoing, it’s not a good idea for me to comment on this. When it’s properly settled I will definitely share my comments on it but for now let’s wait and see."

Van Dijk was part of the Liverpool side that accumulated 97 points in 2019 and 92 points in 2022, but finished second on both occasions. They were also knocked out of domestic cups at the hands of Guardiola's City.

View 2 Images Virgil van Dijk's CV could look very different had it not been for Man City's success

‌



There was a clear feeling of anger at Anfield on Sunday as City played for the first time since their guilty verdict. The Liverpool crowd held up numerous banners making light of the scandal, highlighting the fact Enzo Maresca's side had cheated the system for years.

That came before City produced a ruthless second-half display to win 3-0, which kept them on top of the Premier League with six wins from six.

Van Dijk said: "Second half the red card changed the game, especially when you concede quickly afterwards. We end up with 10 men is the fact and we concede quickly after and it becomes a difficult game against them again."

Sports.title: Gary Neville picks out brutal Man City chant which will 'catch on' around Premier League grounds
Sports.content:
Gary Neville picks out brutal Man City chant which will 'catch on' around Premier League grounds

Manchester City rose above the noise to beat Liverpool 3-0 and maintain their unbeaten start to the Premier League season - but Gary Neville had a message for Enzo Maresca’s side

View 3 Images Gary Neville (Image: (James Gill - Danehouse/Getty Images))

Gary Neville has told Manchester City’s players that they will continue to face chants of “cheats”. And the former England international also believes a “huge cloud” will hang over the Premier League for months to come.

‌



‌



Enzo Maresca’s side were berated with chants of "cheats" as they returned to action for the first time against Liverpool since they were found guilty of more than 100 breaches of the Premier League’s financial rules during a nine-season period.

‌



Ryan Gravenberch’s dismissal for two bookings just after the hour changed the course of the game as City scored three times through Erling Haaland, Jeremy Doku and Rayan Cherki to maintain their unbeaten start to the season. But as those on the Kop chanted “cheats” as the game entered its final few minutes, and Neville, speaking on Sky’s commentary, said: "That is brutal. The players out there are being called cheats.

‌



“That's one of the worst things you can be called. That one could catch on across the grounds and across the country until the punishment does come in.”

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



While speaking after the game, Neville said: “This is the first Manchester City game I’ve done since the guilty verdicts were handed out a few weeks ago. I’ve said, if you could take me off Manchester City games moving forward for the next few months, until the (appeal) has been heard, I’d be absolutely delighted!

“To come and win at Anfield is really difficult. We should be eulogising over them without a ‘but’ or any hesitation. But there is that thing in the back in your mind, they’ve done a brilliant job here today, they’ve obviously dominated the game in the last 20 minutes, from the red card onwards.

“They’ve dug in, players like (Gianluigi) Donnarumma, (Ruben) Dias, (Elliot) Anderson, in that first half were excellent and stood strong as a group, senior players.

‌



View 3 Images Erling Haaland celebrates after scoring for Man City against Liverpool

“But at the end of the game, it’s quite hard, because you’re imagining if these guilty verdicts are confirmed in January, February, that Manchester City are not going to be in the position that they’re in, and there’s going to be a huge cloud hanging over the whole League.

“This is not good for the Premier League right now, that’s what I’ve just recognised today – this is really bad for the Premier League. And it’s going to continue for a few months.”

‌



City deny any wrongdoing and forward Haaland said post-match: "Every single person part of Man City, and every fan, this is a lovely moment that will stay with us for a long time. It was tough, it was hard but we showed amazing character from back to front. So proud of everyone.

View 3 Images Manchester City's players celebrate after their win over Liverpool at Anfield (Image: (Paul ELLIS / AFP via Getty Images)

"It's always tough to come here, if you look at the record it's tough. With the Pep and Klopp era it was tough for both teams, always has been.

Article continues below

“Important to stay strong mentally, stick together and do what you can do something about and the thing we can do something about is to play good football and fight together. That's the only thing we can do."

While team-mate Elliot Anderson hailed his side’s courage, saying: “I think we’ve shown real togetherness and fight. It’s a tough place to come and it’s challenging and we really stuck together out there, fought for each other and played well as well. I think we’ve shown courage here."

Sports.title: Gary Neville makes ‘take me off’ request to Sky Sports bosses as Premier League called out
Sports.content:
Gary Neville makes ‘take me off’ request to Sky Sports bosses as Premier League called out

Manchester City's victory over Liverpool in the Premier League forced Gary Neville into making a clear Sky Sports request

City fans fill Anfield away end with bananas

Gary Neville has told Sky Sports to take him off Manchester City games until the outcome of their appeal against breaching Premier League financial rules is known. Neville was on co-commentary for City's win against Liverpool at Anfield and found it difficult to dish out praise as the points may end up meaning nothing.

‌



‌



In a hostile atmosphere, City delivered a professional display and quitened the home crowd before taking immediate advantage of Ryan Gravenberch's red card card midway through the first half.

‌



Erling Haaland, Jeremy Doku and Rayan Cherki all found the back of the net in a blistering 13 minutes from Enzo Maresca's side. Despite winning in some style, it was Elliot Anderson that left Neville impressed.

‌



Man City players booed off at Anfield

However, he had refrained from issuing huge praise due to the ongoing financial charges case which later saw him make quite the request to Sky Sports.

He said on Sky Sports: "This is the first Manchester City game that I have done today since the charges or guilty verdicts were handed out a few weeks ago.

‌



"We were just doing the podcast then and said if you could take me off Manchester City games moving forward for the next few months until the verdicts have been heard, I would be absolutely delighted.

FOLLOW OUR MAN CITY FB PAGE! Follow our Manchester City Mirror Football Facebook page

"To come and win at Anfield is really difficult, we should be eulogising over them without a but or any hesitation, but there is that thing in the back of your mind.

‌



"They have done a brilliant job here today. They have dominated the game in the last 20 minutes, from the red card onwards. They have dug in and I think players like [Gianluigi] Donnarumma, [Ruben] Dias and Anderson, in that first-half were excellent. They stood strong as a group"

View Image Gianluigi Donnarumma made six saves to keep his clean sheet

"At the end of the game it is quite hard because you are imagining basically if these guilty verdicts are confirmed in January or February then Manchester City are not going to be in the position they are in and there is going to be a huge cloud hanging over the whole league, which is not good for the Premier League right now and that is what I have just recognised today. Really bad for the Premier League and it is going to continue for a few months."

‌



The appeals process has already been initiated, though it could be a considerable period before a definitive conclusion is reached. The sanctions hearing is also ongoing, with their potential penalty likely to be revealed first.

While praise may be challenging to offer, both Neville and Jamie Carragher made it abundantly clear that the players don't warrant the hostile treatment.

Neville said: "That's the problem for the Man City staff, players and supporters, they are blameless in all of this. The stain, stigma, reputational damage that hits them, it's nothing to do with them but they have to face it on the pitch, in the stadium, week after week."

Article continues below

Carragher added: "The players on that pitch they've had to face the criticism. All eyes on this game, you almost look at the director's box thinking they should be on the pitch facing the barrage of criticism."

Sports.title: Potters Charm makes his chasing debut at Worcester
Sports.content:
We have a busy day's racing on Monday with action from Newcastle, Worcester and Yarmouth, live on Sky Sports Racing...

3.07 Worcester - Potters Charm makes chasing debut

Potters Charm makes his chasing debut in the Paul Ferguson's Jumpers to Follow Novices' Chase at Worcester.

He found it tough when pitched into open company last season after only losing once in his novice campaign but got back to winning ways in January at Windsor before scoring at Grade Two level in the National Spirit Hurdle at Fontwell.

Connections have always been optimistic of him doing his best work over fences so they will be hoping for a successful chasing debut, clearly being the one to beat.

Jupiter des Mottes remains unexposed and holds a good level of form over hurdles, notably when winning a solid handicap hurdle at Perth in April. He made his chasing debut back in November 2025 but did not take to fences at the time, however, he looks the type to improve for a fence at three miles and switched to top trainer Dan Skelton, a much better chasing attempt is anticipated.

Who's Glen has run respectably over fences, and he can use his experience here, although Nick Scholfield's charge will be hoping that the former two fluff their lines over fences.

Irish pointer, Vicomte le Brave makes rules debut.

6.00 Newcastle - Promising Starburster makes handicap debut

Promising two-year-old Starburster makes handicap debut in the Follow @attheraces On Instagram Nursery Handicap at Newcastle.

The Richard Spencer-trained filly was an eye-catching fourth on debut before improving for her second start when scoring at Newbury. She showed a willing attitude that day to beat Bidsta who won on her next two starts. Her unexposed profile and strong form should mean she can be very competitive off an opening mark of 82.

She does meet some creditable rivals as Innichen holds plenty of experience in big meeting nurseries and should go well in calmer waters and Blazing Inferno can bounce back to form after finishing last in the Weatherbys 2-Y-O Stakes at York, with a poor draw in 15.

Siouxperb could potentially be overlooked. He disappointed in the Coventry after a dazzling debut, before running well to finish a close second to a nice type in Sonic Angel. The Acomb Stakes was then too hot for him before he didn't seem to enjoy the soft conditions at Ayr. He contains the potential to return to form back on the all-weather and dropped two-pounds in the handicap.

Minzelle is another who has been highly tried in Listed company after impressive early form. She has gone off favourite in her last three, although has not shown much.

2.24 Yarmouth - Eye-catching Status Symbol steps up in trip

Eye-catching Status Symbol steps up in trip in the British EBF Restricted Novice Stakes at Yarmouth.

His opposition set a solid standard, although Status Symbol stayed on very nicely into fourth on debut at 50-1. Ed Walker's two-year-olds usually improve plenty for their first starts, and this son of Space Blues looks sure to improve now up in trip to 10 furlongs, with his dam being a winner over a mile and a half.

Able Tasman remains the only winner in the field as he won after a four-month break on his second start, beating the re-opposing Deira Moon, who he reopposes here.

Deira Moon ran on well that day, despite getting hampered in the final strides. He produced his best effort to date next time out at Goodwood when second again, and a seven-pound penalty for Able Tasman could bring them even closer.

Quintillion put up a much improved second start when bumping into the smart Wykehurst Park. Up again in trip to 10-furlongs should suit and he can put up a bold bid in attempting to break his maiden tag.

Good Job and Spong Hill make their debuts, with the former containing the most promising pedigree being half-brother to dual Group Two winner, Opal Tiara.

City's victory at Liverpool on Sunday, which hinged on Ryan Gravenberch's controversial dismissal, took them back to the top of the Premier League ahead of champions Arsenal.

But the win was inevitably overshadowed after the independent Premier League commission found Manchester City in breach of the Premier League's financial rules - City have denied wrongdoing and have lodged an appeal - with commentator Peter Drury describing the game as "the most peculiar day in Premier League history".

"We're sat here not knowing what it means," reflected Gary Neville. "City supporters will be delighted [with the win], but I don't think they recognise right now the stain, the stigma and the damage this is going to do to them.

"Liverpool fans are singing 'going down' they're shouting 'cheats' and you can't get away from that."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jamie Carragher says the country's feelings towards Manchester City will only grow unless the case is swiftly resolved. Listen to the Gary Neville podcast in full on Sky Sports platforms

Jamie Carragher added: "In some ways, the feeling around Manchester City will only grow the more they win. It will keep growing and growing around the country. We need a resolution as soon as possible. We're watching a game today, but what does it actually mean?

'Cheat' banners were unfurled by both sets of fans, with every touch by a City player greeted by a chant of 'cheat' in the final minutes.

"There was a banner over in that far corner which I thought was devastating - 'A generation of supporters have been cheated'. I thought you know, that will be the mood around the country for 10-15 years they've been cheated," said Neville on his podcast.

"We should be absolutely eulogising over a performance like that, where they've come through and withstood a really difficult opening spell - which is always the case here at Anfield - and then gone on to come out on top.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Roy Keane shares his thoughts on Manchester City following the club being found guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of Premier League financial rules by an independent commission; City have lodged their appeal against the verdict

"But there's a 'but', isn't there? And we're sat here not knowing what this means.

"We know that Manchester City go three points clear at the top of the league but there's a feeling that ultimately this is not going to be where Manchester City finish."

Sports.title: Euro Debrief: Gordon's first Barca goal and Spence's Inter debut
Sports.content:
Welcome to The Euro Debrief, a new Sky Sports column in which Adam Bate rounds up some of the key stories from the latest matches across the continent. This week:

Gordon scores for Barca

Dortmund and Bayern slip

Lazio still pushing Inter

PSG go through the gears

Tightest title race ever?

LaLiga: Gordon's first Barca goal

Not everyone was convinced when Anthony Gordon signed for Barcelona in the summer but the former Newcastle winger has emerged as a popular figure there already. He bagged his first Barca goal two minutes into their 3-0 home win over Getafe on Saturday.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the LaLiga match between Barcelona and Getafe at Spotify Camp Nou

Lamine Yamal is the darling of the crowd and Raphinha is the talisman up top but there is a role for Gordon - as well as fellow new arrival Karim Adeyemi - and both are playing it to perfection thus far by taking some of the load off the star man. Hansi Flick is happy.

"He is doing great. He was also doing well in the previous matches when he did not score," said the Barca coach afterwards. "He gives us a lot. He has speed, moves well with the ball, all the dribbling he has. He is always dangerous and creates chances."

Image: Anthony Gordon is already proving a popular figure at Barcelona

LaLiga: Table | Fixtures & results

Yan Diomande is also off the mark for Real Madrid, his winner coming in a more fraught win over Villarreal. The game was notable for Vinicius Junior thinking that he had scored only to be sent off for pulling the hair of Nathan Saliba on the way to making it happen.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the LaLiga match between Real Madrid and Villarreal

Jose Mourinho was unimpressed, skipping media duties, but at least it was a win after the derby loss to Atletico. Mourinho's side remain fourth as there were wins for Atletico and for Real Betis, who did not even need Troy Parrott to score in their 5-2 win over Osasuna.

For once, another Madrid side took much of the headlines in Spain as Rayo Vallecano fans succeeded in getting their game against Athletic Club abandoned. Paper planes and rubber balls rained down in the first game of the season at the Estadio de Vallecas.

The ground had been closed due to health and safety concerns and the protest was part of an ongoing dispute between supporters and the club's owner-president Raul Martin Presa over his failure to invest in the atmospheric old venue. Consider awareness raised.

LaLiga results: Malaga 1-1 Espanyol, Rayo Vallecano A-A Athletic Club, Deportivo Alaves 1-2 Atletico Madrid, Barcelona 3-0 Getafe, Real Madrid 1-0 Villarreal, Elche 0-0 Celta Vigo, Real Sociedad 3-2 Deportivo A Coruna, Real Betis 5-2 Osasuna, Racing Santander 2-2 Valencia.

Bundesliga: Neuer scrutiny at Bayern

The fastest goal of the weekend, indeed the fastest goal in Bundesliga history, was scored against Bayern Munich on Saturday. Augsburg's Robin Fellhauer dispossessed the great Manuel Neuer and put his side in front after just eight seconds of the game.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Bundesliga match between Augsburg and Bayern Munich

Bayern recovered to earn a point, Harry Kane assisting both of their goals in a 2-2 draw, and Vincent Kompany's team really should have won it. But with Neuer also culpable for the second Augsburg goal there is increasing heat on the 40-year-old goalkeeping icon.

Neuer's Germany return at the World Cup was not a success and with Jonas Urbig, his Bayern deputy, having been given his international debut by Jurgen Klopp in the recent window, it feels a matter of when not if the legend is replaced at club level now too.

Bayern's slip will only leave Borussia Dortmund more frustrated that they threw away a two-goal lead late on at home to Werder Bremen on Friday evening. Niclas Fullkrug, the former Dortmund striker, found the equaliser in stoppage-time at Signal Iduna Park.

As a result, it is Freiburg who top the table in Germany. Elsewhere, the evergreen Patrik Schick scored in a fifth consecutive Bundesliga game for Bayer Leverkusen, while there was a hat-trick for Christopher Nkunku, who is enjoying his second spell with RB Leipzig.

There are only four teams in Europe's major leagues yet to concede a league goal in front of their own supporters this season. Schalke are among them despite not scoring themselves. Leverkusen have six goals, AC Milan five. But Leipzig have scored 14 without reply.

Down at the bottom, Borussia Monchengladbach are still searching for their first point of the campaign after another painful defeat - this time in the derby in Cologne. Said El Mala, who nearly joined Dortmund in the summer, scored the winner in that one.

Bundesliga results: Borussia Dortmund 2-2 Werder Bremen, Augsburg 2-2 Bayern Munich, Hoffenheim 2-3 Hamburg, Mainz 3-4 Bayer Leverkusen, Paderborn 0-2 Stuttgart, Union Berlin 1-0 Elversberg, RB Leipzig 6-0 Eintracht Frankfurt, Cologne 2-1 Borussia Monchengladbach, Freiburg 2-1 Schalke.

Serie A: Spence debuts for Inter

Djed Spence made his belated debut for Inter in their comfortable 3-0 win over Parma. The result was safe long before the England international was introduced as a second-half substitute but Inter boss Cristian Chivu welcomed the chance to call upon him.

"Let us enjoy his first 25 minutes, and not forget that he has only been training with the team for a week. You cannot ask too much of him or you will push him into the red," said Chivu. "Today, San Siro gave him a shot of adrenaline and that will help all of us."

There was British interest elsewhere with Harry Winks' Cagliari drawing at home to Juventus to stay fourth. Scott McTominay also made his return from minor heart surgery as a substitute in Napoli's win over Frosinone, with Kevin De Bruyne scoring two.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kevin De Bruyne starred as Napoli defeated Frosinone in Serie A

Incredibly, nobody has scored more goals in a major European league than Donyell Malen for Roma in this calendar year but the Netherlands forward is going to struggle to hang on to that record much longer as he faces a suspension for his red card at Como.

Roma did well to leave with the point that preserves both teams unbeaten records, something Milan can claim too after their draw at Sassuolo. But Lazio are currently the closest challenges to Inter after their 3-1 win at Monza continued their unlikely run this season.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Former Arsenal defender Nuno Tavares scores incredible THUNDERBOLT for Lazio!

Ex-Arsenal man Nuno Tavares scored a stunner in that one. Gennaro Gattuso had been expected to struggle, particularly with the fans protesting the ownership. Instead, with five wins and a draw from their six games, it is Lazio's best start to a Serie A season ever.

Serie A results: Genoa 2-1 Fiorentina, Inter 3-0 Parma, Napoli 3-0 Frosinone, Como 0-0 Roma, Lazio 3-1 Monza, Lecce 1-2 Bologna, Sassuolo 1-1 Milan, Cagliari 1-1 Juventus.

Ligue 1: Monaco slip as PSG prowl

Filipe Luis had sought to downplay Monaco's title prospects despite topping the table in France and that pessimism was somewhat explained as his side lost a two-goal lead at home to Toulouse. It is a disappointing draw with Paris Saint-Germain climbing ominously.

PSG were 3-1 winners over Le Mans, a result that lifts them up to sixth in Ligue 1 after their slow start. Luis Enrique is still rotating heavily but it only needed a brief blast from the big guns, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia coming on to score what proved to be the winner.

Elsewhere, Cameron Archer scored for the fourth game in a row in a losing effort for Auxerre, while less familiarly, Liam Rosenior fell to defeat for the first time as Paris FC coach. Marseille, meanwhile, managed to beat Troyes to move out of the bottom three.

Ligue 1 results: Lens 2-1 Lyon, Lille 1-0 Le Havre, Brest 5-1 Angers, Lorient 1-0 Paris FC, Monaco 2-2 Toulouse, PSG 3-1 Le Mans, Nice 2-1 Strasbourg, Rennes 4-1 Auxerre, Troyes 0-2 Marseille.

Elsewhere: Norway's title race

Porto keep doing it. Eight wins from eight now for the reigning champions in Portugal but they are not making it easy. This week they came from behind to win late on at Maritimo. Porto have now won after conceding the first goal in three of their last four matches.

There were changes at the top in the Netherlands and Turkey. Feyenoord bumped AZ Alkmaar down to third to claim their spot in front of a fantastic crowd at De Kuip, while Amedspor conceded a stoppage-time equaliser that means Galatasaray lead in Turkey.
