Viking are currently top with eight games to go based on the head-to-head record. Bodo/Glimt do have a home game to come against the leaders but turning that head-to-head record around will be surely impossible. Viking won 5-0 in the previous game in April.

Sports.title: Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s action
Sports.content:
1 City’s triumph leaves pressing questions

The manner of Manchester City’s victory at Liverpool was an article of both vindication and vilification. Those gleefully wielding inflatable bananas in the Anfield away end could thumb their noses. Why not enjoy the dances of defiance until the music stops? The same went for City players, asked to perform under the darkest of clouds, able to focus, at last, on football, rather than legal argument and uncertain futures. Beyond City, the sight of a club found guilty of 100-plus charges laying waste to such rivals as Liverpool was deeply uncomfortable. The Premier League season and product are badly damaged until the matter is somehow resolved. What happened at Anfield should double the haste for a resolution. Chants of “cheat” whenever City players, the game already won, slipped the ball around, are bound to be repeated at other stadiums. Enzo Maresca has described his club’s plight as “noise” but his team’s victory did absolutely nothing to turn the volume down. John Brewin

View image in fullscreen Enzo Maresca soaks up the acclaim of the travelling fans at the end of the match. Photograph: Robbie Jay Barratt/AMA/Getty Images

2 Iraola’s revolution yet to take off

Andoni Iraola’s Liverpool reboot will require patience. They showed plenty of drive and determination against Manchester City but also uneven edges, polish lacking. Iraola’s aim was to get his players in their opponents’ faces, deepening any doubts circulating in City’s players. Mission mostly accomplished during the first half. A flurry of chances at the beginning of the second half had City rocking only for Ryan Gravenberch’s dismissal to pull the rug. With Alexander Isak and Cody Gakpo missing, Liverpool lacked the quality to cause the necessary damage. Lewis Koumas played well in the role of agitator as emergency centre-forward. Víctor Muñoz continues to be full of buzz but Bradley Barcola and Florian Wirtz, both players signed for £100m plus, are supposed to supply the cutting edge. Barcola has the mitigation of being a new arrival, while discussions about Wirtz border on football cliche. Once Gravenberch departed, and Trey Nyoni was required in midfield, the finger was always going to be pointed in the German’s direction. JB

3 Sage rides luck to get one over on Glasner

For the second time this season, Pierre Sage watched his Crystal Palace side win a Premier League game despite not being at their best; the Frenchman was honest enough to admit they had been slightly fortunate against Nottingham Forest. But after overcoming Oliver Glasner on his return to Selhurst Park, Sage can look forward to a reunion of his own against Lyon in the Europa League on Thursday. He will know Palace must improve defensively. Axel Disasi will be available again after being suspended against Forest, although he will miss the trip to face Palace’s arch-rivals Brighton next weekend. “It’s not normal to concede as many chances as we conceded,” Sage said of the first 40 minutes against Forest, when Walter Benítez made a string of fine saves. “We need to be consistent but after the international break it’s a good result that can help us in our future games.” Ed Aarons

4 Maitland-Niles makes a mess

Ainsley Maitland-Niles has some apologising to do. The right-back made two errors that ultimately cost Everton a first away victory in the league since February. The former Arsenal player contrived to botch what should have been an easy interception, gifting Sorba Thomas the chance to tee up Joe Gelhardt for Hull’s opener. With the visitors having turned the game around to lead, Maitland-Niles then got too cute defending against Elliot Stroud in the corner, allowing the Swede to find Mohamed Belloumi for the equaliser. With a squad short on attacking options, Everton cannot afford to score twice away from home and come away with only a point. Tom Bassam

View image in fullscreen Ainsley Maitland-Niles (centre) did not have the best game for Everton. Photograph: Tony McArdle/Everton FC/Getty Images

5 Spurs’ slow progress is still progress

With Manchester United so sluggish and shapeless, they did not serve as much of a barometer of Tottenham’s progress under Roberto De Zerbi. Though if anyone can take positives from Saturday’s clutter of a contest full of mistakes, it should be Spurs. “From a long time Tottenham played without this blood, this character, and I want it,” said De Zerbi. He has plenty to improve upon. Dominic Solanke wore the captain’s armband and got the late equaliser his team’s efforts with 10 men had threatened. If only Spurs’ finishing had not been so profligate in a first half when their energy made United fans mothball their jibes at Manchester City and resume worrying about the failings of Michael Carrick’s team. “Work together, stay together, have dinner together and get to know each other better,” is De Zerbi’s prescription for improvement. He continues to talk of a work in progress. Slow progress, slower than desirable, but Old Trafford offered hope. JB

6 Madueke shines as Arteta rolls dice

A key topic of discussion for Arsenal fans before the Leeds match was who Mikel Arteta would pick on the left in the absence of the injured Christos Tzolis. Noni Madueke got the nod and the England winger, who was dropped from the latest Three Lions squad, proved a point. “He deserved the chance and he took it,” Arteta said of the wide man, who played out of position but whose pace was too explosive for Leeds’ James Justin and Jayden Bogle. Madueke’s deliveries were also consistently dangerous. He created the most chances in the game (three) and had the most touches in the box (eight). This was good news for a player who had looked to be receding from view at both club and international level. But it also cast a dim light on the range of attacking options available to Arteta after a summer in which Tzolis was the only addition to the forward line. Arsenal took a gamble on Madueke here and it worked out. How many more will they have to take over a long and arduous season? Paul MacInnes

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Mikel Arteta ponders his attacking options, or possibly something else. Photograph: Vince Mignott/EPA

7 Swift starts prove a boon for Blues

Chelsea have scored during the first 10 minutes in five of their six games this season. Xabi Alonso says the fast starts are nothing to do with him but Morgan Rogers had a different view after the 5-1 win against Bournemouth. “I put it down to the manager’s team talks,” Rogers said. “He gets us firing, gets us going. We always want to start off on the front foot. It’s about starting well and getting the lead. A lot of games, especially at home, we have won after jumping on the back of early goals – it’s a good trait to have. We need to keep going.” Jacob Steinberg

8 Aston Villa’s ground for concern?

Home form has been a cornerstone of Unai Emery’s extraordinary success but a victory at Villa Park this season is proving elusive. It’s early days, of course, with Wednesday’s Champions League date at home to Fenerbahce offering another chance to get off the mark – but Emery recognises the value of a fortress. The stadium is different on the eye this season, the North Stand being rebuilt to take the ground’s capacity north of 50,000. Can a three-sided ground impact things? “I certainly hated it as a player,” said Brentford’s head coach, Keith Andrews, whose side remain unbeaten this campaign. “It just feels wrong, doesn’t it? When I was growing up as a kid, some Irish legends played here – Ray Houghton, Paul McGrath, Andy Townsend – so it’s always been a special place for me and you can feel the history of it. With a stand missing, it’s a bit different.” Ben Fisher

View image in fullscreen Kristoffer Ajer (third right) secures a point for Brentford late on at Villa Park. Photograph: Nick Potts/PA

9 Steely Tractor Boys show mettle

Six games in Ipswich are well ahead of the run rate on points required for survival. Gary O’Neil, the modern Premier League firefighter, has brought a doggedness to the Tractor Boys that they lacked when Kieran McKenna took them into the Premier League two years ago. The new Ipswich manager has been ruthless too. The summer signing Kjell Scherpen was dropped for a known quantity in Christian Walton after the win at Palace and, while it did not secure a first clean sheet of the league campaign, the veteran keeper does look a more assured presence. The goals against column will concern O’Neil – only two sides in the division have conceded more – but his side’s stamina will be pleasing. Ipswich have now have scored winners after the 90-minute mark three times. It is not a sustainable strategy but it indicates a team with the stomach for a fight. TB

10 Hamstrung Black Cats lacking threat

Sunderland’s supposed summer transfer market priority was the acquisition of a specialist right winger. Ultimately they failed to recruit one and it is arguably costing Régis Le Bris’s team dear. They started Saturday’s deserved home defeat to an impressive Brighton with two natural right-backs on the pitch, the second, Thomas Meunier, operating in an advanced position. When Meunier, a far from shabby player, injured a hamstring, the industrious yet ineffective Nilson Angulo was shifted from his preferred left wing to the right. But a Sunderland XI lacking the hamstrung Brian Brobbey at centre-forward failed to threaten. Surely the moment has come for Le Bris to offer the talented but currently overlooked Chris Rigg or Chemsdine Talbi starting spots at Bournemouth next Sunday? Before that Sunderland travel to face Torreense in Portugal on Thursday. After collecting only four Premier League points this season, Le Bris is likely to rotate heavily for that Europa League engagement. With a Bournemouth trip followed swiftly by a game at Lech Poznan and a visit from Leeds, his task looks tricky. Louise Taylor

Sports.title: Premier League returns in shadow of Manchester City’s judgment day | Jonathan Wilson
Sports.content:
The Cimbri are heading menacingly south, but in Rome life goes on. The asteroid is definitely coming this way, but people go to work, eat, drink, plan as usual. The White Walkers are approaching the Wall, but the squabbles between the great houses go on. Everyone in the Premier League knows the crisis is approaching, thinks – hopes, fears? – it may be apocalyptic, but until it arrives, what can you do but carry on?

After any break, there’s always an awkward moment while everybody resets. What was the cliffhanger we left the soap opera on? What new plotline had just been seeded? This is one of the reasons international weeks are so disruptive. It’s not just that the Premier League story slows for a while, it’s that we are reminded that these entities are not eternal but alliances of convenience between paid employees who have a life outside the soap opera.

But there has never before been an international break so disruptive as this, never such a sense of unreality about a weekend of Premier League football. It’s not that, the 2022 World Cup aside, this has been the longest international break in history. Nor can anyone, surely, be unaware of the dominant narrative of this window: between 2009 and 2018, Manchester City cheated. Perhaps an away game at Anfield for City is not quite the event it was when Pep Guardiola and Jürgen Klopp were at their peak, but it should still be a great footballing occasion. Yet this was an afternoon when the football felt secondary.

City continue to protest their innocence, clinging to the now-familiar formula that they have a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence that will somehow clear their name, if only people wouldn’t keep refuting it. They have launched an appeal, but if that fails the sanction is likely to be unprecedentedly severe. Do their games matter? Will they be annulled before the season’s end? Was this victory just the difference between finishing the season on -100 points and -97? Could they be expelled from the league? Until sentence is announced, there will an air of provisionality about everything they do. It’s the seconds after an incident that everybody knows VAR will check, the ghost football that might be cancelled, but extended for weeks.

This, though, is not only an issue of the present; it’s an issue of the past. The sanction may or may not strip City of their titles. Many City fans will ignore such a punishment, continue to claim those honours, will point out that memories cannot be so easily extinguished. But even if City’s appeal is successful, or even if the sanction does not relitigate the past, there will be asterisks there in the minds of those who are not City fans, and perhaps also in the minds of some of those who are. Add in Chelsea’s offences, and the Premier League is coming to the end of an 18-year period in which very little was quite as it seemed.

View image in fullscreen Manchester City fans remain defiant despite the guilty verdict against the club they support. Photograph: Michael Regan/Getty Images

The inflatable bananas brandished by City’s support at Anfield on Sunday may have harked back to an earlier, more innocent era, but there is no going back. City are not the club of Imre Varadi any more; as it stands they are the club guilty of the greatest act of cheating in English football history. Their fans can do the Poznan in a spirit of resistance, but they cannot turn their back on the shame their leaders have brought upon them.

What that means for the longer-term credibility of the league can only be guessed at. The basis of sport is faith. Incredible finishes mean little if nothing can be believed. Why go through the emotional agonies if a result might be struck off a decade later for offences committed in the air-conditioned offices of a distant state? Will the City decision undermine faith, or reaffirm it, come as proof that cheats do not prosper, that they will – eventually – be exposed, that the Premier League, almost alone in this grubby world of compromise with and abasement before the mega-rich, is prepared to do what is right?

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

City were booed, there were some chants of “going down” and there were a handful of banners, but Anfield was not the seething pit of disgust many had anticipated. Nor was there much City-related fury at other grounds, although Manchester United fans, erasing all the silverware of the past 15 years, reinstituted their counter on the Stretford End recording the length of time since City last won a trophy. The general sense is of bafflement and bewilderment; what does this mean? What might happen?

It is as though the scale of City’s offences have not yet been fully grasped, that no one quite knows what might happen next. City fans, similarly, seem set on a policy of defiance, as though the scandal is something that has been done to them, rather than the result of the actions of their own directors. To an extent, that is understandable. Until the sanctions are announced, until the result of the appeal is known, the sense of unreality, the phoney war, will go on. The crisis is coming, but its impact has not yet been felt.

Sports.title: Manchester City shrug off chaos and controversy in public shaming at Anfield | Andy Hunter
Sports.content:
Anfield welcomed Manchester City to their new reality, a sullied place where every touch is accompanied by cries of “cheat”, any favourable decision is considered proof of further conspiracy and every victory hollow. But Welcome to Hell this was not. The only body of irrefutable evidence in City’s favour since the guilty verdicts landed is that Enzo Maresca’s league leaders appear immune to prosecution and persecution.

That may well change depending on the outcome of City’s appeal and any punishment that eventually arises, likewise the merits and value of a commanding 3-0 win on Liverpool soil. The sight of Erling Haaland savouring a statement victory in front of City’s supporters after the final whistle, while chants of “going down” echoed around the rest of the stadium, captured the schism at the heart of this Premier League season.

City were transformed by the introduction of Jérémy Doku and the dismissal of the Liverpool midfielder Ryan Gravenberch. They were never intimidated, always composed and look a genuine threat to Arsenal’s defence of the title. And yet this could prove their last Premier League appearance at Anfield for the foreseeable future.

It may be difficult, nigh on impossible, to sustain this level of motivation and desire knowing that relegation beckons. Knowing that no one outside City will give them credit for another title triumph did not affect them here, however.

In the 17 days since news of City’s guilt first emerged, and the gestation period of a prolonged international break, their return to action in a Premier League undermined and distorted by their 114 breaches had been built up as a chastening day of reckoning for Maresca’s side. It proved nothing of the sort.

Anfield can still make its voice heard to seismic effect and in the frantic start when Liverpool flew at City, with a fired-up Ronald Araújo whipping up the crowd after winning a challenge against Antoine Semenyo, the collective sense of injustice at a club pipped three times to the title by those in sky blue inspired Andoni Iraola’s players. But bear pits rarely feature in the corporate packaged world of Premier League entertainment 2026.

The “reception committee” for the City team coach before the game was populated by fans carrying selfie-sticks and club shop carrier bags, not an incensed brooding mob. At half-time the Kop was asked to cheer on corporate guests of the club sponsor Standard Chartered as they took part in a penalty shootout, many clearly kicking a ball for the first time in their lives.

There were incessant chants of “you cheating bastards” and various banners of damning judgement, many with an Oasis twist that may have been appreciated by Noel Gallagher in the away end. “And after all you really robbed us all” read one. “All of your stars are fading away,” read another. “A generation of supporters cheated,” cut to the heart of the issue confronting not only Liverpool but the Premier League itself.

View image in fullscreen Liverpool supporters point out that their side finished second to Manchester City three times in the space of eight years. Photograph: Peter Byrne/PA

The City support responded in kind. “In Khaldoon we trust – we’ve won it all!” proclaimed the away flags. The visitors, while performing the Poznan before kick-off, also reclaimed one of the “Cheat” flags that had been doing a healthy trade outside the ground before the game. The inflatable bananas that were once part of the City fanscape also made a comeback, a throwback to more innocent days when their club was not in the dock for inflating sponsorship deals. There was more bickering than tangible animosity. The four men who walked on to the pitch carrying the Premier League hoardings before kick-off received a more hostile reception than City’s players when they appeared for the warm-up.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The decision for City’s team coach to arrive by a different route ensured a tame reception for the visitors. All eyes were on the usual entrance on Anfield Road as City were ushered in from the opposite side of the stadium. It meant even the referees’ chief Howard Webb could walk in almost unnoticed. The hostility cranked up as soon as the contest started and City, using their vast experience to telling effect, gradually drained the venom from the atmosphere and the threat from a depleted Liverpool team. But it was the 62nd-minute dismissal of Gravenberch that had the greater bearing on the outcome.

Doku proved a devastating substitute for Iliman Ndiaye and tormented Liverpool from the left, being involved not only in the red card but all three City goals. The hosts, minus their two most potent attacking players this season in Cody Gakpo and Alexander Isak, plus a hamstrung Dominik Szoboszlai, had no answer with Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola largely anonymous.

The Kop made no calls to be handed the trophies lost to City – and what would that really mean now anyway? – but took solace in demanding that punishment be served in the form of relegation this season. “No trophies for 50 years, que será, será,” the home crowd chanted. But there was no immediate retribution for Liverpool here. City dealt with the chaos and the controversy serenely.

Sports.title: ‘We make our own noise’: Maresca hails Manchester City after Liverpool triumph
Sports.content:
Enzo Maresca praised Manchester City for “making their own noise” at Liverpool as they brushed aside the controversy and threats surrounding the club with a comprehensive 3-0 win at Anfield.

City, in their first outing since the club were found guilty on 114 charges relating to Premier League financial rules, maintained their 100% start to the season courtesy of goals from Erling Haaland, the excellent Jérémy Doku and Rayan Cherki. A sixth successive league win ensured Maresca equalled the best start to a managerial reign in Premier League history and kept City at the top of the table.

The City head coach said: “My message to the players since we were together three days ago, when they all came back from their national teams, has been quite clear: guys, the noise will always be there so it’s about how we learn to deal with the noise and it’s our duty to make our noise. Our noise is to win games in the way we did today and to be happy. It was our fans making the noise at the end of the game today.”

Maresca smiled when asked whether he needed City’s appeal to be heard as quickly as possible in order to celebrate such an impressive win. “You cannot imagine how happy I am,” he replied. “I don’t care. I’m here to try and prepare games and to win games. Hopefully I can speak about this situation when we win the appeal.”

City’s chief executive Ferran Soriano was present at Anfield as the fallout from the club’s guilty verdict continues. Maresca reflected: “We were all together. For the importance of the game, Liverpool away, Anfield away, it was a good idea from the club to be all together. That togetherness is what we need.”

The game turned on the 62nd-minute dismissal of Liverpool midfielder Ryan Gravenberch for a second bookable offence. Haaland opened the scoring one minute later and City then ran riot.

Andoni Iraola, the Liverpool head coach, said: “We played two different games: one until the red card, and one from the red card until the end. I think we were the better team until the red card and they were better than us, obviously, after the red card. But I think the players deserve credit today because they’ve given everything.”

Iraola insisted Gravenberch’s red card was harsh. “I think the first foul of Ryan is never a yellow card, never,” he added. “The referee doesn’t even call the foul straight away. He lets it go, Elliot Anderson does a couple of steps and then decides to go down. I don’t know why he shows the yellow card after that because it’s not a situation where it leaves an advantage.”

Sports.title: Pino finishes off Nottingham Forest on Glasner’s unhappy Crystal Palace return
Sports.content:
It is fair to say Oliver Glasner has had more enjoyable afternoons. The Nottingham Forest head coach arrived in south London dressed like a bouncer from All Bar One in a black bomber jacket, as if he was anticipating trouble, but was instead given a rapturous reception by the home fans who used to worship him.

The generosity towards their former manager seemed to have extended to Palace’s players as Dan Ndoye was handed a goal in the third minute. Pierre Sage’s side were awful in the opening 40 minutes. Yet Forest could not find a way to beat Walter Benítez again as Liam Delap missed a golden chance to extend their lead and the Argentina goalkeeper’s heroics inspired a thrilling comeback that secured Sage’s first home victory in the Premier League since taking over from Glasner in the summer.

The irony that Daichi Kamada, who won the Europa League under Glasner while they were at Eintracht Frankfurt before he brought him to Selhurst Park on a free transfer, should score his first Premier League goal to equalise in his 68th appearance was surely not lost on the Austrian.

But he and the notoriously trigger-happy Evangelos Marinakis – the Forest owner who was conspicuous by his absence from the directors’ box after his public spats with his Palace counterpart, Steve Parish – will have serious concerns about how his team capitulated after conceding the equaliser. Jefferson Lerma bundled home the second from a corner just before half-time and Yéremy Pino wrapped up the points with a goal that was greeted with a chorus of: “You’re getting sacked in the morning”, directed towards Glasner.

“Call it karma or whatever but it was like I didn’t deserve to win at Selhurst Park because the players did everything,” said Glasner, who claimed not to have heard the taunts from the Palace fans. “I think this was the most dominant Nottingham Forest performance. But not the right result. So, this gives me confidence. My job is not to be influenced negatively by the result.”

There has been plenty of water under the bridge since these two sides met here 14 months ago. Marinakis is suing Palace and “persons unknown” after a banner featuring an incendiary cartoon of him was unfurled during the first half of that game, with the supporters’ group that is thought to have been behind it having since disbanded. Glasner’s decision to join Forest in the summer only added to the ill-feeling that was created by the dispute over Palace’s demotion from the Europa League last season, even if the Austrian was given a warm welcome before and after the game.

The home fans made it clear where their grievances remain as they immediately launched into the anti-Uefa and Marinakis song that was the soundtrack to their Conference League triumph under Glasner, while the Forest supporters responded with taunts of: “We’ve got Ollie Glasner”. They had more reason to celebrate after only two minutes when Anan Khalaili’s weak header presented Ndoye with the chance to run through and score. Forest could barely believe their luck.

View image in fullscreen The Nottingham Forest head coach, Oliver Glasner, responds to a generous reception from the Crystal Palace supporters. Photograph: Andrew Couldridge/Action Images/Reuters

They piled on the pressure, with makeshift defender Lerma – only playing in the absence of the suspended Axel Disasi – looking particularly vulnerable. Jaydee Canvot was guilty of losing possession when Morgan Gibbs-White picked out the unmarked Ndoye and Benítez tipped over before Daniel Muñoz was inches away from scoring against his former club.

But the momentum shifted firmly towards the hosts thanks to a miraculous save from Benítez – deputising for the injured Dean Henderson – that denied Delap from three yards out after Gibbs-White’s shot rebound off the crossbar. “Walter made a save with a lot of bravery,” said Sage, who refused the opportunity to gloat about beating Glasner. “It’s not about revenge,” he insisted.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Delap spurned another golden opportunity with his head and Forest were made to pay just before the break when Kamada scrambled home inside the six-yard area after Jørgen Strand Larsen’s pass deflected straight into his path. Suddenly Palace found their belief. Tyrick Mitchell’s volley was tipped over and from the resulting corner Lerma leapt highest and the ball squirmed through the legs of Matz Sels and just over the line. Replays suggested that Lerma’s effort grazed the arm of team-mate Khalaili on its way in, but VAR let the matter go.

One characteristic Sage has inherited is his team’s difficulty in defending set pieces and Palace were lucky to escape when a header from Gibbs-White at the start of the second half was deflected on to the post by Mitchell. Forest looked at sixes and sevens at the other end when Lerma again caused chaos from a corner but they scrambled the ball away.

There was no such reprieve a few minutes later when Quinten Timber’s pass was diverted into the path of Strand Larsen and Pino made no mistake with the rebound. The Spain forward then turned provider but Strand Larsen could not find a way past Sels. That didn’t stop the Palace fans from gleefully asking Glasner what the score was. Ndoye and Neco Williams had chances to make things interesting late on but Forest – and Glasner – had been humbled by then.

Sports.title: Mohamed Belloumi grabs point for Hull in seesaw draw with Everton
Sports.content:
Hull retained their unbeaten home record since returning to the Premier League with an entertaining draw against Everton at the MKM Stadium.

Brennan Johnson found the net in the 34th minute but was denied a first Premier League goal for Everton following a video assistant referee check, leaving the sides to go in goalless at the break. The hosts wasted little time after the interval, however, as Joe Gelhardt opened the scoring in the 48th minute following an error by Ainsley Maitland-Niles.

Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall equalised for Everton seven minutes later, and Thierno Barry, who had squandered plenty of earlier chances, then put the visitors ahead midway through the second period. Hull responded swiftly, though, with the substitute Mohamed Belloumi pulling the home team level in the 74th minute.

The Tigers have returned to the top flight with an unexpected bang, tasting defeat for the first time in their final fixture before the international break at Newcastle. They were slow off the mark in the early exchanges here, but eventually produced a forward burst of play that saw both Oli McBurnie and then Lewie Coyle threaten before being thwarted.

Gelhardt caused danger with a run down the right in the 22nd minute but his shot was comfortably collected by Jordan Pickford. Matt Crooks got his head to a corner 10 minutes later, but James Tarkowski cleared and play sped to the opposite end.

Barry unleashed a shot that was gathered by Konstantinos Tzolakis, but the ball rolled from his hands and was fired in by Johnson for what appeared to be the opener 11 minutes before half-time. But, after a lengthy VAR check, the winger was ruled offside. Gelhardt and Nobel Mendy then went close to easing the nerves of home fans with near-misses before half-time.

The hosts did not have to wait long for the opener after the break though. Sorba Thomas capitalised on a mistake from Maitland-Niles and fed Gelhardt, who coolly nudged the ball beyond Pickford in the 48th minute.

The Everton response was fairly rapid, however, and Maitland-Niles atoned for his slip-up by finding Dewsbury-Hall, who headed home in the 55th minute.

View image in fullscreen Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall heads home to make it 1-1. Photograph: Lee Parker/CameraSport/Getty Images

Barry, who had much to ponder after missing two earlier chances, then redeemed himself when he pounced to lash beyond Tzolakis to put the visitors ahead for the first time in the match.

But Hull, who had made a handful of changes, were not behind for long as the substitutes Elliot Stroud and Belloumi linked up and the latter sent a left-footed shot past Pickford in the 74th minute to secure a point for the Tigers.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

David Moyes felt his Everton squad completely underperformed. Change is afoot at the club after it was announced earlier in the week they would be put up for sale, but their manager was in no mood for excuses after the draw.

He said: “I’m really disappointed that we didn’t come away with three points, I couldn’t see them getting a goal when we went 2-1 up – I thought if anything we would go on and finish it. It looked really unlike us, the way we gave the goals away today, it was very, very poor.

“Hull have had some great results here, against Manchester United and Villa, they’re not easy to beat and they weren’t [today] but I thought we should have gone on and won the game comfortably.

“The overall performance from everyone was so far below our level, way below where we should be. I’m not giving the players any room for excuses because of what’s going on, whether that be the transfer window or that be ownership.”

Sports.title: European football: Freiburg move top of Bundesliga while Isco keeps Betis flying high
Sports.content:
Ten-man Freiburg scored an 85th-minute winner ⁠through Keisuke Goto to snatch a 2-1 home victory over ⁠Schalke 04 ⁠on ​Sunday and move top of the Bundesliga.

Freiburg, who had ⁠already made a club-record start with 10 points from their opening ⁠four matches, climbed to 13 points, ​ahead of Borussia ‌Dortmund on ‌goal difference. The champions, Bayern Munich, who drew 2-2 ‌against Augsburg on Saturday, are third on 11.

With Freiburg in control, Maximilian Eggestein put the hosts in front after 10 minutes, but Schalke hit ‌back through Adrian Gantenbein on the half-hour. Freiburg were reduced to ​10 men when Yuito Suzuki received a second yellow card in the 64th minute, seemingly handing Schalke the initiative.

But ⁠the visitors were far too passive and ​toothless ​in attack to ​make the extra man count ​and Freiburg ‌punished them ​five ​minutes before the end with the Japan international Goto snatching the winner with a glancing header.

Borussia Mönchengladbach remained rock bottom of the Bundesliga after a 2-1 defeat to local rivals Cologne on Sunday, in a match overshadowed by ugly scenes on the terraces.

The game was suspended for several minutes and riot police surrounded the away block after Gladbach fans appeared to fire fireworks into the home sections after Said El Mala’s superb second-half winner. That maintained pointless Gladbach’s miserable start to the season as the new coach, Alexander Blessin, failed to prevent the club falling to their fifth defeat in as many games.

The Real Betis playmaker Isco scored in each half ⁠as his side breezed to a 5-2 home win over Osasuna on ⁠Sunday that lifts ⁠them ​to third place in La Liga, five points behind the leaders, Barcelona, and one ahead ⁠of Real Madrid.

Isco fired home from the penalty spot in the 10th minute to ⁠open the scoring, and Abde Ezzalzouli added a second ​before the break after ‌Betis won the ‌ball high up the pitch and countered quickly.

Betis ‌looked to be set for a comfortable afternoon when Diego Llorente added a third three minutes after half-time, but two quick goals for the visitors from Ante Budimir and Raúl García reduced the ‌deficit to 3-2 in the 56th minute.

However, Isco eased their nerves again when he ​snapped up a loose ball in the box and rifled it home, and José Antonio Morante came off the bench in the 90th minute before scoring deep ⁠into stoppage time to leave Betis on 19 ​points after ​eight games.

Earlier on ​Sunday, Real Sociedad held off a spirited ​comeback from ‌Deportivo La Coruña ​to ​emerge with a 3-2 win at home, while struggling Elche grabbed a much-needed point by holding visitors Celta Vigo to a scoreless draw.

Lazio moved level on points with Inter at the top of Serie A with a 3-1 win over Monza on Sunday as 10-man Roma played out the first goalless draw of the Italian season at Como.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Nuno Tavares gives Lazio an early lead. Photograph: Riccardo Antimiani/EPA

Under Gennaro Gattuso, who has bounced back after his failure in charge of the Italian national side that missed out on the 2026 World Cup, Lazio continued their strong start to the season. Still unbeaten, the Roman side secured a fifth victory in six matches to pull level on 16 points with Inter, who beat Parma 3-0 at San Siro on Saturday.

Nuno Tavares gave Lazio a third-minute lead and Gustav Isaksen doubled it midway through the first half. Monza had Lorenzo Lucchesi sent off on 35 minutes for hauling down Tijjani Noslin as he broke through on goal, but the 16th-placed visitors rattled Lazio after the break, pulling a goal back and coming close to equalising before conceding a third goal in the closing stages.

Roma left Como frustrated. The dismissal of league top scorer Donyell Malen for a dangerous tackle early in the second half forced them to scale back their ambitions. Neither team could find the breakthrough in a clash between two sides widely regarded as dark horses for the title, leaving Inter and Lazio two points clear of Roma after their respective wins over Parma and Monza.

Bologna picked up their first win of the season by beating Lecce 2-1. Milan remain unbeaten in Serie A after drawing 1-1 with Sassuolo. Adrien Rabiot’s opener was cancelled out by Cas Odenthal as Milan settled for their third draw of the campaign and stay fifth in the table. Juventus are one point behind Milan after an 81st minute equaliser from Randal Kolo Muani salvaged a 1-1 draw with fourth-placed Cagliari.

Marseille put an end to their four-game losing run in Ligue 1 as Amine Harit and Himad Abdelli scored in a 2-0 win at Troyes. Struggling Marseille began the weekend in the relegation zone after suffering five losses in a row in all competitions, but a pair of second-half goals lifted them to 13th place.

Harit steered in a cross from Emerson Palmieri shortly after half-time before Abdelli converted a late penalty as Marseille avoided matching their worst losing streak over the past 40 years. Troyes had gone close to an equaliser just before Abdelli made the points safe for Marseille, but Renaud Ripart’s stoppage-time volley crashed against the post.

Rennes moved up to third earlier in the day with a 4-1 win against Auxerre, while Nice came from behind to beat Strasbourg 2-1.

Sports.title: Joy for Eckert as 10-man Southampton edge out Portsmouth in feisty derby
Sports.content:
At the full-time whistle in the south coast derby, Tonda Eckert thrust his arms out wide and roared into the sky with the rest of the Southampton supporters. It had been a tense 90 minutes after a tense few months, but finally the young German coach could let it all out. At the end of a week where he found out that he will face no immediate ban for his part in the Spygate scandal that rocked the Championship last season, he helped deliver Southampton’s first home win over Portsmouth for 22 years.

Southampton played more than half of a fiercely contested game with 10 men after Cameron Bragg was sent off for a second yellow card on 44 minutes and Eckert was keen to divert credit elsewhere at full time. “I think that one today belongs to the players,” he said. “If you go a man down there’s not so much you can do as a manager outside of trying to give a structure that helps. It’s the players that dig out games like this.”

There was widespread surprise at the leniency of the punishment that allowed Eckert to take his seat in the dugout for the derby. After Southampton admitted to spying on three opponents last season, the 33-year-old was handed a six-week ban, suspended until the end of the 2027-28 campaign, and a £28,000 fine for misconduct.

An FA independent disciplinary commission noted Eckert’s “genuine contrition” at what had happened. At Southampton, there is a sense that their expulsion from the playoffs in May and subsequent four-point deduction was punishment enough, and Eckert is keen to move on from a period of uncertainty that he admitted this week had changed his life.

This win was evidence of a club sticking together. James Bree was the author of the winning goal, turning the ball home after 20 minutes, but the pattern of the game shifted with Bragg’s dismissal. Southampton, united and resolute, held on to move into the top half – they would be third without the points deduction – with Eckert now able to contemplate another promotion push.

View image in fullscreen Southampton’s James Bree coolly opens the scoring, his goal turning out to be the winner. Photograph: Adam Davy/PA

Portsmouth were as usual given a pre-match police escort to St Mary’s and their full-back Jayden Meghoma, who made his professional debut for Southampton as a 17-year-old, was a magnet for Saints ire. He was a threat down the left, firing wide at the near post in a promising opening, but he lost Bree for the goal. Finn Azaz was given too much space in midfield and clipped a ball in behind a static Meghoma for Bree, forward from right-back, to guide a left-footed finish into the far corner.

Ebou Adams, who scored Portsmouth’s equaliser in a 1-1 draw in this fixture in January, was a central figure early on. He twice picked Bragg’s pocket in the Southampton half and drew yellow cards on both occasions. Bragg was consoled by his teammates after seeing red for an instinctive tug of Adams’s shirt after being caught on the ball.

The decision to start Bragg in a holding midfield role had backfired. “It will be a learning [curve] for him, but I asked him to be brave,” Eckert said. “I asked him to get on the ball and he does just that. I’ll take that on me, then.”

View image in fullscreen Cam Bragg is consoled as he walks off the pitch. Photograph: Robin Jones/Getty Images

Colby Bishop, whose header was well saved by Daniel Peretz, and Ryan Kavuma-McQueen, who drilled a shot just wide, went close to equalising before Eckert could try to plug the gaps at half-time.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The game was just as frantic after the break. Azaz was perhaps lucky not to be sent off for a wild lunge on Adams. When Bree was treated for a battle scar around his eye, Eckert held council with his remaining midfielders James Ward-Prowse and Flynn Downes as Pompey continued to knock on the door. The substitute Adrian Segecic was drifting into spaces and had fizzed a couple of low efforts wide in the minutes before, while the right-back Zak Swanson saw his cut-back cleared by Jack Stephens from under the Southampton crossbar.

View image in fullscreen Tempers fray at St Mary’s but the hosts held on for victory. Photograph: Warren Little/Getty Images

“It was a different game after the red card,” said the Portsmouth head coach, John Mousinho. “But for the amount of pressure that we had in the second half, the amount of opportunities we had, to not put the ball in the back of the net – we’re devastated.”

While Eckert gradually cut back his side’s attacking presence, Mousinho emptied his bench in an attempt to find a way through a Southampton defence marshalled by Stephens and Keven Schlotterbeck, who laid their bodies on the line more than once in front of Peretz. Their clean sheet was a priceless end to a week where their manager was given something of a clean slate.

Sports.title: Chelsea star Cole Palmer under fire as he 'can't even be bothered to say hello' to desperate young fans swarming him and his girlfriend as they walk home
Sports.content:
Chelsea star Cole Palmer under fire as he 'can't even be bothered to say hello' to desperate young fans swarming him and his girlfriend as they walk home

Cole Palmer has been criticised for blatantly ignoring young fans as he left Stamford Bridge following Chelsea's 5-1 win over Bournemouth on Saturday.

Palmer, 24, celebrated signing his new Blues deal with an impressive display against the Cherries, claiming an assist as Xabi Alonso's side ran riot to climb to sixth in the league.

Despite his sprightly performance, Palmer cut an apathetic and totally uninterested figure as he ignored swarms of young Chelsea fans rushing to greet him outside Stamford Bridge.

A video posted to social media on Sunday showed young supporters holding their phones up in an attempt to take a selfie with Chelsea's star man, who wore a hood and kept his hands firmly in his pockets as he and his girlfriend Olivia Holder briskly walked past.

Palmer's decision to flatly ignore the youngsters was met with widespread criticism on social media, as fans expressed their disappointment in him.

'Might risk the wrath of large sections of our fanbase here but Cole comes across as such an arrogant mug in the manner he completely ignored the kiddos screaming his name,' one fan posted.

Cole Palmer leaving Stamford Bridge after Chelsea beat Bournemouth 5-1



🎥 @charliepatrick0 pic.twitter.com/LuqBE5aIhB — londonwillalwaysbeblue (@ldnwillbeblue) October 10, 2026

Cole Palmer has come under fire for completely ignoring young fans after Chelsea's 5-1 win

Palmer was walking away from Chelsea's stadium with his girlfriend Olivia Holder

'If nothing else, showing them’ young fans a bit of tenderness wouldn’t do Palmer any harm whatsoever.'

A second person added: 'I get he wants to be private and all that but damn man, you couldn’t just stop for the kid begging for the signature?'

A third said: 'Getting paid £220,000 a week and you can’t stop for a few minutes to make a kids day?'

Another supporter chimed in and said: 'All this "if he has to stop for one kid, he has to stop for them all is rubbish". Sign the lad's shirt with the Palmer top on and a couple more then apologise to everyone else for not having time to sign them. Simple.'

On Saturday morning, just hours before Chelsea's clash with Bournemouth, Palmer announced his new deal on a mock Twitch livestream, which saw him respond to fake questions from 'fans'.

After signing a new long-term contract until 2034, the attacking midfielder appeared on a livestream to answer a series of generated questions, 'breaking the news' before Chelsea's official announcement.

Reading out the question 'How long are you staying at Chelsea then?', he responded: 'Well, I've just signed a new contract about 20 minutes ago.'

Palmer's decision to ignore the young fans was met with widespread criticism on social media

Just hours before Chelsea's victory over Bournemouth, Palmer announced his new Blues contract on a mock Twitch live stream, answering a series of generated questions

'So I'm staying for about eight more years. So hopefully you can sing that song a bit more that you all sing.'

Palmer had seven years left to run on his previous deal, but has agreed improved terms with the new contract extending his commitment by a further 12 months.

The 24-year-old also claimed the Blues are making progress and will be in contention to win major trophies.

'Chelsea means a lot to me and I think the club is going in the right direction, so I'm delighted to sign and I'm obviously very happy,' Palmer said.

'Speaking to the owners, to the sporting directors and obviously the manager, they gave me a lot of confidence so it was only right to sign.

'Speaking to players as well, everyone has the same ambitions. I feel like we can win major trophies here consistently and I want to be a part of that and play a big role in it too.'

The mock Twitch stream comes after Palmer was temporarily suspended from the platform last month after playing EA Sports FC 27 before the game's release, leading to the midfielder appealing for them to lift his ban.

Sports.title: It's time for Man United's undependable stars to show some backbone for Michael Carrick, writes CHRIS WHEELER - and why club chiefs will rue letting Casemiro go
Sports.content:
It's time for Man United's undependable stars to show some backbone for Michael Carrick, writes CHRIS WHEELER - and why club chiefs will rue letting Casemiro go

By the time Sandro Tonali’s cross reached Lisandro Martinez, he had his back to the ball. So distracted was the Manchester United defender in winning his wrestling match with Domnic Solanke that he had forgotten the most important thing of all.

Having outmuscled the smaller Martinez, the Tottenham striker got enough on his header to send it creeping inside Senne Lammens’ left-hand post as Spurs snatched an injury-time equaliser at Old Trafford.

It’s not like the Argentine hadn’t been warned either. At the start of the second half, he lost another one-sided grapple with Solanke who should have scored from close-range.

Three weeks’ earlier, in United’s previous game before the international break, Martinez was guilty of a hapless own-goal before Michael Carrick’s side scored a late equaliser of their own at Craven Cottage.

Martinez is by no means the only reason United have made their worst start at this stage of a league season in 40 years. Far from it. The problems at this club reach far and deep.

But he is typical of the senior players at United who, for one reason or another, are failing Carrick this season after helping their head coach get the job in the first place. The Dependables have now become, well, rather undependable.

Lisandro Martinez's performances are indicative of United's stars lacking fight for Carrick

Start in goal, where the previously unflappable Lammens appears to have lost his composure since returning from the World Cup, and work your way through this United team. It is littered with men in red playing within themselves.

Carrick insisted after Saturday’s 1-1 draw that he doesn’t feel let down by them, but he would not be the first United boss to pay the price for players who either cannot or will not stand up and be counted.

Ole Gunnar Solskajer used to privately confide to his coaching staff – including Carrick – that ‘this lot will get me sacked’ and very little seems to have changed despite the volume of managers and players who have passed through Old Trafford since then. Erik ten Hag failed to fix the ‘no good culture’ at the club and so did his successor Ruben Amorim.

Of course, Carrick must take his fair share of the blame as well. Losing to Manchester City after his opponents went down to 10 men a quarter of the way into the Old Trafford derby last month was bad enough. Conceding an injury-time equaliser to Tottenham after a winless team sitting bottom of the table had a man sent off was downright careless.

It raises questions about Carrick’s game management that cannot be masked by a shocking VAR call in City’s favour or Martinez losing his bearings against Spurs when it mattered most. Understandably questions are being asked over whether he is the right man for the job.

The United boss is suffering what undid his predecessors at Old Trafford

But there is only so much Carrick can control. Three weeks after his players were shamed by their running stats at Fulham, they failed to match Tottenham’s physicality and hunger for much of this game. Roberto De Zerbi may be worse off than Carrick on paper, but only one of them left Old Trafford on Saturday night with any cause for optimism.

This week, United travel to Atletico Madrid and Leeds. The Metropolitano and Elland Road are a test for even the most resilient of teams. In Martinez’s defence, he is exactly the kind of character you need for such assignments.

Carrick desperately needs the rest of his players to rise to the challenge in a way that has proved beyond them this season. It’s time for them to show some backbone. His job may depend on it.

Bring back Casemiro!

Another game, another moment for the United hierarchy to glance back at the transfer window and wonder if they should have done things differently.

Carlos Baleba made an encouraging debut off the bench in the draw with Tottenham, but it’s never a good look when your biggest summer signing isn’t fit to play until mid-October.

Elsewhere, Carrick started with centre-back Leny Yoro at right-back and right-winger Bryan Mbeumo at centre-forward in the continued absence of Benjamin Sesko. Mbeumo scored but only after reverting to the right flank when Joshua Zirkzee replaced Amad Diallo.

Who knows when Sesko will be available again, but United were well aware of the shin injury that has limited the Slovenian to just two starts since the beginning of May (including pre-season) and yet chose not to sign a striker when they were busy rebuilding their midfield.

Youri Tielemans looked well off the pace against Spurs and some will be questioning the decision to let Casemiro go

Of the players brought in, Baleba is almost ready for a first start, but Youri Tielemans looked well off the pace against Tottenham. The 29-year-old made way for his new teammate as one of three changes just before the hour mark.

And what of Andrey Santos? The Brazilian hasn’t started in the Premier League since the embarrassing opening-day defeat at Hull, and didn’t make it off the bench against Spurs even though, in theory, he would have been well suited to helping United defend a one-goal lead.

Is United’s midfield any better for all that wheeling and dealing in the summer? Bring back Casemiro!

How Spurs became United's bogey team

Nearly 40 years after Sir Alex Ferguson was parachuted into Old Trafford to salvage United’s season the last time the club’s first six games went any worse than this, he arrived at the old place on Saturday using a walking stick and with his left foot still in a protective boot.

Following the publication on Thursday of his latest book Games of My Life, United’s draw with Tottenham won’t even have been the best game Ferguson has seen this week.

Spurs used to be Ferguson’s home banker. He won 39 of 61 meetings with them in all competitions, a better record than against any other team.

‘Lads, it’s Tottenham,’ he famously said to his players before a game against the North Londoners, as if no other words were needed.

Given that United have now only won once in the last 10 matches between the two clubs – including the 2024-25 season when Spurs won the Europa League final and knocked them out of the Carabao Cup – the boot appears to be on the other foot.

Sports.title: England appoint new bowling coach who Ben Stokes named 'the best I've EVER worked with'
Sports.content:
England are set to name Eric Simons as the new bowling coach of the Test side – Stephen Fleming’s first appointment after replacing Brendon McCullum, and a man once described by Ben Stokes as the best bowling coach he had ever worked with.

The 64-year-old Simons coached his native South Africa for two years until 2004, and later spent two years as a bowling consultant to the Indian national side, before working more recently with the South Africans.

He has also worked at Chennai Super Kings in the IPL, where he worked closely with Fleming, before Fleming stepped down in July after 18 years with the franchise.

Simons, who played the last of his 23 one-day internationals in 1995, will take over bowling duties from New Zealander Tim Southee, while the ECB intend to update their Test-match backroom staff sometime this week.

His arrival will not affect Troy Cooley, the popular Australian who is the ECB’s elite national lead for pace bowling, and works across the whole of England’s performance programme.

Eric Simons (right) worked with South Africa at the 2023 World Cup

Simons earned rave reviews from Stokes, who worked with him at the Rising Pune Supergiant IPL franchise in 2017, and described him as ‘the best bowling coach I ever worked with’. Stokes added: ‘I probably learned more in two months with him than I did in 10 years before that.’

Simon’s first gig with as one of Fleming’s assistant coaches will be back in South Africa, whre England begin the first of three Tests, at Centurion, on December 17.

Those who know him speak highly of his technical expertise and the strong personal relationships he forges with individual bowlers.

Sports.title: 'Unwell' Lewis Hamilton taken to Singapore Grand Prix medical centre after gruelling night race in front of girlfriend Kim Kardashian
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton had to receive medical treatment after a torrid Singapore Grand Prix on Sunday.

The Ferrari driver was pictured crouched over in parc ferme with his head bowed moments after getting out of his car at the Marina Bay Circuit – where he fell from P3 to P6 following a disastrous race strategy.

It was then confirmed that the 41-year-old was taken to the medical centre, with the seven-time world champion excused to skip his obligatory post-race media duties.

Sky Sports' F1 presenter Simon Lazenby confirmed the situation trackside, saying: 'We were hoping to hear from Lewis Hamilton before we go, however, he got out of the car and he was feeling unwell so he has gone to the medical centre.

'He has been given dispensation not to go to the pen and face the world's media.'

Hamilton was watched on by girlfriend Kim Kardashian in Singapore, with the reality TV star, 45, telling Sky Sports' Martin Brundle she was 'praying' for a good result before the race.

Lewis Hamilton was taken to a medical centre at the Singapore Grand Prix after feeling unwell

Hamilton endured a difficult race on Sunday, where he was supported by girlfriend Kim Kardashian

Kardashian, who was criticised for snubbing Brundle during a 'rude' interaction at the Monaco Grand Prix, made amends with the legendary motorsport broadcaster.

'Did I not know the rules? Did we get off on the wrong foot?' she said as she jokingly placed her hand on his arm.

Of Formula One, she said: 'I think it's amazing and fun and wild and something I've never seen before. It's amazing.

'I'm just praying for the best tonight. Yes, [he is] very confident and so am I, just got to pray for the best.'

Hamilton's health compounded a difficult few hours for him as his bold decision to go against team orders backfired during the race.

Ferrari looked set to finish second and third on the podium with Hamilton's team-mate Charles Leclerc in the former position. However, Hamilton slipped from third to sixth in the closing stages of the race as his tyres faded away.

The iconic Italian outfit had requested Hamilton to pit to prevent that scenario but he disagreed and later apologised to his team over the radio after crossing the chequered flag.

'Sorry, boys. I let you down today with that strategy,' he said. 'My call, and I lost us valuable points. I'll try and make up for it in the next one.'

Team principal Frederic Vasseur said: 'Clearly we asked them to pit. Charles pitted. Lewis didn't want to pit because he... I don't know why. And then he realised it was the wrong call. It's why he apologised to the team.

'Now it's not a drama for me that he made the wrong call. I'm making mistakes, he's making mistakes, we're all making mistakes sometimes. Now we have to look ahead and make mistakes positively.'

Hamilton (right) dropped from third to sixth in the closing stages after ignoring orders to pit

SINGAPORE GP: TOP 10 1. Max Verstappen 2. Charles Leclerc 3. Kimi Antonelli 4. Lando Norris 5. Oscar Piastri 6. Lewis Hamilton 7. Liam Lawson 8. Nico Hulkenberg 9. George Russell 10. Isack Hadjar

After receiving medical treatment, Hamilton then released a statement explaining his reasons why he ignored the pleas to pit.

'Today wasn't the result we were looking for and it was on me,' said Hamilton. 'At a track that's difficult to overtake, you need to try something different and I chose to start on a new medium tyre, to go long and try to make a one-stop work. Unfortunately the medium didn't perform as well as the soft.

'I had a good second stint and the pace was back, but I couldn't make the progress I needed. Under the VSC, the team called me in but I missed the entry.

'After that, I decided to stay out and try to hold track position to the end but in the closing laps, I was struggling massively with tyre degradation and lost three places, finishing P6, which doesn't reflect the pace we had in the car today.

'A painful lesson today, but I take full responsibility for the decisions I made. Not every call will work out, and I can accept getting it wrong but I'm sorry for the team for the points we lost today. They put so much into every weekend, and I wanted to deliver more for them.

'I'll continue to put the work in and come back fighting at the next race.'

Sports.title: Teenage rider devastated after car crashes into her 'Olympic' horse Benny who had to be put down - dashing their Team GB hopes
Sports.content:
A talented teenage horsewoman's dreams are in tatters after a car crashed into her on a Cotswolds village lane – leaving her elite prizewinning horse dead.

Tinks Walker, 17, a great hope for British equestrian sports, went headfirst through the car's windscreen and came round to find her star gelding, Benny, dying in the road.

The accident shattered the youngster's hopes of selection for Great Britain in the Eventing European Championships for Young Riders next year.

Now her family want justice after Wiltshire Police decided not to prosecute the driver – despite concluding there was sufficient evidence.

The family have launched their own legal proceedings for the injuries to Tinks and for the value of 10-year-old Benny, said to be worth hundreds of thousands of pounds.

'He was the equine equivalent of an Olympian,' said Tinks, who has been riding horses since she was a toddler.

Tinks Walker and Benny riding together. He was a star horse who had previously been ridden by Olympic champion Laura Collett and was passed to Tinks to develop a new partnership

Tinks was devastated by the loss of Benny, the extraordinary eventing horse whom she described as her best friend

The 17-year-old, seen here with another horse, has been riding since she was a toddler and rises at 4am to fit in training with her A Level studies

On April 2 this year, Tinks took the thoroughbred, Killossery Kaptain - known as Benny - out for an early morning ride with Lily, a two-star event horse, being 'led' by them.

As they walked along a country lane about a mile from her family home, near Malmesbury, Wiltshire, she saw a car 'flying around the curve in the road ahead of me', she told police. She pulled Benny and Lily onto a grass verge but the approaching car did not slow down, she said. 'This made me panic...seeing the car barrelling directly towards me.

'I was on the grass, off the road. I thought to myself "has she seen me or not?". I felt totally powerless and the next thing was I felt an impact. I woke up on the floor. It felt like I had been beaten up.'

Her account to police continued: 'I saw Benny lying on the floor. Benny did try and get up once - but struggled to do so and ultimately fell back down to the floor. He did not try and stand up again.'

Benny was a four-star competition horse previously ridden by Team GB double Olympic gold medal winner Laura Collett, the current European Eventing Champion.

It had been decided to pass him to Tinks to develop a next-generation partnership for Team GB. The A Level pupil trained with him every day, often rising at 4am to fit in her studies.

Benny's injuries from the crash were so severe, he was put down at the roadside by a vet.

Tinks riding Benny at Tweseldown Horse Trials on March 15, 2026

Benny was 'the kindest horse you would ever come across', said Tinks's mother Netia Walker. The four-star eventing horse had to be euthanised at the scene of the accident

Prizewinner Benny with his previous owner, the double Olympic gold medal champion Laura Collett

Tinks told the Mail: 'It was awful. I was completely helpless. There was nothing I could do. Every day I've thought about it. When I close my eyes, I see it happening.

'Benny was my best friend. He taught me things that no other horse ever had. He taught me that making mistakes was okay.'

Tinks's mother, Netia Walker, added: 'He was the Brad Pitt of horses to us. He came here and was worshipped. He was the kindest horse you would ever come across. He would have been the most amazing horse for Tinks, and it is just horrific.

'My daughter could have been killed, we have lost her best horse and have another one that is so traumatised we can't ride her on the roads.'

After a five-month inquiry, Wiltshire Police wrote to Tinks and said that while 'there is sufficient evidence to bring a prosecution against the alleged offending driver', the woman had instead been offered a 'safe and considerate driving course' to 're-educate' her.

The decision has left the family furious. Now Tinks's solicitor Cathryn Godfrey, of Irwin Mitchell, has begun the process of suing the driver. Another solicitor, Hannah Bradley, of Aria Grace Law, is acting for the owners of Benny, one of whom is Tinks's grandmother. She is suing over the loss of the prizewinning thoroughbred, said by an independent equine valuer to have been worth hundreds of thousands of pounds.

Fi Rutland, the other co-owner of Benny, said: 'The accident has devastated all of us. I have lost my pride-and-joy, it has broken all our hearts, but more importantly it has shattered a talented young girl's dreams and aspirations. The courage she has shown is awe-inspiring.'

Meanwhile a friend of the driver told the Daily Mail she was very distressed by the terrible accident and was adamant she had been driving at low speed. A spokesman for the driver and her company, which owned the car, said: 'We are deeply saddened by the death of Benny following this tragic accident and our thoughts are with all those affected. The incident was a terrible accident, and our team are extremely distressed by what occurred. As this accident is the subject of legal action, it would not be appropriate to comment further at this stage.'

Tinks and her family are being supported by the British Horse Society which is campaigning for rural drivers to slow down – warning that horses are being killed on UK roads at an alarming rate.

As part of its Dead Slow campaign, it said there had been 560 horse fatalities on the roads over the past decade.

Alan Hiscox, the society's director of safety, said: 'Tinks is absolutely devastated at what happened to Benny and she is not alone. I've been to see five riders this year who lost horses on the roads. The biggest trauma is often the guilt of the rider because the horse took the impact and saved them from more serious injury.'

As Tinks focuses on her recovery, she is competing in a charity race at Newbury on November 5 to raise funds for the British Horse Society and help its safety campaign.

Tinks said: 'Nothing can bring back Benny, but if we can raise awareness to make other riders safer on the roads, then maybe some small, good thing can come from this horrible tragedy.'

Sports.title: Liverpool 0-3 Man City PLAYER RATINGS: Who always made the wrong decision in the big moments? Who will Andoni Iraola be demanding more from? And who could be City's main man but for pending punishments?
Sports.content:
Liverpool 0-3 Man City PLAYER RATINGS: Who always made the wrong decision in the big moments? Who will Andoni Iraola be demanding more from? And who could be City's main man but for pending punishments?

It was a game that had so much more to it than a football match. Liverpool fans brought cheating banners, City fans brought bananas to mock their charges – but, ultimately, the Premier League leaders brought their A-game.

Underneath all the off-field chaos, there was indeed a football match taking place. And it was a good one, until Ryan Gravenberch was sent off.

Liverpool went blow-for-blow with Enzo Maresca's City, whose future remains uncertain. 'Going down,' the Liverpool fans chanted – they may well be, but, for now, they are the league's best.

Gravenberch was given his marching orders in the 62nd minute, and Liverpool couldn't cope after. City upped the tempo, and scored three goals, celebrating as if nothing was going on off the field.

Erling Haaland, Jeremy Doku and Rayan Cherki were all on the scoresheet as City carried on their 100 per cent record. Liverpool, meanwhile, have two wins from their six games so far, and are ninth in the standings.

Daily Mail Sport's LEWIS STEELE was at Anfield to rate the players.

Erling Haaland (centre) was on the scoresheet as Manchester City beat Liverpool 3-0 at Anfield

LIVERPOOL (4-2-3-1)

Alisson – 6

Could do nothing about any of City’s goals. Had little to do beforehand but his presence put off Haaland at 0-0.

Ronald Araujo – 5

Played fine overall but Doku and Co gave him the run-around when they started to fly forward after the red card. Booked.

Jeremy Jacquet – 6

Made some fine interventions in the first-half and has been a strong addition to Liverpool’s team.

Virgil van Dijk – 5

Slow to react at times and none of Liverpool’s defenders could cope with City when they had the man advantage. Booked.

Milos Kerkez – 5

Made some powerful runs forward but struggled defensively, which happens all too often for the Hungary international.

Milos Kerkez (right) was good going forwards but once again struggled defensively

Ryan Gravenberch was having his best game this season until an unnecessary red card

Ryan Gravenberch – 6

Was enjoying his best afternoon of the season until he was sent off. The first yellow was harsh but the second was correct and he should have known better than to make the foul.

Alexis Mac Allister – 6

Like midfield partner Gravenberch, the Argentine had a couple of chances to score but had two shots that went inches wide.

Victor Munoz – 7

Liverpool’s best player and a constant nuisance. A rather unknown figure before he signed for the club, Munoz is outshining his big-money team-mates.

Florian Wirtz – 4

Another big game that has gone by without a meaningful moment from £116million Wirtz. Made the wrong decision in the big moments time and again.

Bradley Barcola – 5

Had one or two nice moments but Iraola will be demanding much more from the £123million signing. Has not got going in a red shirt yet.

Lewis Koumas – 7

Like a rash with relentless running, which Iraola will love. This was his first Premier League start and it will not be his last if he carries on impressing like this.

Lewis Koumas didn't stop running and will be enjoying plenty more Premier League minutes if he keeps that up

Manager

Andoni Iraola – 6

His team were well in the game until the red card which ended the contest. Might have done better if not for injuries, too.

Substitutes

Trey Nyoni (for Wirtz, 66) – 6

Jeremie Frimpong (for Araujo, 75) – 4

Rio Ngumoha (for Koumas, 75) – 5

Joe Gomez (for Jacquet, 88)

Federico Chiesa (for Barcola, 88)

MANCHESTER CITY (4-2-3-1)

Gianluigi Donnarumma – 7

Made two strong saves in the space of seconds during Liverpool’s best spell of the game. Commanding at claiming set-pieces.

Matheus Nunes – 7

Pocketed £123million man Barcola for the most part and seems an integral member of Maresca’s side.

Ruben Dias – 7

A captain’s performance from Dias, who could be seen giving mini team talks to his troops during the game.

Marc Guehi – 6

A few shaky moments early doors but settled and produced a confident display as ever.

Nico O’Reilly – 6

Munoz gave him a tough time but O’Reilly made some fine defensive interventions. Good running going the other way but his final ball was lacking. Booked.

Victor Munoz (right) have Nico O'Reilly a tough afternoon but the City man coped well overall

Enzo Fernandez – 7

A tenacious player who has breathed new life into City’s midfield that looked leggy at times last season.

Elliot Anderson – 9

An outstanding footballer who could be the main man for City for the next decade if it was not for pending punishments. Ran the game and seemed to be first to every loose ball.

Iliman Ndiaye – 6

Double trouble for the Senegal international, who was not just a rival player but also an ex-Evertonian. Struggled to affect the game.

Rayan Cherki – 8

Sensational goal and is one of the most exciting players in the Premier League, the sort that kids will want to emulate on the playground.

Antoine Semenyo – 7

Another bright light for City, Semenyo gave his old boss Iraola a few headaches down both wings.

Erling Haaland – 7

Barely noticeable but came up with the all-important moment that opened the scoring. How often does he do that?

Manager

Enzo Maresca – 8

Got his tactics spot on as City weathered the early storm and then started to thrive after the red card.

Enzo Maresca got his tactics spot on with his team excelling after Gravenberch's red card

Sports.title: Man City charges LIVE: Premier League punishment agreement as Liverpool response sent
Sports.content:
Roy Keane has suggested he would be ‘disgusted’ if he was a Manchester City player following their landmark verdict.

The ex-Manchester United captain has absolved the club’s stars of any blame but noted that they should feel particularly let down by City’s behaviour.

Speaking on Sunday, he said: “This is nothing against the players or supporters, this is an ownership issue. If you’re going after the big prizes, we’ve been fortunate to pick one or two up. You want to do it honestly.

“You want to look back at your career and think we did everything. You win some games, you lose some games.

“You can’t be looking back at what Man City have done and found guilty of, I know there’s an appeal. We’ve been sitting here and praising Man City and saying they’re amazing and bringing in amazing players. And Pep turning really good players into superstars.

“But the way they were doing it, that’s the issue, nothing on the players. If I was a player and there were stories about stuff we were doing at Manchester United, I’d be disgusted. I’d be disgusted if there were any dodgy dealings and anyone cooking the books

"Some people think this is a bit strong, but I wouldn't feel like I've earned a league title if there was something dodgy going on in the background. Absolutely not.

“We talk about lads going out and giving their all and picking up injuries but that is your job, that’s what you’re supposed to do when you’re giving it your all.

"You just hope everyone is else is on the same page and being honest and everyone else is trying to do it the proper way.

“I hear a lot of ex-players saying that Man City players gave it their all, we know that. That’s not the issue. But they had unbelievable players on the bench to come on and make them stronger and get them over the line against teams like Liverpool who are pushing each other."

Sports.title: F1 news: Lewis Hamilton taken for medical checks as Sky Sports issue apology
Sports.content:
F1 news: Lewis Hamilton taken for medical checks as Sky Sports issue apology

Max Verstappen produced a dominant victory in Singapore but there was drama with Lewis Hamilton

View 3 Images Lewis Hamilton became unwell in Singapore (Image: Kym Illman/Getty Images)

Max Verstappen claimed his second straight victory at the Singapore Grand Prix but there looks to be no catching Kimi Antonelli at the top of the drivers' world championship. Verstappen has closed the gap further on Lewis Hamilton and George Russell in the overall standings but the trio are playing for minor honours.

‌



‌



Antonelli secured third place at the Marina Bay Street Circuit, which means he is now mathematically just one win away from his first-ever world title. The 20-year-old sits on 340 points and could win the championship at the United States Grand Prix - but only if he wins and his teammate Russell finishes in 10th place or lower.

‌



Mercedes are also sitting top of the constructors' championship, 134 points clear of their nearest rivals, Ferrari. Another double title win could be on the cards but Antonelli is not allowing the potential of a championship cloud his judgement heading into the next Grand Prix.

‌



Speaking post-race, the Italian racer said: "For sure, but at the same time, I know it's very close, I know it's there, but I just need to make sure that I keep doing the best I can. You know, the mindset is always the same, to go out there and win and perform the best way I can. I think this weekend I haven't particularly driven that well.

"I felt like I could have done a better job, but I feel confident that, you know, a week to reset and I'm really looking forward to being back in Austin. But at the end of the day, if I don't do my job well, then the result won't come. So in order to achieve what I want, I need to perform, as simple as that."

Lewis Hamilton update

Hamilton skipped his media duties on Sunday after falling unwell in the paddock after the Singapore GP. The Ferrari star was shipped off to the medical bay after being spotted crouching and staring at the floor after climbing out of his car.

View 3 Images Hamilton ended up in the medical bay post-race (Image: Mark Sutton - Formula 1/Formula 1 via Getty Images)
