The Houthis claimed responsibility for all four strikes on Saudi airports before Sunday’s attack, which has yet to be claimed by any group.

Alvarez, who has held multiple world titles across several weight classes, will face WBC super-middleweight champion M’billi in a highly anticipated bout.

“Canelo reached out ⁠⁠and told me he’ll still fight in Riyadh this October, no matter what happens,” Al-Sheikh, chairman of Saudi Arabia’s General Entertainment Authority, wrote in a social media post. “He [Alvarez] fears nothing.”

The ‌‌Mexican boxer, a former two-time undisputed super-middleweight champion, has not fought since he was ‌‌beaten ‌‌by American Terence Crawford in September 2025.

World.title: If Netanyahu goes, does anything really change for Palestinians?
World.content:
Analysts say opposition victory in October 27 polls may bring only marginal change and no fundamental shift on Gaza or West Bank.

Share If Netanyahu goes, does anything really change for Palestinians? on social media

Four rival Israeli political movements have agreed to work together in a bid to unseat Israel’s longest serving prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu.

The factions – the Yashar party, the Democrats, the Yisrael Beytenu party and the Together alliance – span different parts of Israel’s political spectrum but say they are united in their goal to “preserve and strengthen Israel as a Jewish and democratic state”.

The opposition grouping is in a close battle with a pro-Netanyahu coalition heading into the October 27 elections, recent polling indicated, although neither side appeared on track to win a parliamentary majority.

The election comes as Israel faces a series of domestic crises that are tearing at its social fabric, including questions over political accountability for alleged corruption and security failures, disputes over ultra-Orthodox military service and efforts to exclude Arab parties from political life. The country also faces growing backlash abroad, including from allies, over its continuing attacks on Gaza and Lebanon as well as settlements, which are illegal under international law, and settler pogroms in the occupied West Bank.

Analysts said the combination makes the upcoming elections among the most consequential in Israel’s history but even an opposition victory may bring only marginal change for Palestinians suffering record levels of settler violence and mass displacement. While the opposition alliance has taken Netanyahu to task personally, there is little daylight between them when it comes to Israel’s foundational policies in Gaza and the West Bank.



“Palestinians should not expect a fundamental change in Israeli policy if the Netanyahu bloc loses power,” said analyst Samer Jaber, a doctoral researcher specialising in political economy at Royal Holloway, University of London.

“The major political blocs share core positions on the Palestinian question, including support for the existing settlement structure, while the state institutions that formulate and implement policy would remain unchanged,” he added.

What is the anti-Netanyahu coalition?

The leaders of the four major Jewish-led opposition movements gathered on September 26 and signed a declaration promising not to attack each other in the run-up to the elections and to collaborate in forming a government after the vote.

In addition to Yair Lapid, who leads the official opposition in Israel’s Knesset, the meeting included Gadi Eisenkot, who heads the Yashar party; Naftali Bennett, who leads the Together alliance, cofounded by Lapid; Avigdor Lieberman, who heads Yisrael Beiteinu; and Yair Golan, who leads the Democrats. The declaration does not set out an official leader although Eisenkot is viewed as the opposition’s most likely candidate for prime minister. In a joint statement, the figures said defeating the current government was their “shared highest objective”.

Of the four opposition parties, Yashar is projected to be the strongest. A recent poll by Israel’s Channel 12 suggested Yashar would win 23 seats in parliament, the most of any party and more than the 21 seats projected for Netanyahu’s Likud.

Trailing is the Together alliance, projected to win 13 seats, followed by Yisrael Beiteinu and the Democrats, each projected to win nine.

That would give the opposition a combined 54 seats in the 120-seat Knesset, seven short of a majority. Netanyahu’s alliance, which includes several ultra-Orthodox and far-right parties, is projected to win 49 seats.

Arab-led parties, representing the Palestinian citizens of Israel, who make up about 20 percent of the population, are projected to win 13 seats, but most leaders of the Jewish-led opposition bloc have ruled out joining forces with them.

Roi Zur, an assistant professor at the University of Essex who leads a research project on Israeli parties’ political ideology and policy, said the anti-Netanyahu coalition has a chance to win if turnout is on its side, noting that several parties that do not “strictly oppose” the prime minister could fall below the 3.25 percent threshold to enter the Knesset, shaking up the balance.



“If these parties waste enough right-wing votes, the opposition might translate their support into power,” Zur told Al Jazeera. “But this might not be enough.”

Even if the opposition alliance manages to find a way to oust Netanyahu, it would likely be weak and incapable – or unwilling – to overhaul Israeli policy in the West Bank and Gaza, analysts said.

“An anti-Netanyahu government will most likely be a very disparate coalition with a very thin majority, if any, in the Knesset. That would make it difficult for such a government to agree on any substantial perceived concessions, such as withdrawing completely from Gaza,” Anders Persson, a political scientist specialising in the Israel-Palestine conflict, told Al Jazeera.

“It would also make it difficult for the international community to meaningfully pressure such a government because there will always be a fear that an anti-Netanyahu government could quickly collapse.”

‘Mostly right-wing’

While their positions vary, most leaders of the anti-Netanyahu alliance have taken hardline positions on Gaza and the West Bank that give Palestinians little reason for optimism.

Yashar’s Eisenkot, a former Israeli military chief, has called the idea of a Palestinian state “delusional”, and he supports “strengthening” Israeli settlements. However, he opposes full Israeli annexation of the West Bank and has said he would dismantle smaller Israeli outposts not approved by the Israeli government. He also opposes the current government’s E1 settlement plan, which in effect would cut the West Bank in two. On Gaza, Eisenkot supports pursuing a United States-backed peace plan but only from a place of “strength” and only after “Hamas’s total disarmament”.

Israeli attacks across Gaza since the start of a “ceasefire” in October last year have killed nearly 1,500 Palestinians, bringing the overall death toll since the start of Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza in October 2023 to more than 74,000, according to the enclave’s health officials.

Bennett, a former Likud member who served in multiple Netanyahu-led governments, has described himself as “more right-wing” than Netanyahu and advocated exceptionally draconian policies in Gaza, including once calling for a “shoot-to-kill” policy against Palestinians trying to cross into Israel. Bennett staunchly opposes a Palestinian state and supports settlement expansion although he has criticised Israeli settler pogroms against Palestinians. With respect to the future of Gaza, he wants Israeli forces to stay in the enclave until Hamas is disarmed and proposes that Egypt, rather than Turkiye or Qatar, should play a future security role.

Lieberman’s Yisrael Beytenu party also supports settlement expansion, including the E1 plan. He backs annexing all of Area C of the West Bank – which constitutes 60 percent of the territory and is already under full Israeli control – while transferring control of other parts of the territory to Jordan. On Gaza, his party wants Israel to retain “freedom of action”, cut off water and electricity and eventually transfer governance to “an agreed-upon international entity”.



Golan’s Democrats party is the only one to support a form of two-state solution although it frames it as “responsible separation” that includes the “full demilitarisation” of the Palestinian state and complete Israeli security control of the Jordan Valley and other key areas. His party also supports complete demilitarisation for Gaza and a reconstruction process that involves regional states.

Palestinian lawyer and analyst Diana Buttu said each of the opposition leaders “has supported Israel’s genocide in Gaza” while backing settlements or not believing in full “equality for Palestinians”.

This orientation reflects hardening views within Israeli society itself.

According to a September Pew Research Center poll, only 17 percent of Israeli respondents said peaceful coexistence alongside an independent Palestinian state is possible. And according to an August survey by the Jewish People Policy Institute, 38 percent of Jewish Israeli participants favoured annexing the entire West Bank and more than half supported retaining the settlements as part of any future agreement on a Palestinian state.

‘Lessen the harms’

Nevertheless, some analysts said a new government could roll back or slow down some of the most “controversial and radical steps” of Israel’s current government, which includes far-right settlement proponents Itamar Ben-Gvir, the minister of national security, and Bezalel Smotrich, the minister of finance. Smotrich last month said Israel should “go to war” in the West Bank and repeat what it “did in Gaza”.

Changes enacted by a new government would likely include suspending the E1 settlement project and cracking down “on extremist settler violence/terrorism in the West Bank”, said Dov Waxman, a professor of political science at the University of California, Los Angeles, who specialises in Israeli politics and the Israel-Palestine conflict.

A new government would also be expected to “allow more humanitarian aid to enter Gaza in a more predictable, consistent manner and for reconstruction to finally begin there”, he added.

Ehab Jabareen, a Palestinian political analyst and researcher in Israel, told Al Jazeera that a new government led by Netanyahu’s opponents would likely be “more receptive to US and international pressure”, giving more space for potential reconstruction in Gaza.

But overall, Jabareen said, such a government is unlikely to alter Israel’s overarching “paradigm” towards Palestinians. “I would expect the difference to be less about whether Israel maintains control over the Palestinians and more about how the control is exercised, legitimised and managed,” he said.

Amjad Iraqi, senior analyst for Israel and Palestine at the International Crisis Group, said any “shades of difference” would be meaningful for Palestinians who are currently “suffering nearly uninhibited brutality”.

“We’re at a point of mitigation,” Iraqi told Al Jazeera. “It is about trying to lessen the harms. Palestinians are not in a position to expect any kind of radical shift, but every life saved, every piece of land saved matters a lot for people on the ground.”

World.title: Zelensky backs Trump's 'energy ceasefire' but says Russia continues to hit power plants
World.content:
Donald Trump has claimed that Russia and Ukraine have agreed to an "energy ceasefire", with Kyiv saying it would support such a move but Moscow yet to comment.

The US president insisted that it was "effective immediately" but provided no details.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky initially expressed surprise at the announcement, before saying Kyiv would support it if Moscow did. He also accused Russia of striking Ukrainian energy facilities after Trump's post.

Trump has been urging Ukraine to stop strikes on Russian oil infrastructure - which Kyiv says are vital to curtailing revenue for Moscow's war machine - so Russia can fulfil a recently-struck deal to release diesel to the US and the global market.

The diesel deal, temporarily undoing sanctions on Russian imports, is attracting growing criticism. Zelensky called it a gift to Russian President Vladimir Putin. European officials and some US politicians, including from Trump's Republican party, have said they do not support it.

The deal is Trump's latest effort to lower domestic fuel prices ahead of the midterm elections, having spent months grappling with the political consequences of the war with Iran which has pushed up global fuel prices, particularly those for diesel.

That has soured Trump's standing with the American public, who have been stung by the higher pump prices and knock-on effects that led to across-the-board inflation.

World.title: Documents falsified to evade tax on Abramovich's wealth, BBC finds
World.content:
The world's biggest accountancy firm helped in falsifying documents to hide Roman Abramovich's wealth and evade tax, BBC Panorama has found.

Accounts signed off by Deloitte in Cyprus meant assets such as superyachts, mansions and private jets worth $672m (Â£508m) vanished from Abramovich's company accounts.

Deloitte also appears to have advised on a scheme to evade a huge tax bill on the oligarch's wealth through the falsification of documents.

Barrister Andrew Mitchell KC, an expert in financial services law, said Panorama's evidence showed the scheme was "straightforward" tax evasion and "it couldn't be more blatant".

Roman Abramovich's lawyers said he denies that he evaded tax or concealed his fortune. They said Panorama provided no evidence he knew about, authorised or directed the falsification of any document and said it was legitimate to rely on advice from professionals.

Deloitte Cyprus said it "acts in compliance with applicable laws".

The findings are being revealed following a joint investigation between BBC Panorama and the Bureau of Investigative Journalism.

For nearly two decades, Roman Abramovich was the most famous Russian oligarch in the UK, welcomed in London where he bought Chelsea Football Club in 2003 and bankrolled the club's most successful period. But after Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, he was sanctioned by the UK government as an associate of President Vladimir Putin and forced to sell the club.

Abramovich has been reported to be living in Turkey, a safe haven for him because it did not apply sanctions. In the Channel Island of Jersey, Â£5.4bn of his assets remain frozen and a criminal investigation has been going on for four years.

The oligarch's lawyers told the BBC he denies the allegations in the Jersey investigation and says it was "undertaken for political purposes".

Our investigation has uncovered new evidence about the way Abramovich's business empire has been run. It also raises serious questions about the integrity of some of his professional advisers.

World.title: Trump faces growing backlash over plans to import diesel from Russia
World.content:
US President Donald Trump is facing a growing backlash over plans to import diesel from Russia as the Iran war continues to impact global energy prices.

Trump on Friday announced that Russian President Vladimir Putin had agreed to release 300,000 tonnes of diesel immediately "to the American and global marketplace" followed by several other shipments.

That is despite signing legislation to authorise fresh US sanctions and tariffs on nations that import Russian oil and gas just weeks ago.

The move has been criticised by some Republican and Democratic lawmakers, who believe the deal violates US laws.

As well as the initial release of 300,000 tonnes of diesel, Trump said Russia would then supply 500,000 tonnes in November and one million more after that.

This would be followed by a further three million tonnes, which would be delivered "within a short period" dependent on the condition of its refineries, which have been attacked by Ukraine during the ongoing war between the two countries.

"Lower prices for Americans, especially our Great Farmers, Ranchers, and Truckers, is my Greatest Priority," Trump wrote in a Truth Social post.

Russia's Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak confirmed these numbers to Tass, the country's state-owned news agency, saying the export volume could reach three million tonnes per month in future.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has called the deal a gift to Putin that amounts to "an investment in a war that must be ended".

It is understood the US Treasury is suspending sanctions on Russian diesel exports until 7 April as part of the deal, but other assets like those in American banks are still frozen.

A group of seven senators - four Republicans and three Democrats â on Sunday said the deal violated US laws, urging Trump to "reverse course".

"The United States should not provide Putin with a financial lifeline while Russia continues to kill Ukrainian civilians," the lawmakers said.

They added that Congress had "explicitly banned Russian energy imports in 2022 to prevent American dollars from financing Putin's brutal war against Ukraine".

The statement was signed by Republicans Susan Collins, Lisa Murkowski, Thom Tillis and John Curtis, as well as Democrats Jeanne Shaheen, Richard Blumenthal and Ron Wyden.

World.title: One killed, 11 injured in second Houthi strike on Riyadh airport in two days
World.content:
One person has been killed and 11 injured in a second strike on the international airport in the Saudi capital Riyadh, officials have said.

A Saudi military spokesman said a projectile had hit King Khalid International Airport on Sunday, causing a fire in a passenger hall. Saudi Arabia's civil aviation authority said in a statement on X that one person, a Pakistani resident, had been killed in the attack.

It comes a day after a strike on the same airport killed 13 people and injured 308 others. There have been a series of other attacks earlier in the week.

The Houthis in Yemen said they were behind them and warned airlines and passengers against using Saudi Arabian airports and airspace.

The group said they had targeted the airport with a mix of ballistic and cruise missiles, as well as drones in the past 24 hours.

They also attacked oil facilities and Dammam airport in eastern Saudi Arabia, their military spokesman Brig Gen Yahya Saree said.

He vowed to continue the "escalating operations deep inside Saudi Arabia", warning that all Saudi airports were potential targets apart from those in the holy cities of Mecca and Medina.

The Houthis have said they are targeting Saudi Arabia over its support for government forces in Yemen's civil war, as well as an air strike on the airport in Sanaa.

On Sunday Maj Gen Turki al-Maliki, spokesman for the Saudi-led military coalition, said air defences had intercepted a missile near the airport in Riyadh, while authorities were dealing with the fire caused by an "unknown projectile" that hit Passenger Hall No 4.

US President Donald Trump has said the US would "make a decision" and "move very quickly" on whether to strike the Houthis, while UK Defence Secretary Wes Streeting suggested the UK could "potentially" provide more support for Saudi Arabia.

World.title: American ranchers wrestle with soaring costs - and their loyalty to Trump
World.content:
Nebraska rancher Yvette Mannon was already having a rough year.

In April, a wildfire destroyed 1,600 grazing acres and 13 miles (21 km) of fence along the ranch she bought in 2002. The ranch is nestled in a corner of Nebraska that's home to rolling green hills under sweeping Midwestern skies, the landscape dotted with grain silos and feedlots alongside fields and fields of bovines.

Mannon's 300 cattle survived the blaze - but the fencing needed to be replaced, and the herd still needed to be fed.

With steel prices at their highest levels in years, heavily affected by tariffs imposed by US President Donald Trump, that meant spending $4.89 a foot - for a total exceeding $300,000.

On top of that, because so much good grazing land had been destroyed, Mannon also needed a tractor out every day delivering hay to her cattle - at a time when diesel prices, spiking due to the Iran War, were up more than 40% from the previous year.

Then in August, the Trump administration announced it would import 300,000 metric tons of duty-free foreign beef in a bid to lower consumer prices. The news hit right before the September-November window when most US calves are weaned and sold.

The cattle market tanked immediately.

World.title: Poland detains man suspected of planning assassination of PM Tusk
World.content:
Poland's Prime Minister Donald Tusk said a man accused of plotting an assassination attack against him and his defence minister has been detained.

The interior ministry earlier reported that police had received credible information about possible attacks against Tusk and Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz.

Polish security services convened a special meeting on Sunday after receiving information about the planned attacks, with a spokesman saying officials were treating the threat as "deadly serious".

Tusk thanked the police for "swift and decisive action" in arresting the suspect.

The suspect was arrested in the Lower Silesia region and was a Polish national, Jacek Dobrzynski, a spokesman for the Special Services Co-ordinator told local media.

"In this case we are talking about a strong likelihood that these threats could actually be carried out," he said.

The plan was uncovered when an email with information about the potential attack was forwarded to police by the State Protection Service, which is responsible for ministers' security, Interior Ministry spokeswoman Karolina Galecka said.

Tusk has been Polish prime minister since 2023, having previously held the office from 2007 to 2014.

He served as president of the European Council from 2014 to 2019.

World.title: Watch: Endangered orangutans released back into the wild after Borneo fires
World.content:
Eight orangutans have been released into the wild in Borneo after being rescued from intense wildfires.

Three mothers, their three daughters and two adult males were freed in a reserve in the west of the island on Friday.

Indonesian wildlife authorities rescued 46 of the apes, which are critically endangered, before fires tore through their habitat in August and September.

Read more on this story.

World.title: Dozens of gold prospectors killed in strikes on Egypt-Sudan border, rights group says
World.content:
At least 72 civilians who had been prospecting for gold in a border region of Sudan have been killed in air strikes, a regional rights group says.

Emergency Lawyers, based in the Sudanese capital, Khartoum, said jets targeted the so-called artisanal miners at a popular gold mining sites on Saturday.

Neither the Egyptian government nor the de facto Sudanese authorities have so far commented.

Cairo has previously faced accusations of deadly strikes on gold prospectors as part of a crackdown on illicit activity along its southern border.

Emergency Lawyers noted the previous alleged attacks and said they represented not only a violation of Sudan's sovereign territory but demonstrated the government's lack of control over the region.

"The deliberate targeting of unarmed civilians violates international humanitarian law and the right to life," it said in a statement on Sunday. "These acts may constitute war crimes."

It noted that its death toll was provisional and could rise.

The Paris-based Sudan Tribune reported that the death toll could far exceed the number reported by Emergency Lawyers, citing a survivor of Saturday's attack who said many more people had been injured.

Eyewitnesses said the attack began around 06:00 local time (04:00 GMT), with the aircraft firing more than five missiles directly at the miners' camps, destroying them and excavation pits with people still inside, the newspaper wrote.

The Sudan Tribune reported claims in June that Egyptian forces had used drones and artillery to target artisanal mining sites in the same region, killing several, after sporadic incidents of Egyptian border guards of burning equipment, torching temporary shelters, and firing live ammunition to disperse mine workers.

Days later, Egypt's border agency announced that it and the military had begun a sweeping security campaign along the border to foil illegal migration, drug smuggling and illegal mining.

At the same time, Sudan's de facto leader announced an investigation into the alleged strikes, which were said to have killed dozens.

Gold lies at the core of the border tensions.

Sudan's ongoing civil war has led to a surge in artisanal mining - an often risky practice conducted by civilians with rudimentary tools and without official permission - particularly in remote areas near its borders.

Gold-rich areas lie along porous borders in terrain historically associated with cross-border smuggling routes, with artisanally mined gold potentially feeding into those channels.

Egypt's border force said in June that it had seized 86 tonnes of gold ore along with amateur prospecting equipment.

Artisanal mining has also reportedly continued in Sudan's conflict zones and smuggled gold may be a source of income for armed insurgent groups.

This has raised concerns of illicit Sudanese gold undermining the legitimate Egyptian gold market.

World.title: Kwara public hospitals introduce digital medical records
World.content:
State government-owned hospitals in Kwara State are introducing electronic medical records (EMR) to strengthen health information management and modernise public healthcare delivery in the state.

The Executive Secretary of the KW-HMB, Abdulraheem Malik, disclosed this to PREMIUM TIMES in Ilorin, the state capital.

He said the initiative, being implemented through KW-HMB under the HOPE-PHC Project, will see healthcare workers begin training on the system in November.

The digital healthcare programme is expected to reduce reliance on paper-based medical records, improve access to patients’ medical histories and promote continuity of care across public hospitals in the state.

The system is also designed to strengthen administrative efficiency and support evidence-based decision-making in hospital management.

The rollout builds on an earlier hospital digitalisation pilot involving six hospitals and the state government’s ongoing efforts to integrate digital solutions into healthcare service delivery.

The initiative also complements the board’s efforts to strengthen health information management, including the inauguration of its Data Management Committee in August 2026.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The KW-HMB boss, Mr Malik, commended Governor AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq for approving the initiative, describing it as an important milestone in the state’s drive towards a more efficient, accountable and technology-driven public healthcare system.

READ ALSO: 30 children rescued from illegal orphanage in Kwara

Mr Malik said the adoption of electronic medical records would strengthen hospital operations, improve patient information management and support more efficient clinical encounters across the state.

He reaffirmed the board’s commitment to working with relevant stakeholders to ensure the successful implementation of the programme and deliver more responsive, efficient and patient-centred healthcare services to residents.

The staff training scheduled for November is expected to equip healthcare personnel with the skills required to operate the system effectively.

When fully implemented, the initiative is expected to improve the management of patients’ health information and support better coordination of care across Kwara State’s public hospitals.

World.title: Tinubu hails World Bank’s update on Nigeria, vows to expand targeted cash transfers
World.content:
President Bola Tinubu has applauded the latest World Bank’s Nigeria Development Update, noting that the findings are a testament to the fact that the country’s economic reforms are bearing fruit.

In a statement by Bayo Onanuga, his special adviser on information and strategy, on Sunday, Mr Tinubu said the update shows his administration’s reforms have put the economy on a sound footing for sustained growth.

Since taking office in 2023, Mr Tinubu has pursued an array of reforms aimed at speeding up economic growth in Africa’s most populous country.

Those reforms include removal of costly fuel subsidies, unification of exchange rates, revamp of the nation’s tax system and recapitalisation of the banking and insurance sectors.

In the report issued last Thursday, the World Bank observed that the economy expanded by 4.2 per cent in the first half of 2026, up from 3.9 per cent in the same period of last year, despite the sweeping impact of the Middle East crisis.

It projected the country’s growth to average at least 4.4 per cent this year through 2028.

The World Bank expects inflation, which fell from 27.6 per cent in January 2025 to 15.2 per cent in December 2025, to ease to about 12 per cent by 2028.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Nigeria’s current account surplus rose to $12 billion or 7 per cent of GDP in the first half of 2026, up from $8.6 billion a year earlier, while gross external reserves advanced from $45.5 billion at the end of 2025 to $53.8 billion at the end of August 2026.

The report stated that the reforms have helped raise the federation revenue by 69 per cent in real terms between 2023 and 2025, with states as the largest beneficiaries.

It also noted that Nigeria’s internally generated revenue grew in real terms in 31 of 35 states, with 21 states cutting back their debt-to-GDP ratio between 2021 and 2025. It expects Nigeria’s overall public debt to fall from 40 per cent of GDP in 2025 to 38.1 per cent in 2026.

Mr Tinubu said states used the additional resources to increase capital spending by 151 per cent in real terms over the same period, while much of the increase went to roads and other transport, agriculture, energy and housing.

He added that 29 states shifted their spending towards economic infrastructure, while real social spending per person rose in all but one state.

“These findings confirm that the difficult but necessary decisions to remove the petrol subsidy, unify the foreign exchange market and strengthen fiscal discipline have raised revenues, stabilised the economy and created fiscal space for every tier of government to invest in its people,” Mr Tinubu said.

He vowed that his administration will work more to ensure that the reforms fully translate into better living standards for every Nigerian household, starting with lower food prices and decent jobs for young people.

“We will continue to expand targeted cash transfers, which have already reached more than 10 million households. We will accelerate the deployment of CNG, raise agricultural productivity, and improve access to affordable healthcare and quality education, so that the prosperity being created is shared by all,” he said.

He further urged state governments to deploy their increased revenues more prudently and prioritise projects that improve the health, education and living standards of Nigerians.

World.title: 2027: Lawmakers, former police boss, army general line up for Nasarawa governorship race
World.content:
The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has cleared 13 candidates for the 2027 governorship election in Nasarawa State.

Based on the impressive backgrounds and credentials of the contestants, Nasarawa will have one of the most experienced fields nationwide in the February 2027 elections.

Among the 13 candidates are serving and former lawmakers, a former inspector-general of police, and a retired army general.

They are all seeking to succeed Governor Abdullahi Sule of the APC, who is serving his final term.

The candidates’ political parties include the All Progressives Congress (APC), Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), Labour Party (LP), African Democratic Congress (ADC) and the Social Democratic Party (SDP).

Aliyu Wadada, a serving senator and the APC candidate, and Emmanuel Ombugadu of the PDP are among the prominent faces in the race.

Mohammed Adamu, a former inspector-general of police contesting on the SDP platform, and retired Major-General Nuhu Angbazo of the ADC will also be on the ballot.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The candidates have different political backgrounds, ranging from legislative experience to military and police service, business and community engagement.

The major contenders

Wadada, 61, is the APC candidate and represents Nasarawa West Senatorial District in the Senate. He previously served in the House of Representatives, representing the Keffi/Karu/Kokona Federal Constituency.

His candidacy places an experienced federal lawmaker at the centre of the APC’s effort to retain control of Nasarawa State.

Mr Ombugadu, 48, the PDP candidate, is a former member of the House of Representatives, where he represented the Akwanga/Nasarawa Eggon/Wamba Federal Constituency.

He is a familiar figure in the state’s opposition politics and has previously contested the governorship election.

Adamu, 65, the SDP candidate, is a former inspector-general of police.

His background in policing distinguishes him from several other candidates, although his experience in security administration will be only one of the factors voters may consider in assessing his suitability for the office.

Angbazo, 59, is the ADC candidate and a retired major-general of the Nigerian Army. His military career and links to the Eggon community form part of his public profile.

Gaza Gbefwi, 51, is the Labour Party candidate. He represents the Karu/Keffi/Kokona Federal Constituency in the House of Representatives and is seeking to move from federal legislative politics to the state’s executive leadership.

Full list of candidates

The 13 candidates published by INEC, arranged alphabetically by party, are:

ADC — Nuhu Angbazo (59)

ADP — Christopher Mamman (64)

APC — Aliyu Ahmed Wadada (61)

APGA — Ibrahim Kasimu Aboh (61)

APM — Onawo Mohammed Ogoshi (74)

APP — Dahiru Musa Doma (59)

LP — Gaza Jonathan Gbefwi (51)

NRM — Khalid Muhammad (55)

PDP — Emmanuel David Ombugadu (48)

PRP — Abdullahi Omame Abisabo (35)

SDP — Mohammed Abubakar Adamu (65)

YPP — Kigbu Tanko John (61)

ZLP — Giza Abubakar Abdu (69)

Abisabo, 35, is the youngest candidate on the list, while Ogoshi, 74, is the oldest.

The field brings together candidates with different levels of political and public-service experience.

However, their inclusion on the ballot does not, by itself, indicate their electoral strength or prospects.

The campaigns offer voters across the state’s 13 local government areas an opportunity to assess the candidates’ records, policy proposals and plans for addressing the state’s development challenges.

Issues such as security, infrastructure, employment, education, healthcare and economic development are likely to be central to public scrutiny of the candidates.

The final list is part of INEC’s preparations for the 2027 general elections, scheduled to include the governorship contest in Nasarawa State.

World.title: Why I defend persecuted Christians in Nigeria — Nicki Minaj
World.content:
American rapper Nicki Minaj has revealed that her connection to Nigeria through her pastor and reports of religious violence influenced her decision to speak out against the alleged persecution of Christians in the country.

The rapper made the remarks during an X Takeover event at Tesla’s Giga Texas facility in Austin, Texas. A video of her speech went viral on Monday.

The 43-year-old said the accounts of violence against Christians, especially in Nigeria, deeply troubled her.

“For Nigeria personally, my pastor is from Nigeria, so I have a link to Nigeria because of him. And of course, I have a lot of Nigerian barbs, but what I started seeing was the brutality with which Christians are being treated there just for being Christian”, said Minaj.

More advocacy

According to the rapper, her advocacy is driven by concerns about freedom of religion and the safety of Christian communities.

Minaj encouraged fellow entertainers and influencers to speak out and help raise awareness of what she called the brutal treatment of Christians in Nigeria.

The “Super Bass” crooner added that many public figures avoid discussing difficult or politically charged matters because they don’t see such conversations as trendy.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

She noted, “And I thought, why isn’t anyone making a big deal out of this, you know? And sometimes when things aren’t cool to talk about, people don’t talk about it.

“So right now, actually, I’m hoping that more celebrities or people, influencers, I’m hoping that they come aboard the train to start speaking out about what’s happening to Christians in Nigeria. And I look forward to doing more to help in that way, in that cause.”

Backstory

PREMIUM TIMES earlier reported that Minaj had stepped up her advocacy against religious persecution and violence since the US government designated Nigeria a Country of Particular Concern in November 2025 over allegations of Christian genocide.

The rapper has since used her social media platforms to call for an end to the persecution of Christians, insisting that they deserve freedom of worship in every country.

The mother of one also called for an end to bloodshed worldwide.

“Shed not their blood anymore. All Nations hear this. Shed not their blood; you have shed the blood of those that called you my name. #FreeChristians,” she wrote.

In November 2025, US President Donald Trump designated Nigeria a Country of Particular Concern over allegations of Christian genocide and threatened military action if the alleged killings continued.

World.title: 2027: INEC lists 19 candidates for Taraba governorship election
World.content:
The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has listed 19 candidates for the 6 February 2027 governorship election in Taraba State, with incumbent Governor Agbu Kefas and former senator Emmanuel Bwacha among the prominent contenders.

The list names Mr Kefas as the candidate of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Mr Bwacha as the flagbearer of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), and former senator Abubakar Tutare as the candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC).

The commission’s document contains the names of the candidates and their running mates, as well as their ages, genders and educational qualifications.

The 19 candidates represent different political parties, including the Labour Party (LP), New Nigeria Peoples Party (NNPP), Social Democratic Party (SDP), All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA) and Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC).

Kefas, Bwacha switch political platforms

Mr Kefas won the 2023 governorship election on the PDP platform before defecting to the APC. Mr Bwacha, who contested that election as the APC candidate, now holds the PDP flag.

Their change of platforms has reshaped the contest, placing the incumbent and his party’s former candidate on opposing sides.

In the 2023 election, Mr Kefas polled 257,926 votes, against 202,277 for Muhammad Yahaya of the NNPP. Mr Bwacha polled 142,502 votes to finish third.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Mr Yahaya is now the candidate of the NDC, providing another familiar name in the race.

Mr Kefas is seeking another mandate, while his challengers will be seeking to present themselves as better alternatives to his administration.

Full list of governorship candidates

INEC’s final document lists the following candidates and their running mates:

Accord (A): Jerome Nyameh; running mate, Ali Tanimu. African Action Congress (AAC): Gago Bulus; running mate, Sokira Salihu Njeke. African Democratic Congress (ADC): Abubakar Tutare; running mate, Kwetishe Haruna Kwenyan. Action Democratic Party (ADP): Hamman Mustapha; running mate, Wesley Ekanah. All Progressives Congress (APC): Kefas Agbu; running mate, Ibrahim Abubakar. All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA): Shiddi Usman; running mate, Kawu Muhammad. Allied Peoples Movement (APM): Bawa Mohammed; running mate, Daren James. Action Peoples Party (APP): Henry Banti; running mate, Jamilu Aliyu. Boot Party (BP): Kabiru Bala; running mate, Nawukari Adams. Democratic Leadership Alliance (DLA): Aboki Stephen; running mate, Maryam Geda. Labour Party (LP): Nathan Sanda; running mate, Foku Gaddas. Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC): Yahaya Sani; running mate, Susana Kona. National Democratic Party (NDP): Nuhu Atta; running mate, Abubakar Bitako. New Nigeria Peoples Party (NNPP): Uba Abdullahi; running mate, Emmaunel Luka. Peoples Democratic Party (PDP): Bwacha Emmanuel; running mate, Zakari Aminu. Peoples Redemption Party (PRP): Josiah Wasa; running mate, Hamman Abubakar. Social Democratic Party (SDP): Yusuf Ali; running mate, Nathan Danladi. Young Progressives Party (YPP): Sa’ad Abubakar; running mate, Abdul’alim Umar. Zenith Labour Party (ZLP): Bello Adamu; running mate, Yakubu Nuhu.

Issues for the election

The candidates will be contesting for leadership of a state where infrastructure, agriculture, employment, education, healthcare, security and public finance remain important governance concerns.

For Mr Kefas, the election will provide an opportunity to defend his administration’s record since taking office in 2023.

ALSO READ: PDP affirms Emmanuel Bwacha as Taraba governorship candidate

The opposition candidates, meanwhile, will need to present proposals explaining how they would address the state’s development challenges.

Mr Bwacha has criticised the Kefas administration over infrastructure, economic management and transparency.

Such claims, alongside the administration’s record and responses, will require scrutiny against budget documents, project records, audited accounts and evidence of public service delivery.

The candidates will also need to explain how their proposed programmes would be funded and implemented, rather than relying solely on campaign promises and political endorsements.

The publication of the final list provides voters with an official reference for identifying the candidates and their running mates ahead of the election.

INEC has scheduled the governorship election for 6 February 2027 in 28 states.

World.title: 2027: 17 in Plateau governorship race as NDC ticket faces court challenge
World.content:
Governor Caleb Mutfwang of the All Progressives Congress (APC) and Kefas Ropshik of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) are among the leading contestants in Plateau State’s 2027 governorship race, following the publication of candidates’ particulars by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC).

The commission’s published document contains the names of the candidates and their running mates, alongside their declared ages, genders and educational qualifications, ahead of the election scheduled for 6 February 2027.

Governor Mutfwang defected from the PDP to the APC in January 2026, leaving his former party to seek a new path back to the seat.

The election is also taking shape amid internal disputes within opposition parties, including a legal challenge to the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC)’s nomination.

Mutfwang seeks re-election under APC

Mr Mutfwang, 61, is the APC governorship candidate, with Josephine Piyo, 70, his running mate.

He won the 2023 governorship election on the PDP platform before defecting to the APC in January 2026, a move that reshaped the state’s political alignments ahead of the next election.

The governor’s decision to seek another term under the APC places his record in office at the centre of the campaign.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

His administration will face questions about security, infrastructure, employment, healthcare, education and the management of public resources.

Insecurity remains one of Plateau’s most pressing challenges, with repeated attacks on communities, killings and displacement disrupting livelihoods and raising concerns about the protection of lives and property.

Candidates will be expected to explain how they intend to improve early-warning systems, protect vulnerable communities, strengthen security responses and support residents whose livelihoods have been affected by violence.

Mr Mutfwang will also have to explain his political realignment to voters who elected him on the PDP platform in 2023.

INEC lists his declared qualifications as a primary education certificate, General Certificate of Education and an LLB degree with honours. The commission records a primary education certificate, General Certificate of Education and training at the School of Nursing in Jos for Ms Piyo.

Ropshik leads PDP’s challenge

Mr Ropshik, 50, is the PDP candidate, with Daniel Kim, 61, his running mate.

PREMIUM TIMES reported in May that a faction backed by the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, conducted a primary that produced Mr Ropshik, while the other faction led by Tanimu Turaki nominated Sunday Biggs.

The competing nominations reflected the party’s internal divisions.

Mr Ropshik’s candidacy gives the PDP an opportunity to challenge the incumbent, but the party’s prospects will depend in part on its ability to organise an effective campaign and present a coherent alternative to the APC administration.

The opposition party will need to articulate clear proposals on security, economic development, employment, agriculture and public services, while addressing concerns arising from its internal disputes.

INEC lists Mr Ropshik’s declared qualifications as a first school-leaving certificate and senior secondary school certificate.

For Mr Kim, the commission records a first school-leaving certificate, Grade II teacher’s certificate and Bachelor of Education qualification.

NDC nomination dispute

Jonathan Akuns, 64, appears in the INEC document as the NDC candidate, with Jonathan Pwajok, 56, as his running mate.

His nomination has been challenged by Alfred Dapal, also known as Alfred Damiyal, amid disagreements between the party’s national leadership and its state chapter.

PREMIUM TIMES reported in September that Mr Akuns emerged unopposed at the party’s 29 May primary and was recognised by its national leadership. However, the state chapter subsequently backed Mr Dapal in a separate nomination exercise.

The dispute escalated to the Federal High Court in Jos.

On 28 September, Justice S. T. Ishaya restrained Mr Akuns from presenting himself as the NDC candidate pending the hearing and determination of a suit challenging the nomination process.

The court also restrained the NDC and INEC from taking steps that would undermine the reliefs sought in the suit.

The order was not a final determination of the dispute.

The dispute raises questions about whether the party can resolve its internal differences before the election.

Other parties

INEC’s published document also lists candidates from several other parties, including the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Labour Party (LP), African Action Congress (AAC), Action Democratic Party (ADP), All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA), Allied Peoples Movement (APM), Action Peoples Party (APP), Democratic Leadership Alliance (DLA), National Democratic Party (NDP), National Rescue Movement (NRM), Social Democratic Party (SDP), Young Progressives Party (YPP) and Zenith Labour Party (ZLP).

The candidates named in the document include Sura Sunday of the ADC, Ayuba Adams of the AAC, Dawop Sa’idu of the ADP, Jiga Jarzuka of APGA, Danauta Kyarshik Samuel of the APM, Muhammad Hadi of the APP, Yusuf Umar of the DLA, Nura Tanko of the Labour Party, Yohanna Yilpan of the NDP, Cosmas Jarlath of the NRM, Dafup Simput of the SDP, Jonathan Dogara of the YPP and Bingel Hurung Philomina of the ZLP.

The commission’s document provides the declared ages and educational qualifications of these candidates and their running mates.

However, further independently verified information is needed to establish their professional histories, previous political offices, policy positions and records in public service.

Those details would help voters assess the candidates beyond their party affiliations and credentials submitted to INEC.

Security, governance likely to dominate campaign

The governorship election will take place against the background of Plateau’s prolonged security challenges and public demand for improved governance.

The candidates will be expected to explain how they intend to protect communities, prevent attacks, improve relations between residents and security agencies, and support displaced people and affected businesses.

Economic opportunities are also likely to feature prominently, particularly employment, agriculture, small businesses, education and healthcare.

Beyond broad promises, voters will need specific proposals, implementation timelines and credible explanations of how the plans will be financed.

The incumbent’s record will be scrutinised, while opposition candidates will be expected to demonstrate how their proposed policies differ from the current administration’s approach.

The election will also test the ability of political parties to manage internal disputes and comply with electoral requirements.

The NDC’s court challenge illustrates how unresolved nomination disagreements can complicate preparations for the ballot.

INEC must also clarify the discrepancy between the number of candidate tickets in its downloadable Plateau document and the total reported in its final-list coverage. An authoritative clarification would help prevent confusion among voters and political parties.

As the election approaches, the key questions for Plateau voters will extend beyond party labels: how the candidates intend to address insecurity, improve public services, create economic opportunities and ensure transparent use of public funds.

World.title: Delta records highest oil spill as nine incidents release nearly 130,000 litres of crude
World.content:
At least 129,855 litres of crude oil spilled in nine incidents across Delta, Bayelsa and Rivers states between August and September 2026, with Delta accounting for nearly 90 per cent of the total, according to official oil spill records reviewed by PREMIUM TIMES.

The records published by the National Oil Spill Detection and Response Agency (NOSDRA) show that seven incidents occurred in Delta State, one in Bayelsa and another in Rivers. The largest spill involved more than 112,000 litres of crude oil from a wellhead in Ughelli South Local Government Area of Delta.

The incidents, which occurred between 2 August and 17 September, were attributed to sabotage and oil theft, equipment failure, corrosion, and operational or maintenance errors.

The figures show the persistence of oil pollution in the Niger Delta, where spills continue to threaten land, vegetation, surface water, fishing grounds and aquatic life.

Delta accounts for most of the spilled crude

The largest incident occurred on 26 August at the W14T wellhead in Okpare-Olomu, Ughelli South Local Government Area, where ND Western spilled an estimated 704.5 barrels, equivalent to approximately 112,016 litres of crude oil.

NOSDRA attributed the incident to operational or maintenance error. The spill affected soil and vegetation on land within the company’s right of way.

The records indicate that 440.25 barrels (approximately 70,000 litres) were recovered, leaving 264.25 barrels (equivalent to 42,000 litres) unaccounted for in the reported figures.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The volume released in this single incident was more than eight times the 14,000 litres estimated to have spilled from a pipeline in Bayelsa State during the same period.

Delta also recorded a 1,590-litre spill from Renaissance Africa Energy Company Limited’s six-inch North Bank flowline at Obotobo in Burutu Local Government Area on 15 August. The incident was attributed to sabotage or oil theft. It affected vegetation, surface water and soil, both within and outside the operator’s right of way.

On 4 August, NNPC Exploration & Production Limited reported an equipment-related spill involving 1,110 litres at the Egwa Well 23 Tango in Egwa 2 community, Warri South-West Local Government Area.

The incident affected swamp vegetation, fishing nets, surface water and aquatic life. The joint investigation team reported seeing dead fish floating in the affected area.

Another incident involving six barrels, equivalent to approximately 954 litres, occurred on 17 September at the Heritage Energy Operational Services Limited‘s Olomoro Compressor Station in Isoko South Local Government Area. The spill, attributed to equipment failure, affected surface water and a fish pond, with the incident extending within and outside the company’s right of way.

Two further incidents occurred at Yokri in Burutu Local Government Area. A 159-litre spill from Renaissance’s six-inch Yokri high-pressure bulkline on 27 August was attributed to sabotage or theft, while a 40-litre spill still from Renaissance’s bulkline tie-in on 2 September was blamed on corrosion. Both incidents affected swamp vegetation or soil, with the first also affecting surface water.

The remaining incident in Delta involved approximately one litre of crude oil from Chevron‘s 9B-83 well flowline at Olero RMP 17 in Warri North Local Government Area on 22 August. NOSDRA attributed it to corrosion and reported an impact on surface water.

Bayelsa pipeline spill raises pollution concerns

Bayelsa State recorded the second-largest spill, with an estimated 88 barrels, equivalent to approximately 14,000 litres, released from a 10-inch Diebu Creek-Nun River delivery line at Eniwari in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area.

The incident, reported on 23 August, was attributed to sabotage or oil theft. The joint investigation team observed an inward dent and a tear on the facility, suspected to have resulted from the use of an improvised explosive device by unidentified persons.

The spill affected an estimated 1.62 million square metres of swamp habitat, according to the records.

Renaissance identified as the operator in the records, reported recovering 30 barrels, or approximately 4,770 litres, of crude oil.

The reported recovery leaves about 58 barrels, equivalent to approximately 9,200 litres, unaccounted for in the available figures.

In Rivers State, Oando reported a one-litre crude oil spill on 2 August from the 18-inch Ebocha-Ogoda pipeline at Mgbede community in Ogba/Egbema/Ndoni Local Government Area.

The incident was attributed to sabotage or theft. Investigators identified a two-inch ball valve attached to the pipeline at its 12 o’clock position. The records listed no initial containment measure.

Pattern mirrors previous oil spill reports

The latest figures follow a similar pattern documented by PREMIUM TIMES in its review of July 2026 oil spill records.

In a report published on 10 August, this newspaper found that at least 10 spill incidents occurred across Rivers, Delta, Bayelsa and Imo states during July. The incidents involved sabotage, corrosion, equipment defects and operational failures, with Renaissance Africa Energy Company recording four incidents.

The review for July also documented spills affecting swamp vegetation, surface water and fishing nets, including incidents in which oil escaped both within and outside operators’ rights of way.

In a separate investigation published in August 2025, PREMIUM TIMES reported that NOSDRA’s records documented more than 9,890 oil spill incidents across Nigeria between 2015 and July 2025. Rivers State recorded the highest number, with 4,184 incidents, followed by Bayelsa with 2,118.

The investigation found that sabotage was the predominant recorded cause of spills, while corrosion and equipment failures also contributed significantly to the pollution burden.

The latest records show that the problem is not limited to deliberate interference with oil infrastructure. The largest spill in the period reviewed was attributed to operational or maintenance error, while equipment failure and corrosion accounted for other incidents.

The environmental consequences were also not confined to land. Several spills affected swamps and surface water, while the Egwa incident in Delta was reported to have killed fish and damaged fishing nets, directly threatening the livelihoods of people who depend on the affected waters.

The records provide estimates of the quantities spilled and recovered, but do not, by themselves, establish the full extent of long-term environmental damage, the cost of remediation or whether affected communities have been compensated.

World.title: NPA to fix rail, logistics gaps at inland dry ports
World.content:
The Nigerian Ports Authority (NPA) has moved to address rail connectivity and logistics challenges affecting inland dry ports as part of efforts to integrate the facilities into the nation’s port system and improve cargo movement across the country.

The move followed a meeting between the NPA management, led by its Managing Director, Abubakar Dantsoho, and the Executive Director of Dala Inland Dry Port, Ahmad Rabiu, alongside representatives of Funtua Inland Dry Port, at the authority’s corporate headquarters in Marina, Lagos.

The engagement came after the Minister of Marine and Blue Economy, Adegboyega Oyetola, directed the transfer of operational oversight of inland dry ports to the NPA.

The discussions focused on strengthening institutional collaboration, addressing infrastructure constraints and improving operational efficiency across Nigeria’s maritime logistics chain.

Speaking during the meeting, Mr Dantsoho stressed the need to upgrade inland dry port infrastructure and technical capacity to complement ongoing modernisation efforts at the nation’s seaports.

He said the facilities must be equipped to handle increasing cargo volumes and support the broader transformation of Nigeria’s maritime sector.

“For our Inland Dry Ports to function at the same velocity as the ongoing modernisation across our seaports, we must proactively upgrade dry port infrastructure and technical capacity,” Mr Dantsoho said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He explained that the integration of digital platforms, including the Port Community System (PCS) and the National Single Window, into seaport operations must be matched by corresponding improvements at inland dry ports.

“As we integrate digital systems such as the Port Community System (PCS) and the National Single Window in our seaports, the dry ports must deploy modern equipment and advanced technical capabilities to handle larger cargo volumes and bigger vessels coming to our coast,” he added.

Increased private-sector investment

The NPA managing director also called for increased private-sector investment in inland dry port infrastructure, noting that stronger investment would be critical to improving cargo handling capacity and operational efficiency.

He cited APM Terminals’ establishment of an Export Processing Terminal in Northern Nigeria as an example of private-sector participation in the development of inland logistics infrastructure.

Mr Dantsoho assured stakeholders that efforts to optimise the inland port system were underway and confirmed plans to visit the Dala and Funtua facilities to assess their operational conditions and infrastructure requirements.

Operational oversight

Speaking on behalf of the delegation, Hassan Bello welcomed the transfer of operational oversight to the NPA, expressing appreciation for what he described as a seamless transition.

Mr Bello referenced the gazetted Port Act, which recognises inland dry ports as official ports of origin and destination, while drawing attention to challenges confronting the facilities, particularly inadequate rail connectivity and broader logistics constraints.

Rail access is a critical component of inland dry port operations, as efficient connections to the national rail network can facilitate cargo movement between seaports and inland destinations, potentially reducing pressure on road transport and lowering logistics costs.

The meeting also established a framework for further technical consultations, infrastructure integration and physical planning to identify the requirements for improving operations at the facilities.

The discussions highlighted the need for detailed technical assessments, stakeholder coordination and physical inspections to establish infrastructure priorities and guide subsequent project development.

The planned visits to Dala and Funtua inland dry ports are expected to provide NPA with a clearer understanding of the facilities’ operational challenges and the interventions required to strengthen their roles in cargo distribution, trade facilitation and wider maritime logistics network.

World.title: Just in: Makinde’s chief of staff resigns
World.content:
… Defection to APC likely – Source

By Adeola Badru

The Chief of Staff to the Oyo State Governor, Seyi Makinde, Segun Ogunwuyi, resigned from the government.

Ogunwuyi resigned on Monday, October 12, 2026, becoming one of several aides to have left the Makinde administration in the last two months, a development that has drawn attention to the political undercurrents within the Oyo State Government as the 2027 general elections approach.

His resignation has fuelled speculation about a possible political realignment towards the All Progressives Congress (APC), amid internal wranglings within the governor’s political camp, sources familiar with the developments have said.

A source familiar with the political developments in Oyo State told our correspondent that Ogunwuyi’s resignation could be linked to internal wranglings within the governor’s political camp, amid speculation that he might be considering a move to the APC.

“There have been internal disagreements within the political camp, and Ogunwuyi’s resignation has further fuelled speculation about possible realignments ahead of the 2027 elections.”

“There are suggestions that he could be considering joining the APC, but we cannot say that definitively at this stage,” the source said.

Although Ogunwuyi did not disclose his reasons for leaving the government in his resignation letter, sources familiar with the situation suggested that internal political disagreements could be connected to the latest departure. There was, however, no official confirmation that he had decided to join the APC.

In his resignation letter dated 12 October 2026, Ogunwuyi said his decision took effect immediately, while expressing gratitude to Makinde for the opportunity to serve in the administration.

“I respectfully write to resign my appointment as Chief of Staff to the Governor of Oyo State, with effect from today, 12th October, 2026,” he wrote.

Describing his time in government as fulfilling, the former Chief of Staff said he was proud of the administration’s achievements and remained confident in the state’s continued progress.

“Serving the Government and the good people of Oyo State has been a great honour. It has been deeply fulfilling to be part of the exceptional team that has worked relentlessly to deliver the remarkable achievements of this administration,” the letter read.

Ogunwuyi added that he remained proud of the collective accomplishments of the administration in advancing the state’s development.

“I remain immensely proud of what we have collectively accomplished in advancing the growth, development and prosperity of our dear State. As I take this decision, I do so with profound gratitude for the opportunity to serve, with confidence in the continued progress of Oyo State,” he stated.

He concluded the letter by reaffirming his loyalty to the state and the country.

“Please accept, Your Excellency, the assurances of my highest esteem and unwavering loyalty to Oyo State and the Federal Republic of Nigeria,” he wrote.

Ogunwuyi, a former member of the Oyo State House of Assembly and the House of Representatives, has occupied a prominent position in Makinde’s administration as Chief of Staff.

His departure came amid a series of resignations by political appointees in recent weeks, raising questions about the implications for the governor’s political camp ahead of the 2027 elections.

While speculation continues over Ogunwuyi’s next political move, particularly the possibility of joining the APC, neither he nor the governor’s office has publicly confirmed such a plan.

World.title: Iran ‘deeply concerned’ over escalation between Houthis, Saudi Arabia
World.content:
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi

Iran said Monday it was “deeply concerned” by escalating attacks between Yemen’s Tehran-backed Houthis and Saudi Arabia, after 14 people died in two days of strikes on Riyadh’s airport.

“We are deeply concerned about the developments taking place in the Arabian Peninsula,” foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei told a weekly press conference, adding that Tehran was ready “to help facilitate dialogue between the parties”.

A Houthi strike on Riyadh’s international airport on Sunday killed one person and wounded 11 others, a day after 13 died in the deadliest strike on Saudi soil in more than a decade.

“We absolutely do not want hostilities and war to continue between two Islamic countries,” Baqaei said, urging the parties to resolve the situation “through dialogue and engagement”.

The Houthis are part of the Iran-backed “Axis of Resistance”, a network of groups opposed to Israel that also includes Lebanon’s Hezbollah and Iraqi Shiite armed groups.

AFP

World.title: JAMB warns candidates against accepting admission outside CAPS
World.content:
The Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board (JAMB) has cautioned candidates against accepting admission offers outside its Central Admissions Processing System (CAPS), warning that such offers may not be recognised as valid.

The board issued the warning in a post on X on Monday, advising prospective students to verify their admission status on CAPS before accepting any offer.

“An admission offered by an institution outside the approved JAMB admission process may not be recognised as valid.

“Accepting such an offer could put your academic journey at risk and create complications with your admission records and related processes,” the board said.

JAMB gave the warning while promoting an episode of its JAMB Explained series, which examines what constitutes illegal admission, the consequences and how candidates can protect themselves.

“Your admission journey deserves the right foundation. Verify before you accept,” the board added.

According to information on JAMB’s official website, CAPS was developed to automate admission into tertiary institutions.

The platform allows candidates to check their admission status and accept or reject provisional offers, while enabling institutions to process admissions through the approved system.

JAMB’s 2026 admission guidelines state that admission offers must be processed through the board and made available on its e-Facility platform.

“Any offer of admission from any tertiary institution without JAMB Admission Letter is illegal and is not recognized by the Board,” the guidelines state.

The guidelines also warn that candidates who accept admission outside CAPS do so at their own risk, adding that the board will neither recognise such admissions nor condone them.

World.title: Ukraine ‘will respond’ if Russia does not follow ‘energy ceasefire’ – Zelensky
World.content:
Zelensky

Ukraine’s leader Volodymyr Zelensky said on Monday that his country would retaliate if Moscow did not agree to the “energy ceasefire” that US President Donald Trump unilaterally announced at the weekend.

“If Russia does not agree to an energy ceasefire, we will respond,” Zelensky told the Warsaw Security Forum via videolink.

Trump sowed confusion when he announced an energy ceasefire between the two warring countries without providing details, sparking astonishment in Kyiv, silence from Moscow and support from Ukraine’s Western allies.

“We are waiting for the details of the conversation between the Americans and the Russians, and we are waiting to see what specific steps the Americans are ready to take,” Zelensky said.

Trump’s announcement on Sunday came two days after he declared a temporary easing of US sanctions on Russian diesel, prompting outrage by European allies and Kyiv, who said it would only embolden Russian President Vladimir Putin.

“If Russia wants us to stop our long-range strikes against its oil refineries and oil exports, then Russia must stop its strikes against our energy system and critical infrastructure and stop killing our people,” Zelensky said.

Trump has previously taken to his Truth Social account to announce truces or other arrangements before either Kyiv or Moscow confirmed them.

“An energy ceasefire and other steps to reduce escalation and guarantee security are truly needed here in reality, not just on Truth Social,” Zelensky said.

World.title: AI: World Bank, IMF warn of jobs crisis in Nigeria, others
World.content:
• AI threatens 40% of global jobs — IMF

• World Bank urges local solutions to create jobs

By Babajide Komolafe, Economy Editor, in Bangkok, Thailand

The International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank have warned that artificial intelligence (AI) could worsen the jobs crisis in Nigeria and other developing economies unless governments and businesses take urgent steps to prepare workers and deploy the technology to create employment.

IMF Managing Director, Kristalina Georgieva, gave the warning at the Small AI: More and Better Jobs event during the IMF-World Bank Annual Meetings in Bangkok, Thailand, describing AI as a “slow-moving tsunami”.

According to her, about 40 per cent of jobs globally could be augmented, downgraded or eliminated by AI, with the impact varying across economies and occupations.

Georgieva warned that the technology could disrupt labour markets, stressing the need for countries to understand its implications and equip workers with the skills required to adapt.

World Bank Group President Ajay Banga said the institution’s priority was to ensure that economic development translated into employment opportunities.

“The bank’s entire focus has to be on jobs,” Banga said, arguing that AI should be deployed to improve productivity and support job creation rather than simply replace workers.

He said affordable, practical AI applications could help “a school, an educator, a healthcare system, an agricultural system for small farmers to get to scale”.

Banga illustrated the potential with a farmer using a basic mobile phone to photograph a diseased crop and receive advice on treatment. The technology could also connect the farmer to seeds, fertiliser, credit, insurance and market information.

In healthcare, he said, AI-enabled tools could help frontline health workers assess cases and connect patients requiring specialist attention to appropriate services.

The approach, known as “Small AI”, focuses on applications adapted to local languages, infrastructure, needs and budgets, rather than relying exclusively on expensive, sophisticated AI systems.

The World Bank’s October 2026 Africa Economic Update identifies Nigeria, alongside Kenya and South Africa, as one of the continent’s leading centres of AI activity. However, it stresses that adoption remains at an early stage and that Africa’s immediate opportunity lies in adapting affordable AI solutions to local challenges.

The report identifies agriculture, education, healthcare, finance, logistics and public administration as sectors where AI could improve productivity.

It also warns that unreliable electricity, inadequate internet connectivity, limited digital skills and poor-quality data could constrain adoption.

For Nigeria, the challenge is to build these foundations and ensure AI becomes a tool for creating productive jobs, not deepening existing employment pressures.

World.title: LCCI proposes 20% petrol price cut in six months
World.content:
…Welcomes FG’s stabilisation plan, seeks lower energy, logistics costs

By Yinka Kolawole

The Lagos Chamber of Commerce and Industry (LCCI) has proposed a six-month petrol price reduction programme targeting a 15 to 20 per cent cut in pump prices to ease the burden of high energy and transportation costs on Nigerian businesses and households.

In a statement on Sunday, LCCI Director-General, Dr Chinyere Almona, urged the Federal Government to work with domestic refiners, petroleum marketers, regulators and other stakeholders to achieve progressive, measurable and sustainable reductions in petrol prices.

Almona commended the Federal Government’s proposed petrol price stabilisation mechanism, describing it as timely amid rising energy and transportation costs that have continued to pressure business operations, household purchasing power and the competitiveness of Nigerian enterprises.

The Chamber welcomed the proposed ceiling of ₦1,350 per litre on the ex-gantry or landing cost of petrol, subject to monthly reviews and public disclosure, describing it as recognition of the economic consequences of excessive volatility in energy prices.

However, Almona warned that stabilising petrol prices at elevated levels would not provide sufficient relief to businesses already grappling with high electricity tariffs, alternative power costs, expensive financing and rising logistics expenses.

She said the proposed mechanism could cushion businesses against sudden price increases but would not necessarily guarantee lower pump prices.

According to her, the government should assess the initiative not only by its ability to moderate price volatility but also by its capacity to reduce operating costs and improve economic welfare.

The LCCI chief also cautioned that requiring refiners and importers to absorb temporary cost increases and recover them when market conditions improve could create deferred obligations that might eventually push prices upwards if not transparently managed.

Recommendations for lower costs

To support the proposed six-month programme, the Chamber urged the government to ensure predictable and commercially viable crude oil supplies to domestic refineries to reduce procurement uncertainties, foreign exchange exposure and avoidable logistics costs.

It also called for the accelerated deployment of alternative transportation options, including compressed natural gas (CNG) and electric vehicle infrastructure, to reduce the cost of moving goods and people across the country.

Other recommendations include addressing transportation bottlenecks, improving storage and distribution infrastructure, eliminating unlawful charges, and maintaining exchange-rate and macroeconomic stability.

Almona further stressed the need for clear rules governing the price-stabilisation mechanism to prevent open-ended losses for refiners and importers, discourage investment or trigger fuel shortages.

She said Nigeria could not indefinitely insulate its petroleum market from international oil price movements, adding that sustainable relief required reducing domestic costs that amplify the impact of global market fluctuations.

The LCCI maintained that the ultimate test of the policy should be lower petrol expenditure for businesses, reduced transportation and distribution costs, improved competitiveness and meaningful relief for consumers.

World.title: Riyadh airport hit by fresh Houthi strike day after deadly attack
World.content:
This screen grab taken from CCTV footage released by the Saudi Media Ministry on October 11, 2026, shows the moment King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh was hit by a Houthi strike on October 10, 2026. The deadliest strike on Saudi soil in more than a decade killed 12 people at Riyadh’s international airport and wounded hundreds, prompting the Saudi-led coalition to vow on October 11, 2026, a decisive response against Yemen’s Houthis. The attack came during an unprecedented wave of Houthi strikes on the kingdom since a truce in the group’s long-running war with Yemen’s Riyadh-backed government unravelled in July 2026. (Photo by SAUDI MEDIA MINISTRY / AFP) / RESTRICTED TO EDITORIAL USE – MANDATORY CREDIT “AFP PHOTO /Saudi Media Ministry” – HANDOUT – NO MARKETING NO ADVERTISING CAMPAIGNS – DISTRIBUTED AS A SERVICE TO CLIENTS

A fresh Houthi strike hit Riyadh’s international airport on Sunday, killing one person and wounding 11 others, a day after another deadly attack claimed by the Yemeni group forced authorities to suspend operations there.

Saturday’s attack, the deadliest on Saudi soil in more than a decade, was a sharp escalation in the Yemen war, where Riyadh has long militarily supported the internationally recognised government against the Houthis.

The Iran-backed group on Sunday claimed multiple attacks over the last 24 hours, including on the airport, and threatened to keep targeting the kingdom’s transit hubs, calling them “a theatre of operations for our forces”.

Hours later, the Saudi-led coalition fighting the group reported that a projectile struck King Khalid International Airport, sparking a fire.

Air defences also intercepted a missile nearby, it added.

The fresh attack on the airport killed one person — a Pakistani resident — and wounded 11 others, Saudi Arabia’s civil aviation authority said on X.

Authorities have extended the closure of the airport by 24 hours until 2100 GMT on Monday, the tracking site Flightradar24 said on the same platform.

AFP journalists and locals reported hearing multiple blasts in the Saudi capital on Sunday.

“The birds went into a frenzy after the sound. The whole house shook,” said one resident of the Al-Aarid neighbourhood in the north of the city.

The civil aviation authority also reported another attack on Dammam airport in the east — which the Houthis also said they had targeted — a day after the Saudi coalition reported a projectile landing nearby.

Shortly afterwards, the coalition reported shooting down a drone, also in the east.

It said early on Monday that it had also “intercepted and destroyed” a Houthi ballistic missile heading for the southern Saudi city of Khamis Mushait, home to a major military base.

– ‘Full-fledged war crime’ –

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said in a call with his Saudi counterpart that “insisting on a military approach and disregarding a political solution would further complicate the current situation”, Iran’s state media reported.

He said Tehran was ready to help “initiate dialogue between Saudi Arabia and Yemen and facilitate the achievement of a political solution”, according to official state news agency IRNA.

The Houthis have stepped up their attacks on the Riyadh airport — where three people were also killed on Thursday — as well as on Saudi oil facilities and tankers in the Red Sea.

Although Saudi Arabia has poured billions into its military, Houthi attacks continue to slip through.

“Saudi air defences have been able to intercept some Houthi missile and drone attacks, but Saudi Arabia is so large that it’s simply impossible for them to consistently defend themselves,” said Thomas Juneau, security analyst at Ottawa University.

The anti-Houthi coalition called Saturday’s attack a “full-fledged war crime” and vowed to “respond decisively”.

Houthi media reported two Saudi strikes in Yemen’s Houthi-controlled Sanaa governorate on Sunday.
