A spokesman for the Houthi-run health ministry said on X that one of the strikes killed a civilian and wounded five others.

Saturday’s attack drew condemnation from the United Nations and leaders around the world, including US President Donald Trump, who said he was considering joining Saudi strikes against the Houthis.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, whose country does not have diplomatic relations with Saudi Arabia, also denounced the “horrific terrorist attack”.

Four Saudi citizens, two Bangladeshis, one American, one Egyptian, one Jordanian, one Syrian, one Palestinian and one Sudanese were killed, the civil aviation authority said, with 309 people wounded.

The Indian embassy in Saudi Arabia also said one of its citizens died on Sunday after being wounded the day before.

– Operations suspended –

Witnesses to Saturday’s strike described chaos in the aftermath.

“Some had lost a hand or an arm. People were running while carrying injured people, covered in blood,” a 32-year-old Riyadh resident told AFP.

The US, Canadian, German and Spanish embassies in Saudi Arabia have warned their citizens to avoid Riyadh airport.

Australia condemned the Houthi attacks as “unacceptable” on Monday, having earlier urged its citizens in Saudi Arabia to stay indoors and “shelter in place”.

Saudi Arabia leads an international coalition that has supported Yemen’s government militarily since 2015, including by seeking to exert control over Yemeni airspace and the airport in the Houthi-held capital Sanaa.

Ottawa University’s Juneau said the Houthis now “want to do to Saudi Arabia what Saudi Arabia does to them”.

On the ground in Yemen, Saudi-supported government forces were advancing in their counter-offensive against the Houthis around the Bab al-Mandab strait, a key shipping route, military sources said Saturday.

The Houthis claimed to have repelled them.

Claims by both sides have been impossible to independently verify, with the situation moving fast on the ground and access for journalists difficult.

World.title: Tinubu’s economic policies deepen Nigerians’ hardship — ADC
World.content:
By Muhammad Inuwa, Dutse

The African Democratic Congress (ADC) has accused President Bola Tinubu’s administration of worsening economic hardship in Nigeria, saying its policies have placed an enormous burden on ordinary citizens.

The Jigawa State governorship candidate of the party, Sabo Muhammad Nakudu, stated this in a post on his official Facebook page on Sunday.

Nakudu said the economic policies introduced by the Tinubu administration since May 29, 2023, had made life increasingly difficult for many Nigerians.

He called for urgent and sustained measures to address the situation and improve the living conditions of citizens.

The ADC candidate blamed the economic difficulties on the policies of the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC), arguing that Nigerians deserved better living conditions.

Nakudu also described the one-month reduction in fuel prices announced by the Tinubu administration as deceptive, insisting that Nigerians needed more sustainable relief from the rising cost of living.

He linked the price reduction to a proposal by former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, the ADC’s presidential candidate, to restore fuel subsidy if elected president in 2027.

According to Nakudu, ordinary Nigerians have continued to suffer since the Federal Government announced the removal of fuel subsidy on May 29, 2023.

He said the temporary fuel price reduction, which he attributed to pressure arising from Atiku’s proposal, was insufficient to address the economic challenges confronting the country.

Nakudu urged Nigerians not to regard the price reduction as a permanent measure, alleging that it was intended to mislead the public.

He said the ADC’s objective was to rescue ordinary Nigerians from the economic hardship and insecurity which, according to him, had characterised the APC-led government.

World.title: New Money Market Fund Opens to Public from N10,000
World.content:
A new money market fund offering two billion units at N1.00 each has opened for subscription, targeting retail and institutional investors seeking short-term, low-risk returns.

The Berkshire Money Market Fund, an open-ended unit trust registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), is being offered at par, putting the total offer at N2 billion.

According to the fund manager, Berkshire Asset Management Limited, the offer is designed to provide capital preservation, liquidity and competitive income returns consistent with prevailing opportunities in the Nigerian money market.

Rated by DataPro Limited and audited by Ijewere & Co, the fund will invest primarily in short-term, investment-grade money market instruments, with its performance benchmarked against the average yield of 91-day Nigerian Treasury Bills.

Subscription opens at a minimum of 10,000 units (N10,000), with later investments in multiples of 5,000 units.

The fund was launched in the presence of key industry stakeholders, including CFG Africa Trustees Limited as Trustee, Rand Merchant Bank Nigeria Limited as Custodian, and Cordros Registrars Limited as Registrar.

Commenting, the Managing Director/CEO of Berkshire Asset Management Limited, Mr. Adetola Odusote, said: “The launch remains a significant milestone in the company’s journey to create channels for optimisation of capital allocation for economic development, whilst leveraging technology to democratise investment by pooling small amounts of cash from everyday individuals to access low-risk, short-term debt instruments.”

Chairman of the company, Mr. Usman Abdulqadir, added that the fund would relieve investors the burden of selecting, valuing, monitoring and managing financial assets which will be handled by the manager.

He said: “Berkshire was formulated with the intent to deepen the Nigerian capital markets through development of a wide array of investment products, and the formal launch of its money market fund lays credence to the vision of the company to become the leading reference for digital investment solutions anchored on innovative products.

Managing Director of the fund’s trustee,CFG Africa Trustees Limited, Mr. Akindele Ogundepo, assured Nigerians that the trustee will oversee the fund’s operations to ensure compliance with investment objectives and protect investors’ interests.

He explained that pooling investors’ contributions could provide individuals with access to investment opportunities that may otherwise be out of their reach.

World.title: Prophet Ugochukwu Predicts Obi’s Victory in 2027, Foresees Violent Transition
World.content:
Mary Nnah

The Overseer of Immaculate Chapel Ministries (ICM) Global, Prophet Alex Ugochukwu, has predicted that former Anambra State Governor and presidential hopeful of the National Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, will win the 2027 presidential election “clean and clear.”

The prophecy was contained in a declaration he made on September 30, 2026.

Ugochukwu, a Nigerian cleric based in Canada, said he saw Obi, whom he described as “a man with an open tooth, handsome, tall man in the midst of jubilant Nigerians following an election. Come the 2027 election, Peter Obi will win the election clean and clear.”

According to the cleric, the latest vision is a fulfilment of an earlier revelation in which he saw “a new face” taking a seat, but whose manifestation was delayed.

He cited Habakkuk 2:3, noting that “though the vision tarries, it will surely come to pass.”

While predicting victory for Obi, Ugochukwu warned of a potentially violent transition period.

He said the aftermath of the election could witness widespread unrest and bloodshed, not instigated by Obi himself, but by Nigerians who are unwilling to continue with what he described as corrupt governance.

He claimed that foreign interests would attempt to intervene but would be resisted, describing the period as Nigeria’s “last battle” before the emergence of a ‘New Nigeria’.

The September 30 declaration followed another prophetic message released on September 11, 2026, in which Ugochukwu spoke of an impending “plane crash” involving the Imo State Government and the federal government.

In the vision, he said the Imo State governor was expecting a federal government delegation that failed to arrive, prompting the governor to fly his private jet to Abuja to ascertain what went wrong. During the flight, he said he saw another aircraft attempting to land before a crash occurred.

The cleric, however, clarified that the vision “may not necessarily refer to a physical plane crash.”

According to him, the aircraft could symbolise a political “crash” – a major breakdown, collapse or disruption in relations between the state and the federal government, which he linked to what he termed corrupt communications.

He also warned of another significant crisis that would hit the presidency.

Ugochukwu has been issuing political and national prophecies since 2021 through his ministry, also known as ‘Jesus The High Court Judge’, in Owerri.

His past predictions, widely published by Nigerian online platforms, covered national security, the death of Prophet T.B. Joshua, Pope Francis, former President Goodluck Jonathan, and former US President Donald Trump, whom he predicted would not return to the White House after his first term ended on January 20, 2021.

In May 2021, he also warned that “three more jets will go down in Nigeria” and predicted possible bloodshed in Owerri. His latest prophecies come as political activities are intensified ahead of the 2027 general election, with Obi positioning himself as a leading opposition figure against incumbent President Bola Tinubu.

World.title: CDS Calls for Sustained Investment in Indigenous Space Technology
World.content:
Linus Aleke in Abuja

The Chief of Defence Staff (CDS), General Olufemi Oluyede, has called for sustained investment in indigenous space technology, research and innovation to strengthen national security and enhance the operational effectiveness of the Armed Forces of Nigeria (AFN).

The CDS made the call at the inaugural Defence Space Administration (DSA) Day celebration, under the theme, ‘Space Power and National Security.’

According to a statement by the Director of Defence Information, Major General Samaila Uba, the CDS commended the DSA for its achievements, particularly the launch of DelSat-1, the establishment of geospatial intelligence infrastructure, the deployment of a Modular Earth Observation Outpost at the Headquarters of Operation HADIN KAI, and the commencement of academic activities at the Defence Space School in Orogun.

He charged the administration to strengthen indigenous research and development, improve the reliability and security of space-based products, and deepen their integration into joint and inter-agency military operations to address emerging security challenges.

The CDS further underscored the importance of strengthening collaboration among the Armed Forces, academic institutions, industries and relevant national agencies to accelerate indigenous innovation and expand Nigeria’s capacity to harness space technology for defence and national development.

In his welcome address, the Chief of Defence Space Administration, Major General Philip Ilodibia, emphasised the need for stronger synergy among the Nigerian Army, Nigerian Navy and Nigerian Air Force to enhance joint operational effectiveness.

He also called for sustained collaboration with the National Space Research and Development Agency, Nigerian Communications Satellite Limited and other stakeholders to advance Nigeria’s space capabilities in support of national security and development.

World.title: Scores Killed as Bandits Raid Two Communities in Niger
World.content:
Laleye Dipo in Minna

Reports have claimed that scores of people were, at the weekend killed, when bandits raided two Niger communities, Kokani and Kigbera in Borgu Local Government of the state.

Several houses and shops were razed by the gunmen said to be over 30.

According to reports from the areas, the gunmen wielding guns and matchers stormed the communities in the early hours of Thursday making the villagers to run helter skelter searching for safety.

It was gathered that some food stuff and animal were taken away by the marauders.

The reports added that the communities were among those raided about two months ago during which not less than 500 villagers were abducted and not less than 50 killed. The government then intervened sending a high powered team of security men to rescue those abducted.

THISDAY learnt that because of improvised explosive devices allegedly planted on the roads the rescue efforts were hampered.

Confirming the story to THISDAY the state Police Command Public Relations Officer, Superintendent of Police Wasiu Abiodun, said four men of the local vigilance group were injured during the invasion.

Abiodun did not confirm any loss of life but said people in the affected villages “ were forced to flee to different locations.”

The confirmation statement made available to THISDAY by Abiodun read:”On 8th October 2026 at about 4.30p.m, a group of armed bandits invaded Kokani and Kigbira villages, under Borgu LGA, set houses ablaze which forced few people in the villages to flee to different locations for safety.

“Report further indicated that four vigilance members were injured during the attack, while joint security teams were later drafted to the scene to restore normalcy.

“Further assessment is ongoing and further development will be communicated please.”

World.title: Mutfwang Urges Christian Unity as FBC Jos Marks 115 Years
World.content:
Yemi Kosoko in Jos

Plateau State Governor, Caleb Mutfwang, has called on Christians across Nigeria to strengthen unity in faith, love and purpose, declaring that a united church remains crucial to advancing the gospel and promoting peace as First Baptist Church, Jos, celebrated its 115th anniversary yesterday.

The event, held at the church auditorium under the theme, “Advancing Through Impactful Celebration,” drew government officials, church leaders, past and present pastors, members of the Baptist family, friends and well-wishers who gathered to thank God for sustaining the church for more than a century.

Mutfwang, who attended the celebration, congratulated the church on its 115 years of service to God and humanity and urged Christians to remain united in faith, love and purpose.

According to him, unity among believers remains critical to the advancement of the gospel and the promotion of peace in Plateau State and across Nigeria.

The governor commended the church for its contributions to the spiritual growth and socio-economic development of the state and prayed for its continued expansion and relevance in the years ahead.

Emphasising the importance of remaining grounded in biblical truth, Mutfwang said seeking guidance from the scriptures remains the surest path for the growth of the Christian faith.

“When we preach Christ and Him crucified, nothing more and nothing less, the gospel will thrive,” he said.

The governor also challenged leaders of the Nigerian Baptist Convention to continue fostering revival within the denomination and the wider body of Christ.

“I want to encourage you to do your best. May the Lord, through your hands, bring a revival that will spread beyond the Baptist Convention into the body of Christ. One hundred and fifteen years is no mean feat, and our prayer is that the Lord who has begun this good work will perfect it in Jesus’ name,” he added.

In his sermon, President of the Nigerian Baptist Convention, Rev. Dr. David Olusola Idowu, urged members to continually seek God’s presence as the foundation for growth and advancement.

Preaching from Psalm 100:4, he expressed gratitude to God for preserving the church through generations and called on members to remain committed to advancing the kingdom of God through dedicated service to humanity.

Idowu said true advancement begins when believers move beyond routine worship into a deeper relationship with God, noting that divine presence brings revelation, direction and transformation.

“As we trust the Lord to make greater impact, touch more lives, depopulate the kingdom of darkness and populate the kingdom of God, it is important for us to come into His gates and into His courts,” he said.

According to him, God’s presence provides enlightenment and understanding, especially during periods of uncertainty and challenges.

He noted that impactful celebration should inspire believers towards greater spiritual commitment and deeper engagement in the work of God.

The anniversary celebration featured praise and worship sessions, the cutting of a commemorative cake, special thanksgiving, goodwill messages and prayers for the church, Plateau State and the nation.

Founded in the early years of Christian missionary activity in Northern Nigeria, First Baptist Church, Adebayo Street, Jos, remains one of the oldest Baptist congregations in the region and continues to play a significant role in evangelism, discipleship and community development.

World.title: As Organised Labour Squares Up with FG over Worsening Living Conditions…
World.content:
Onyebuchi Ezigbo takes a look at various demands and position of the two Labour Centres – Nigeria Labour Congress and Trade Union Congress – over the biting cost of living in the country. While NLC is demanding outright reduction of the pump price of petrol to about N668 per litre, TUC, on its part, is seeking a revaluation of the Naira to exchange at N800 to a dollar so as to trigger reduction of fuel price to about N600 per litre.

When organised labour speaks, government usually listens with one ear open for the sound of strike drums.

But this October, the sound coming from Labour House is not a single beat. It is two different rhythms for same destination – bringing down the cost of living facing Nigerian workers.

The Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC), which is the more militant of the two centres, drawing more of it’s members from average and low income earners has bluntly demanded an outright reduction in the pump price of petrol to at least half of it’s current cost. Bring petrol back to N668.30 per litre, it said. That was the price when President Bola Tinubu signed the N70,000 minimum wage into law in July 2024.

On the other side, the Trade Union Congress (TUC), in a more technocratic posturing said: Don’t just slash pump price, fix the exchange rate of Naira to N800 to one Dollar and the pump price will fall to N600 on its own.

Two Labour Centres, one pain, two prescriptions. At the same time the federal government appears to be torn in between two difficult choices of abandoning it’s professed policy of total removal of subsidy, floating of national currency and restoring the subsidy and intervening to shore up the Naira value.

NLC’s Ultimatum: Return To 2024 Fuel Price Level:

The NLC fired first. On October 7, 2026, after its National Executive Council and Central Working Committee converged at the Olaitan Oyerinde Hall at Labour House, Abuja. The atmosphere, according to communiqué signed by President Comrade Joe Ajaero, was sombre.

“The joint meeting-in-session notes with profound alarm the deepening misery inflicted on the Nigerian working class… Inflation continues to soar unabated, the Naira remains traumatised, wages have been rendered worthless, and the cost of living has become unbearable,” the communique reads.

Its resolution was direct. A two-week ultimatum beginning Friday, October 9, for government to: reduce petrol price to what it was at signing of current minimum wage in 2024; commence renegotiation of a new national minimum wage; implement February 5, 2026 Terms of Settlement with it’s affiliate – the Joint Health Workers Union (JOHESU); and implement demands of Joint Public Sector Negotiating Council or it will be compelled to take remedial steps.

For NLC, the argument is moral and mathematical. as at mid 2024, when minimum wage was fixed at N70,000, petrol was N668.30 per litre. Today petrol hovers above N1,400 in many cities. That means the wage has lost over 40 percent of its energy purchasing power before food and transport are even considered. In NLC ‘s view, bringing petrol back to N668 will only restore the original bargain.

NLC also demanded tax relief and wage awards, insisting government “cannot continue to demand sacrifice from workers while not offering any relief.”

However, for TUC the diagnosis of the present energy crisis and it’s biting impact on the populace should be tackled by first identifying it’s causative factors which Is the exchange rate debacle.

Before it’s latest recommendation on the revaluation of the Naira, TUC had earlier urged the government to see if it can plough back part of the extra profit or windfall from unbudgeted higher crude oil prices to subsidize local refineries to cause a reduction in the cost of their product for domestic market.

In 2024, TUC had presented a 15-point demand with exchange rate as central. It has not shifted. Last week, TUC President, Comrade Festus Osifo mounted the podium after the Congress NEC meeting to further demand that Federal government upgrades the value of the Naira which in the union’s view has been grossly undervalued.

“High exchange rate of Naira to a Dollar is central to rising cost of goods including the pump price of petrol,” he said.

Osifo acknowledged improvements: macroeconomics picking up, inflation achieving some stability, exchange rate gaining strength.

While commending the CBN Governor, Olayemi Cardoso, he, however, said N1,300 to $1 official rate is still a failure.

“We still believe that Naira should be somewhere between seven to 800 Naira to $1. At 400 it was overvalued. At 1,300 it is undervalued. It is not trading at the strength it should,” Osifo argued, citing local and international think tanks.

This is the TUC path. Nigeria imports refined fuel, even with Dangote Refinery and Port Harcourt running, pricing remains import-parity linked. Every Dollar rise adds to pump price. Strengthen Naira to N800/$, you cut import bill by almost 40 percent, you cut petrol to about N600, you also cut cost of drugs, school fees linked to Dollar, spare parts and food imports. It is not just fuel, it is everything.

On wages, TUC is more patient. It expects formal minimum wage talks by February 2027, six months to expiration of Minimum Wage Act, but wants immediate talks on allowances and wage awards. It also backed warning strike by Joint National Council of federal workers and pledged to escalate if unresolved, and waded into JOHESU health dispute and the Niger tragedy where about 30 minors reportedly died in NSCDC custody, demanding culprits be punished.

From all indications, it appears that the Labour Centres are adopting different tactics to drive home the demand of the workers for better living conditions in the face of harsh economic situation in the country.

The difference is not just economic; it is strategic. NLC wants an immediate, administratively determined relief – government should order NNPCL and marketers to drop price, even if it means subsidy or price modulation. Quick win for workers, but with fiscal cost.

On the other hand, TUC wants a market-correcting structural fix – monetary policy that makes Naira truly reflect its value, which will naturally drag down petrol and general inflation, but requires CBN reforms, improved dollar supply, oil production and investor confidence.

Labour watchers say both NLC and TUC may be right but incomplete in their submissions. A stronger Naira to N800 would indeed crash petrol below N600 without subsidy, but can CBN sustain N800 without burning reserves? A forced price cut to N668 would instantly relieve workers, but without Forex reform, queues and scarcity may return.

What unites them is urgency. The current minimum wage, which looked like victory in 2024, now buys less Garri than it did then. Organised Labour, which has been relatively quiet in 2026, is smelling the 2027 pre-election air where government is more likely to concede. For President Tinubu’s government, the clock is ticking away. NLC ultimatum lapses on October 23, 2026. TUC has not given a date but its warning on escalation of federal workers’ strike adds weight. If government ignores the two labour unions, it risks a joint action – NLC shutting down economic activity, TUC also crippling oil sector expertise led by PENGASSAN, its affiliate body headed by Osifo himself. That combination grounded Nigeria in 2012 and 2024. The question now is whether Abuja will choose NLC’s quick cut, TUC’s strong Naira, or, as often happens, a middle road that satisfies neither of the two parties.

World.title: Tinubu: World Bank Report Shows Economic Reforms Working
World.content:
Says FG waived N3.3tn fuel taxes, duties to ease prices

Urges opponents to explain what their promises will cost

Again, presidency knocks Atiku’s subsidy plan, says it’s unrealistic

W’Bank: Nigeria among top 10 recipients of $112bn private capital in 2026

Deji Elumoye and Emmanuel Addeh in Abuja

President Bola Tinubu yesterday defended his administration’s economic reforms, citing stronger economic growth, rising foreign reserves and increased revenues to states, and welcomed last week’s World Bank report indicating Nigeria’s steady economic growth.

The president also disclosed that the federal government had forgone more than N3.3 trillion in fuel taxes and duties to cushion the impact of rising petrol prices, while highlighting the expansion of compressed natural gas (CNG) transportation as part of efforts to reduce the cost of living.

The president’s comments on the reforms came as the country emerged among the top 10 recipients of the $112 billion private capital mobilised by the World Bank Group in the year ended June 2026, according to information from the global lender.

Besides, the presidency has again knocked the fuel production subsidy being proposed by former Vice President and candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) in the January 2027 presidential poll, Atiku Abubakar, describing it as ‘unrealistic’.

However, in a statement issued by his Adviser on Information and Strategy, Bayo Onanuga, Tinubu said the World Bank’s October 2026 Nigeria Development Update, titled: “Beyond the Federal Purse: How Higher Revenues Reshaped State Priorities,” confirmed that the difficult decisions taken since 2023 were beginning to yield results.

Tinubu said the removal of the petrol subsidy, unification of the foreign exchange market and efforts to strengthen fiscal discipline had increased government revenues, stabilised the economy and created room for federal and state governments to invest in development.

“These findings confirm that the difficult but necessary decisions to remove the petrol subsidy, unify the foreign exchange market and strengthen fiscal discipline have raised revenues, stabilised the economy and created fiscal space for every tier of government to invest in its people.

“The dividends of reform are becoming visible. But more work remains to ensure they fully translate into better living standards for every household, starting with lower food prices and decent jobs for our young people.

“Our administration will stay the course of reform and redouble its focus on inclusive growth under the Renewed Hope Agenda,” he assured.

What the World Bank Report Says

According to the report, Nigeria’s economy grew by 4.2 per cent in the first half of 2026, compared with 3.9 per cent in the corresponding period of 2025, despite the effects of the conflict in the Middle East. The World Bank also projected that growth would average at least 4.4 per cent between 2026 and 2028.

Besides, the World Bank report found that federation revenues increased by 69 per cent in real terms between 2023 and 2025, with state governments emerging as the largest beneficiaries. The additional resources enabled states to raise capital expenditure by 151 per cent in real terms over the same period.

Most of the increase in state spending, it said, went into roads and other transport infrastructure, agriculture, energy and housing. According to the report, 29 of 33 states shifted their spending towards economic infrastructure, while real social spending per person increased in all but one state.

The report also found that Internally Generated Revenue (IGR) grew in real terms in 31 of 35 states, while 21 states reduced their debt-to-GDP ratios between 2021 and 2025. Nigeria’s overall public debt is projected to decline from 40 per cent of gross domestic product in 2025 to 38.1 per cent in 2026.

On inflation, the report noted that the rate fell from 27.6 per cent in January 2025 to 15.2 per cent in December 2025. However, higher global fuel prices linked to the Middle East conflict have slowed the pace of disinflation, even as the World Bank said it expects inflation to ease to about 12 per cent by 2028.

Nigeria’s external position also improved, with the current account surplus rising to $12 billion, equivalent to 7 per cent of GDP, in the first half of 2026, from $8.6 billion in the corresponding period of 2025. Gross external reserves increased from $45.5 billion at the end of 2025 to $53.8 billion at the end of August 2026.

The report further indicated that poverty had stabilised for the first time since 2019, with the World Bank expecting a gradual decline as economic growth outpaces population growth.

Tinubu Elated, Welcomes Findings

While welcoming the report, Tinubu said his administration would expand targeted cash transfers, which he said had reached more than 10 million households, while accelerating CNG deployment and improving agricultural productivity, healthcare and education.

“I urge state governments to use their higher revenues more prudently and prioritise projects that improve the living standards of Nigerians, and the health and education of our people.

“I commend the Economic Management Team led by the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, state governors and all stakeholders for their cooperation in implementing these reforms.

“I assure Nigerians that the best is yet to come under the Renewed Hope Agenda 2.0, which will accelerate the delivery of shared prosperity for all Nigerians,” he stated.

Beyond the development update, the president used his message on X yesterday to highlight what he described as the benefits of government-backed CNG transportation, citing commuters and commercial drivers who said the alternative fuel had reduced their travel costs.

Tinubu expressing his view on a documentary on the progress of the CNG initiative in Nigeria, recounted the experience of some citizens, including Blessing, whose journey from Masaka to Berger in the Federal Capital Territory, he said now costs N500, compared with N1,500 previously, representing a saving of N1,000 per trip.

He also cited Ada and Abigail, who reportedly pay N1,600 to travel from Enugu to Nsukka instead of N4,000, saving N2,400 per journey. A taxi driver in the video, Kabir, told the president that N10,000 worth of CNG enabled him to make three additional return trips compared with colleagues using petrol. Tinubu also said he had received reports from Borno of commuters paying as little as N50 per trip on CNG and electric vehicles.

“Your various experiences show what our investment in CNG transportation is intended to achieve. Lower operating costs for drivers should translate into more affordable fares for passengers, leaving families with more money for their everyday needs.

“When we removed the petrol subsidy, I knew the decision would bring difficulties for many households. With that decision came a responsibility to provide practical alternatives that would ease transportation costs. Your stories show this is already happening, and I want more Nigerians to experience these benefits,” he added.

The president said the federal government was working with state governments, through the Nigeria Governors’ Forum (NGF), and private investors to expand services under the National Affordable CNG Transportation Programme.

He disclosed that Ekiti had received 15 buses in recent weeks, Lagos 20, while Akwa Ibom had 50 buses ready for service. Katsina had introduced 30 CNG hybrid buses and 200 electric tricycles, while Kano had received 30 CNG buses and five electric buses, with another rollout scheduled for Edo.

Tinubu added that Kaduna’s 100 CNG buses had carried more than 3 million passengers, while over 400 certified centres had converted more than 120,000 vehicles to CNG. The government, he said, was also expanding refuelling infrastructure to improve access to alternative fuel.

“I also recognise the pressure rising petrol prices place on families and businesses. To cushion the impact, we have waived over N3.3 trillion in fuel taxes and duties. NNPC Retail is foregoing its profit margin for 30 days, prioritising public transport operators, while we work towards a N1,350-per-litre ceiling on wholesale petrol supply costs to reduce price volatility.

“These measures are intended to ease the immediate burden while we continue expanding affordable transportation alternatives,” he pointed out.

Tinubu also challenged opposition politicians seeking to lead the country to explain the cost and sustainability of their proposals, arguing that political promises must be supported by credible financing plans.

He added: “Every commitment must be sustainable and backed by a credible plan. That responsibility guides our decisions, including the difficult ones. Anyone seeking to lead Nigeria should be prepared to explain what their promises will cost, how they will deliver them, and whether they can sustain them.

“Promises are easy to make when the costs can be postponed, leaving Nigerians and future generations to pay the bill.”

‘Nigeria Among Top 10 Recipients of $112bn Private Capital’

The president’s defence of the reforms came as Nigeria has emerged among the top 10 recipients of private capital mobilised by the World Bank Group. The bank attracted a record $112 billion in private capital in the year ended June 2026, up from $69 billion in the preceding year.

World Bank Group President, Ajay Banga, disclosed the figures in an interview with Reuters ahead of the annual meetings of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank. Nigeria was listed alongside Brazil, India, Turkey, Romania, Argentina, South Africa, Bangladesh, Mexico and Chile among the leading recipients.

The $112 billion in private capital mobilised was in addition to $123 billion invested from the World Bank Group’s own resources, bringing its combined financing to $235 billion during the year. Africa attracted $22 billion in private capital, while Latin America and the Caribbean received $36.3 billion, Europe and Central Asia $21.3 billion, and South Asia $19.2 billion.

The World Bank’s figures indicated the scale of efforts to draw private investment into developing economies at a time of mounting financing needs.

Banga said the World Bank was also discussing potential crisis assistance with 30 to 40 countries as rising energy and fertiliser prices linked to the Middle East conflict threaten to increase economic pressures.

The bank had initially made $25 billion available to countries when the conflict began in late February, but relatively few had sought assistance at first, partly because the global economy had proved more resilient than anticipated. Banga said countries could access another $35 billion by redirecting resources from previously approved World Bank projects.

“There is pressure, and so I think maybe over the coming months, more countries will come for some slice of that first $50 to $60 billion,” Banga said. “We’ll see, ⁠but we’re ready. We’re engaged. We’re having conversations with a number of them, you know, 30 to 40 countries are in dialogue with us,” he added.

Banga said the bank could make as much as $100 billion available if the situation deteriorated, exceeding the $70 billion it disbursed during the COVID-19 pandemic.

Presidency Knocks Atiku’s Petrol Subsidy Proposal

Meanwhile, the presidency yesterday again knocked the fuel production subsidy being proposed by former Vice President Atiku.

Describing it as unrealistic, it explained that Nigeria doesn’t have the crude oil volumes to fund it. It also described the plan as a dangerous mathematical fantasy wrapped in political deceit.

Presidential spokesperson, Sunday Dare, made this submission in a statement entitled “Atiku’s Demagoguery in the Face of Tinubu’s Logical Policies,” describing the recent news conference addressed in Abuja by Atiku, as “a seminal example of shallow, election-laced demagoguery.”

Atiku had criticised the 30-day discount on petrol by NNPC Retail and a price modulation framework, which he described as a “panic-driven gimmick,”. He also claimed that Tinubu copied his economic homework without the production subsidy that made it work.

Dare cited the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, as saying on national television that Nigeria produces about 1.8 million barrels of crude per day for a population of over 200 million. The presidency added that the country does not really own all the oil produced daily.

It stressed that under joint ventures and production sharing contracts signed over decades, production costs, royalties and profit-oil sharing ratios “severely reduce the equity crude available to the state,” leaving fewer than 700,000 barrels per day of unencumbered free crude.

“To propose a blanket ‘targeted production subsidy’ on crude without the physical, unencumbered volume to back it up is pure economic illiteracy, invites the very opacity, fraudulent round-tripping, and fiscal haemorrhage that crippled Nigeria for decades under the old subsidy regime,” it emphasised.

The presidency noted that refineries such as the Dangote Petroleum Refinery need more feedstock than the state can freely supply without breaching international supply contracts, which is why Dangote and other domestic refiners also import crude.

It, therefore, rejected a comparison of crude allocation with farm produce like garri or cassava, saying it misrepresented commodity markets.

The government also pointed to the United States, which it said produces over 10 million barrels per day for 330 million people but sells petroleum at market prices, and to Qatar, which it said had to cut energy subsidies significantly despite its large gas reserves and a population of under 500,000.

“Atiku’s attempt to frame NNPC Retail’s decision to forgo its profit margin as a return to the fuel subsidy is a deliberate mischaracterisation designed to mislead the public and incite public dissatisfaction. First, NNPC had offered the discount to celebrate the 66th Independence anniversary. It merely offered to extend the discount by another 30 days.

“The administration’s intervention is a market-smoothing price modulation framework, not a return to unbudgeted federal spending. When NNPC Retail agrees to sell fuel at landing cost for 30 days during an unprecedented global crude price spike, it is not writing checks to opaque import cartels. It is leveraging its corporate balance sheet to absorb short-term global volatility, backed directly by President Bola Tinubu.

“Furthermore, the federal government’s negotiation of an interim N1,350 per litre ceiling on ex-gantry costs is a structural shock absorber, not price control. Under this framework, refiners and importers absorb short-term cost spikes above the ceiling and recover those costs later when global crude prices cool or local exchange rates adjust,” it explained.

It further stated that the removal of the petrol subsidy and the unification of the exchange rate had ended a multi-trillion-naira drain on public funds, which now flows to the 36 states and local governments through allocations.

According to the presidency, fuel queues have been eliminated and the gap between the official and parallel exchange rates closed.

“The government eliminated multi-day fuel queues. For decades, Nigerians spent days sleeping at filling stations due to artificial scarcity, hoarding, and unpaid subsidy claims. Today, despite global energy shocks, fuel queues have been eradicated nationwide because market forces drive supply.

“The dangerous gap between the official and parallel exchange rates—which let well-connected political elites collect official dollars cheaply and sell them on the black market for instant billions—has been eliminated,” it stressed.

World.title: PDP Tackles INEC over Omission of Its Candidates in Final List of 2027 Contestants
World.content:
*Pantami’s camp calls devt temporary challenge

*Gwarzo remains our candidate, says NDC

*Kwankwasiyya movement wants reason from INEC over NDC exclusion in new list

Chuks Okocha in Abuja, Segun Awofadeji in Gombe and Ahmad Sorondinki in Kano

Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) has expressed concern over the omission of some of its candidates from the final list of successful contestants released by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) yesterday.

Some of the PDP governorship candidates whose names were not listed by INEC in the final list were Ladi Adebutu, the Ogun State governorship candidate, and Ali Pantami, the Gombe State governorship candidate.

The party, in a statement by its National Publicity Secretary, Hon. Jungudo Haruna Mohammed, also assured all affected candidates, members and supporters that it was already engaging with INEC to address the issues responsible for the omissions, with a view to securing an amicable resolution in accordance with the law and established electoral guidelines.

PDP assured all concerned that it was treating the development with utmost seriousness and would communicate further developments as appropriate.

Meanwhile, a former senator, Shehu Sani, advised candidates omitted from the INEC list to stop pursuing legal action. Sani said the Supreme Court ruling on party membership requirements was clear.

He said in September, a seven-member panel of the Supreme Court upheld an appeal filed by INEC and restored Sections 77(5), 77(6), 77(7) and 84(2) of the Electoral Act.

Section 77(5) provides that only members whose names appear in a political party’s membership register submitted to INEC at least 21 days before a primary, congress or convention, could participate in the exercise.

In a post on X, Sani urged affected candidates to conserve their resources and prepare for future elections rather than spend more money challenging their exclusion in court.

He stated, “The Supreme Court ruling that enabled INEC to exclude some names of candidates is very clear. Affected candidates should not waste their money, time and energy fighting a lost battle.

“I also wish to appeal to those Barristers and SANs to ‘pity’ those candidates and allow them to rest, and not mislead them into spending more money ‘filing fresh suits’. Four years will come and go; let them strategise for the future.”

Pantami’s Camp: It’s Temporary Challenge

The Pantamiyya Movement, a group loyal to Professor Isa Ali Pantami, described the omission of his name from INEC’s final list as a temporary challenge.

A statement by its spokesperson, Professor Suleiman Mohammed, which Pantami also shared on his Facebook account, urged supporters of PDP and the Pantamiyya Movement to remain calm, hopeful, and focused.

The statement said the omission did not amount to a final determination of the former minister’s political future.

“This is a temporary challenge and a normal part of the electoral process, not a final determination, in sha Allah,” the statement added.

Gwarzo Remains Our Candidate, Says NDC

The leadership of Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) said in spite of the latest list of successful candidate for 2027 elections, which omitted its candidate as released by INEC, Aminu Abdussalam Gwarzo remained its governorship candidate.

In a telephone interview, Kano State NDC Chairman, Alhaji Hussaini Mairiga, dismissed notion of a change in the party’s ticket, assuring party faithful that the structure of the ticket remains entirely intact as originally planned.

According to him, the joint ticket of their governorship candidate and his running mate, Mustapha Rabiu Kwankwaso, was duly processed, finalised, and submitted to the electoral body in strict accordance with all established electoral guidelines and statutory deadlines.

“Gwarzo’s name was submitted to INEC, and he and his running mate, Mustapha Rabiu Kwankwaso, are the authentic flagbearers of the party,” Mairiga stated, reiterating the party’s backing for their candidates.

Addressing the discrepancies observed in the newly published list, the chairman attributed the development to administrative friction rather than an official rejection by the commission.

He suggested that human error or a logistical miscommunication within the broader bureaucratic process likely triggered the anomaly.

“I believe there is a mix-up somewhere, and I do not think the list is from the commission, since we are sure that the name we submitted is what stands,” Mairiga stated, downplaying fears of a deliberate party disenfranchisement.

Kwankwasiyya Movement Wants Reason from INEC over NDC’s Exclusion in New List

Kwankwasiyya Movement demanded a clear explanation from INEC over the exclusion of the NDC Kano State governorship candidate, Comrade Aminu Abdussalam Gwarzo, from final list of candidates.

Reacting to the development in a statement yesterday, the spokesperson of the movement, Dr. Habibu Sale Mohammed, said the group was concerned about the omission, noting that there was no known court order to justify it.

Mohammed stated, “We understand the anxiety this development has caused among our supporters across Kano State and beyond,” Dr. Mohammed said, appealing for calm while the matter was being addressed through proper channels.

“We, therefore, appeal to everyone to remain calm, exercise restraint and avoid speculation while the matter is being addressed through the appropriate administrative and legal channels.”

According to the statement, available records show that Gwarzo duly registered with NDC within the stipulated period as required by the Electoral Act.

“We are not aware of any court order or judicial pronouncement that could serve as basis for his omission from the published list,” the movement said.

In Bauchi INEC Excludes Four Parties

In Bauchi State, INEC published the names of 15 governorship candidates and their running mates for the 2027 general election.

INEC, however, excluded the names of the governorship candidates of Social Democratic Party (SDP), New Nigeria Peoples Party (NNPP), Action Alliance (AA), and Accord Party (AP) from its final list of candidates for the 2027 governorship election.

The exclusion means that the four political parties, whose candidates were earlier submitted to INEC, are not represented on the published list.

INEC published Abdullahi Adamu as African Action Congress (AAC) governorship candidate, with Shehu Imam as running mate, while African Democratic Congress (ADC) had Halliru Dauda Jika as its candidate and Samaila Mohammed Kabir as running mate.

Action Democratic Party (ADP) said it will contest with Yunusa Shehu Jinda as its governorship candidate and Badia Lawal Muhammad as running mate.

All Progressives Congress (APC) had Muhammad Abdullahi Abubakar as its candidate, with Farouk Mustapha as running mate, while All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA) had Naziru Usman and Aminu Mohammed Kabiru as its governorship candidate and running mate, respectively.

Similarly, Allied Peoples Movement (APM) will be represented by Yakubu Adamu, with Babamaji Mahmood as running mate, according INEC

Action Peoples Party (APP) had Kabiru Abdulhamid Shuwa as its governorship candidate and Yunusa Mamuda as running mate, while Labour Party (LP) will field Idris Aliyu Muhammad and Yilkat Samako as its candidate and running mate, respectively.

The commission okayed Kashim Ibrahim Muhammad as the New Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) governorship candidate, and Tata Alhaji as running mate.

National Democratic Party (NDP) had Haruna Muhammad Ningi as its candidate, with Shehu Usman Abdu as running mate, while National Rescue Movement (NRM) will field Muhammad Muhammad Zaharaddin and Kabiru Umar as its governorship candidate and running mate, respectively.

INEC also listed Adamu Usman Ahmed as the candidate of Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), with Alin Bababa Abdulkadir as running mate.

INEC equally okayed the Peoples Redemption Party (PRP) governorship candidate Shehu Umar Buba, with Aliyu Tijjani Mohammed as running mate.

Young Progressive Party (YPP) had Aliyu Umar A.G. as its candidate, with Bello Buhari as running mate, while Zenith Labour Party (ZLP) will contest with Lami BabaGeidam as its governorship candidate and Aliyu Shafiu Garba as running mate.

The four parties missing from the final list had earlier submitted the names of their candidates and running mates to the commission.

SDP had nominated Abdullahi Yakubu as its governorship candidate, with Yahaya Abubakar Maikobi as running mate. Action Alliance submitted Musa Zubairu as its candidate and Shehu Buba as running mate, while NNPP nominated Ahmed Shuaibu as its governorship candidate, with Ismail Zailani as running mate.

Similarly, Accord Party had fielded Mohd Aminu Bauchin Bauchi as its governorship candidate and Daniel Meshack as running mate.

However, their names were not included in the final list published by INEC.

World.title: Cape Town now has its own SWAT team
World.content:
Cape Town has launched a new SWAT unit to tackle serious crime. Image: City of Cape Town

Cape Town has launched a Special Weapons and Tactics (SWAT) unit, giving the City a new capability to respond to serious crime and high-risk incidents.

The unit was showcased alongside the City’s Metro Police Aviation Unit, which provides aerial surveillance and support for policing operations across Cape Town.

The SWAT unit will assist with gang-related crime and extortion, high-risk arrest warrants, hostage and barricaded-suspect situations, as well as security at high-profile events.



It is equipped with an armoured vehicle, modern firearms and technology including night-vision and heat-detection equipment.

According to the City, members of the team have extensive experience with the SAPS Special Task Force and are also helping develop training for future SWAT officers.

Cape Town also expands aerial policing

In another boost for policing, the City of Cape Town will also expand its aerial surveillance. The City’s Metro Police Aviation Unit includes certified pilots and four types of aircraft for different operational requirements.

Its work includes crime hotspot patrols, suspect tracking, search and rescue, crowd and event monitoring and land protection.

The aircraft use thermal and zoom cameras, AI-assisted tracking and laser rangefinders to help officers locate suspects and activity, including in difficult-to-see areas such as bush and rooftops.

Live aerial footage can be streamed to control centres, allowing officers on the ground to be directed more quickly.



The City said the units have already supported operations resulting in arrests in Delft, Somerset West, Strand, Tafelsig and Elsies River, among other incidents.

New digital nerve centre

The new specialised units form part of Cape Town’s wider policing expansion, which includes more than 1 300 new City police officers added during the current term of office.

The City is also finalising its Joint Policing Services Operational Centre (JPSOC), a digital nerve centre intended to bring together live information from drones, body-worn cameras, in-vehicle cameras, CCTV and automatic number plate recognition systems.

Cape Town Mayor Geordin Hill-Lewis said the City was building its policing capacity to tackle serious crime and wanted its officers to have expanded powers to investigate gang, gun and drug crime.

The City also said requests from SAPS to access its camera footage for investigations increased by 35% over the past year.

World.title: Manyi slams Zuma health ‘frenzy’, challenges Ramaphosa over Nkandla
World.content:
Jacob Zuma's hospitalisation has sparked a political row, with questions now being raised over the treatment of former heads of state and media scrutiny of their health. Image: X

MK Party MP and Jacob Zuma Foundation spokesperson Mzwanele Manyi has taken aim at President Cyril Ramaphosa over Jacob Zuma’s hospitalisation, questioning whether his concern for the former president extends to maintaining his Nkandla homestead and replacing his ageing vehicles.

Manyi also accused the media of double standards, questioning why Deputy President Paul Mashatile’s recent illness did not attract the same scrutiny.

His remarks come as the 84-year-old Zuma remains in hospital in Pietermaritzburg, KwaZulu-Natal, where he has been receiving medical treatment since last week.



MANYI CHALLENGES RAMAPHOSA OVER NKANDLA

In a post on X on Sunday, 11 October, Manyi questioned whether Ramaphosa and the Presidency were doing enough to protect Zuma’s dignity.

He argued that the concern expressed by the president should extend beyond messages of support.

“The proper maintenance of the Nkandla homestead, through the relevant public works structures, and the replacement of his ageing fleet are matters that warrant serious consideration,” Manyi said.

He maintained that former heads of state deserved respect regardless of political differences.

“Leadership is ultimately measured not only by words, but by the consistency with which principles are translated into action.”

If President @CyrilRamaphosa and @PresidencyZA are genuinely committed to the well-being and dignity of H.E. President Jacob Zuma, this commitment should be reflected in practical and meaningful action.



The proper maintenance of the Nkandla homestead, through the relevant public…  October 11, 2026

Manyi’s remarks followed Ramaphosa’s public confirmation that Zuma had been unwell and was receiving medical treatment.

The president wished his predecessor a speedy recovery.

MASHATILE DRAGGED INTO ZUMA HEALTH ROW

In a separate X post, Manyi accused the media of applying different standards when reporting on Zuma and Mashatile.

“When the country’s current Deputy President, Paul Mashatile, was reportedly unwell for approximately two months, we did not witness this kind of media frenzy,” he said.

He questioned why Zuma’s hospitalisation had prompted such intense scrutiny.

Manyi acknowledged the media’s responsibility to keep South Africans informed but accused journalists of fuelling speculation.

“The question is simple: Why does the media apply such different standards, and who benefits from turning President Zuma’s health into a national spectacle?”

He called for Zuma to be allowed to recover without further speculation about his medical condition.

Mashatile returned to work last week after recovering from illness. His office thanked South Africans for their support and acknowledged journalists’ enquiries during his recovery.

ZUMA REMAINS IN HOSPITAL

Zuma remains at Netcare St Anne’s Hospital in Pietermaritzburg after reportedly falling ill during an MK Party campaign visit to Msinga last Tuesday.

The MK Party initially described his hospital visit as a routine medical check-up and maintained that he was healthy and in good spirits.

However, Ramaphosa subsequently confirmed that the former president had been unwell.

Minister in the Presidency Khumbudzo Ntshavheni said on Sunday that Zuma was receiving care under the supervision of the military surgeon-general.

She stressed that only Zuma’s doctors could disclose details of his condition with his consent.

Neither his family nor his medical team has publicly confirmed a diagnosis or indicated when he could leave hospital.

World.title: Kaizer Chiefs’ midfield maestro is missing
World.content:
Kaizer Chiefs lost midfield schemer Lebohang Maboe just before the international break, and nobody is sure how long he’ll be out.

Maboe’s injury prognosis is unclear

Lebohang Maboe has been in stellar form for Kaizer Chiefs this season. The midfield playmaker has weighed in with two goals and two assists in the Betway Premiership this term, form that earned him a call-up to the Bafana squad to face Eritrea and Guinea. The 32-year-old was set to feature against Guinea but pulled up with an injury in Chiefs’ 0-0 draw with Golden Arrows before the international break. Maboe also missed a penalty in that encounter, so it wasn’t his finest moment. Now, there’s no certainty as to how long that thigh issue will keep him out of action.

Latest Kaizer Chiefs injury news wrap

Kaizer Chiefs are dealing with a lengthy injury list, but several players are on the comeback trail soon. Striker Flavio Silva is back in training alongside Khanyisa Mayo, who has recovered after a hernia operation. 21-year-old winger Langelihle Phili is also nearing a return after a serious ankle injury he sustained in late August during training, but he’s unlikely to be fully fit before the end of October.



Are Chiefs specialists in failure?

Since 2014-15, Chiefs have just a solitary piece of silverware to show for their efforts. A win against Orlando Pirates in the 2025 Nedbank Cup final was a timely fillip, but it’s not enough. Chiefs have to mount credible title challenges every year, otherwise, their work is considered a failure.

Chiefs have forgotten how to win

They’ve drawn four of their last five Betway Prem matches. The only win in that sequence was a 3-2 success over Siwelele. Next up is a clash with bogey team Stellenbosch, with ex-Stellies man Thabo Moloisane now lining up for the Glamour Boys. Chiefs trail newly-crowned MTN8 champions Sundowns by seven points, so they can’t drop too many more before Christmas to stay in the title race. Chiefs vs Stellenbosch on Tuesday, 13 October kicks off at 19:30.

World.title: KZN beaches get a major Blue Flag boost ahead of summer
World.content:
Several KZN North and South Coast beaches have attained Blue Flag status for the 2026/27 season. Image: canva

Beachgoers heading to KwaZulu-Natal (KZN) this summer have more internationally recognised options to choose from, with the province’s Blue Flag beaches expanding for the 2026/27 season.

The latest awards recognise beaches that meet stringent standards covering water quality, safety, accessibility, environmental management and environmental education.

The 2026/27 awards were announced by the Wildlife and Environment Society of South Africa (WESSA) at its National Blue Flag and Green Coast Awards in Hermanus on 8 October.



South Africa received 62 Blue Flag sites for the new season, as the programme marked 25 years of coastal stewardship in the country.

Which KZN beaches have Blue Flag status?

KwaZulu-Natal’s recognised beaches are concentrated along the North and South coasts.

On the KZN South Coast, 11 beaches now have full Blue Flag status for the 2026/27 season, while a further five have pilot status.



Full Blue Flag beaches: KZN South Coast

Trafalgar Beach

Marina Beach

St Michaels-on-Sea Beach

Umzumbe Beach

Southport Beach

Hibberdene Beach

Pennington Beach

Rocky Bay Beach

Preston Beach

Bazley Beach

Mtwalume Beach

The South Coast’s latest list represents a notable expansion from previous seasons. In 2025/26, the region had eight full Blue Flag beaches, including St Michaels-on-Sea, while several Umdoni beaches were still in the pilot programme.

The move is particularly significant for Umdoni Municipality, which has reported five full Blue Flags for 2026/27, compared with one full Blue Flag in the previous season.

The municipality said the improvement reflects continued work on beach safety, cleanliness, environmental management and service delivery.



Five beaches also have pilot status. These were:

Port Edward Beach

Umtentweni Beach

Scottburgh Beach

Lucien Beach

Ramsgate Beach

A Pilot Blue Flag means a beach is working towards meeting all the requirements for full Blue Flag status. WESSA describes pilot beaches as sites that do not yet meet every criterion but are working towards achieving full accreditation.

KwaDukuza has four

The KZN North Coast also features prominently in the 2026/27 awards. KwaDukuza Municipality has secured four full Blue Flags for:



Salt Rock Main Beach

Willard Beach

Thompson Bay Beach

ClubMed-Tinley Manor

It has also received pilot status for Tinley Manor Main Beach.

The municipality retained its four full Blue Flags from the previous season, although the sites have changed, with ClubMed-Tinley Manor joining the full-status list.

What does a Blue Flag actually mean?

Blue Flag status is more than an award for a beach that looks good in photographs.



The programme assesses beaches against requirements relating to water quality, environmental management, safety and services, accessibility and environmental education.

Water quality is a particularly important component, with bathing water required to be tested regularly and information made available to beachgoers. Beaches must also provide appropriate safety measures, facilities and information.

The accreditation is renewed annually, meaning beaches have to continue meeting the required standards rather than simply retaining the award indefinitely.



A boost for KZN’s summer tourism

The awards come ahead of the busy summer holiday period, when KZN’s beaches are expected to attract large numbers of domestic and international visitors.

KwaDukuza Mayor Siduduzo Gumede said the municipality expects increased activity at its Blue Flag beaches through mid-January 2027, linking the awards to tourism, investment, and job creation.

For the South Coast, the growing number of accredited beaches is similarly significant for a region where coastal tourism is a major part of the local economy.

World.content:

World.title: Audi Q3 Sportback TDI S line Black review
World.content:
Meet the Audi Q3 Sportback TDI S line Black, a sloping-roofed crossover for just over R1 million. A million rand used to buy you a full-blown executive sports saloon or SUV. Nowadays, it buys you the second smallest offering in the marque’s compact crossover range. And we’ll say it up front: this is not an attractive new car. Striking, yes. Specced to the hilt, for sure. But we defy anyone to pick it out of a line up as good looking.

AUDI Q3 SPORTBACK TDI S LINE BLACK

Curved double screen is a masterstroke in hardware design. As is the rest of the Audi Q3’s cabin. Image: Ray Leathern

Nevertheless, when you’re inside it you could care less how it looks. Because Audi’s new cockpit is the main event. Better still, the brand always rolls out the same tech across all its models. So, no matter if you’re in a Q8, A3 or Q3, the hardware is democratised. A curved panoramic display houses an 11.9-inch digital instrument cluster and a 12.8-inch central touchscreen. This represents a massive improvement over the outgoing technology.

It gives the dashboard a sleek, floating-glass look that’s good looking and easy to navigate. Standard kit on this test unit also includes MMI navigation plus, OLED lighting (with a cool start-up light show), Audi Connect services, automatic climate control, interior ambient lighting, leather upholstery and electric tailgate/towbar. Luggage space isn’t too badly compromised by the low roofline either. 488 litres with the seats up, 1 289 litres with the rear seats folded. That’s only about 100-litres less than the Q3 SUV that offers 1 386 litres folded.



DIESEL TDI SIPPER

20-inch wheel designs, with shades of the Lamborghini Huracan Evo to them. Ride isn’t overly compromises either. Image: Ray Leathern

Under the bonnet sits the firm’s 2.0-litre four-cylinder turbodiesel. It produces 110 kW and 360 Nm, the latter available from just 1 600 rpm in the rev range. It’s quick rather than fast but shove comes from a wide, low plateau, which is exactly what you want from a diesel daily commuter. You don’t wring its neck. You lean on it. As ever, power goes through a seven-speed S tronic dual-clutch automatic. And the transmission rarely feels like it needs to hunt for the right cog.

Performance wise, the numbers confirm the temperament. Zero to 100 km/h takes 9.2 seconds and top speed is 208 km/h. You see, brisk enough to merge and overtake without drama, but not the Audi performance model the dark 20-inch alloy wheels and S line addenda might suggest. Moreover, Audi quotes a claimed consumption of around 5.0 l/100 km. And real-world driving with trucks and Ubers that won’t move out of your way timeously, you’ll return closer to 6.5 l/100 km on a mixed cycle.

THE VERDICT

The first Audi with badge that lights up in red at the rear. Image: Ray Leathern

So, what about the cost? Well, the Audi Q3 Sportback TDI S line Black isn’t exactly classified as a bargain at R1 002 300. And our test unit’s lavishly specced options list took it somewhere beyond R1.1 million. But here’s the thing, it’s polished, quiet, comes with a gorgeous cabin and – like it or loathe it – the styling package does turn heads.

The Sportback silhouette does the heavy lifting and that coupe-style rear gives the Q3 a sleeker presence than the regular SUV. Plus, the S line Black spec adds a lot of nice-to-haves visually. If you have the money to spend and want a premium compact crossover that looks slick doing the daily grind, this one is hard to fault. Our time behind the wheel absolutely flew by, as did the miles. And as a result, we haven’t been in anything this accomplished all year probably.

World.title: UPDATE | Jacob Zuma ‘recovering well’ in hospital
World.content:
Former president Jacob Zuma is recovering well in hospital and is in high spirits, according to the Jacob Zuma Foundation. Image: X @JGZ_Foundation

Former president Jacob Zuma is recovering well in hospital and is in high spirits, according to the Jacob Zuma Foundation, which has appealed to the public and media to respect his privacy.

Zuma was admitted to a hospital in Pietermaritzburg last week.

The foundation has since reassured supporters about his condition while thanking members of the public for their messages of support.



Foundation spokesperson Mzwanele Manyi also expressed appreciation for the government’s statement calling for Zuma’s medical privacy to be respected.

‘In good spirits’

Speaking about the former president’s condition, Manyi said someone who had been with Zuma reported that he was doing well and remained in good spirits.

“The concern and the anxiety that is out there is warranted, so we want to underscore that,” Manyi said.



He added that, as of 15:00 the previous day, a person who had been with Zuma reported that he was “in very high spirits”.

“He’s good, he’s fine, he’s joking,” Manyi said.

According to the spokesperson, Zuma was even looking at other programmes and hoping to return to the stage to sing his well-known struggle song, Umshini Wami.



Manyi said there was no reason for alarm based on the information shared with the foundation.

Foundation appeals for privacy

The foundation also criticised journalists who have reportedly been camping outside the hospital where Zuma is receiving treatment.

Manyi urged the media to respect the former president’s privacy during his hospital stay, describing the practice of waiting outside the facility as “un-African”.



The foundation acknowledged the public’s concern about Zuma’s health but said that concern should be balanced with respect for his privacy.

It also thanked the public for the well-wishes and messages of support received since news of his hospitalisation emerged.

The government has similarly called for Zuma’s medical privacy to be respected, while the foundation says it will continue to provide reassurance about his condition as appropriate.

World.title: Red Level 10 fire danger: How serious is the threat?
World.content:
Dry vegetation and strong winds can fuel fast-spreading veld fires during extremely high fire danger conditions. Image: Pexels

Extremely dangerous fire conditions can turn a small veld fire into a fast-moving blaze, putting homes, farms, livestock and lives at risk.

The South African Weather Service (SAWS) has flagged extremely high fire danger conditions in parts of the country for Monday, 12 October.

What does Red Level 10 fire danger mean?

Red Level 10 sits at the highest end of the fire danger rating scale used in South Africa.



It indicates conditions that could allow fires to start easily, spread rapidly and become extremely difficult to control.

Hot temperatures, dry vegetation, low humidity and strong winds can increase the risk. Wind can also carry burning material ahead of a fire, allowing new fires to develop.

A Red Level 10 warning does not mean a fire has already started. It warns that weather and vegetation conditions could make a fire particularly dangerous if one breaks out.

Which areas face the warning?

Monday’s Red Level 10 warning covers several areas across the Western Cape, Northern Cape, Eastern Cape and North West.

These include Beaufort West, Prince Albert, Ladismith, Sutherland, Laingsburg, Victoria West, Vryburg, Barkly West, Queenstown, Graaff-Reinet, Cradock and Burgersdorp.

The warning runs from 08:00 until 18:59 on Monday, according to published SAWS warning listings.



How does SAWS measure fire danger?

SAWS uses the Fire Danger Index (FDI) to assess how easily fires could start and spread.

The index considers temperature, humidity, wind speed and rainfall over the previous 21 days.

An FDI above 75 falls into the red category, which indicates extremely dangerous fire conditions.

What should residents do?

Residents in affected areas should avoid lighting fires outdoors, burning rubbish or carrying out activities that could produce sparks.

People should also extinguish braai fires completely and report any signs of smoke or uncontrolled fires to their local fire services.

SAWS advises firefighting teams to remain on full standby during extremely dangerous fire conditions.

World.title: Small businesses urged to prioritise fire prevention
World.content:

World.title: New York's notorious Rikers jail awaits elusive closure
World.content:
NEW YORK - New York's notorious Rikers Island jail, long criticised for unsanitary and violent conditions, will miss a deadline for the vast complex to close down, prompting disappointment from activists.

The jail, which opened in 1932 and has counted John Lennon's killer Mark David Chapman, rapper Tupac Shakur, and Sex Pistols musician Sid Vicious among its residents, was due to shutter by 2027.

That was a pledge by former mayor Bill de Blasio, responding to persistent issues ranging from staff shortages, broad drug use and broken cell doors and windows.

He promised to replace Rikers with smaller facilities, but their construction is lagging behind schedule.

Lauren Stossel, a former psychiatrist at the jail who now sits on New York City's independent Board of Correction, has raised several concerns about the jail.

"Conditions generally, I think, are very poor," she told AFP, adding that violence is "rampant."

Rikers, which sits on the East River between the Bronx and Queens boroughs, primarily holds people who are awaiting trial in New York, as was the case for disgraced producer Harvey Weinstein.

Mayor Zohran Mamdani, who took office this year, has strongly supported closing Rikers but has acknowledged the city will not meet the 2027 deadline.

"We are very focused on advancing the closure of Rikers Island on the fastest timeline possible," said Dana Kaplan, who is overseeing the mayor's efforts to shutter the jail.

"This can't just be a project that's about replacing one set of buildings with the other. It really is about a transformational vision of our city's pretrial justice system."

"We see the closure of Rikers Island as part of shutting the door on what has been a stained history in our city of a correctional system that does nothing to serve the people in its custody or the staff that work there every day," Kaplan said.

World.title: Conservation groups alarmed at marine mammals' deaths in Spain
World.content:
MADRID - Conservation groups on Sunday condemned the death of a dolphin transferred from France to a Spanish marine park, saying it added to the deaths of other sea mammals recently moved to Spain from Canada.

Rocky, a 29-year-old male dolphin, died Saturday night in the Selwo Marina park near Malaga in Spain, where he had been transferred in July, according to the Marineland park in France where he had been previously kept.

Both Marineland, located on the French Riviera and closed to the public since January 2025, and Selwo Marina are owned by a Spanish group called Parques Reunidos, itself owned by a Swedish investment group called EQT AB.

Rocky's death followed those of a dolphin and a beluga whale that were moved from a Canadian park to another Spanish marine park, in Valencia, the Oceanografic aquarium, described as the largest aquarium in Europe.

The Canadian dolphin and beluga were transferred from a similarly shuttered park, which was also called Marineland but which is not connected with the Marineland park in France nor Parques Reunidos.

Another three belugas transferred from the Canadian Marineland to a park in the United States, in Chicago, also died.

"After the deaths of the five mammals from Canada's Marineland... it's Rocky's turn," the group Sea Shepherd France said in a statement posted on X.

It said it had warned about the health risks to the animals transferred from the French park, which it had unsuccessfully attempted to stop through legal action.

- Campaigners blame France -

The group said the French government was responsible for the transfers and should be held accountable.

Another conservation group, Tilikum's Spirit, said that, in its view, Rocky had died "because of a transfer decided by the captivity industry".

"We asked from the start for all the animals in Marineland to stay" and "we warned that this could happen", it said.

Rocky was born in captivity on March 13, 1997 in the Zoo Aquarium of Madrid, which is also owned by Parques Reunidos. He was transferred to the group's Marineland in France in 2011.

His transfer to Parques Reunidos's Selwo Marina park happened along with seven other dolphins from the French park.

Another four were scheduled to be transferred from Marineland in France to Valencia, in Spain.

Several groups have tried to stop the transfers, arguing that they should not be allowed under a 2021 French law prohibiting the captivity of sea mammals.

World.title: Policymakers take on energy shock, rising debt at IMF-World Bank meetings
World.content:
BANGKOK - Finance ministers and central bankers meet in Bangkok this week for the annual gatherings of the International Monetary Fund and World Bank, with the global economy buffeted between the US-Iran war's energy shock, rising debt pressures and the AI boom.

The meetings run from Monday through Saturday in the Thai capital, and will see policymakers tackle some stark choices, with the IMF calling on governments to rein in spending even as vulnerable citizens' needs may be growing in the face of surging inflation and climate risks.

The week will see a combination of high-level closed-door meetings, public events and policy announcements from the world's top economic officials.

On Tuesday, the IMF will unveil its global economic forecast, along with detailed regional outlooks through the week, as policymakers set about tackling the challenges darkening the economic horizon.

"To put it simply, the global economy is being pulled in two opposite directions: a negative energy supply shock and a positive demand shock from AI," said IMF chief Kristalina Georgieva at an event kicking off the meetings in Singapore last week.

"The combined impact of these two forces is highly uneven across the world."

- 'Perfect storm' -

Chief among the concerns will be the economic fallout of the US war on Iran, which has seen energy prices skyrocket as Tehran's retaliatory action has targeted Washington's Gulf allies and curtailed global oil and gas supplies.

World.title: Zheng beats Andreeva to become first home player to win China Open
World.content:
BEIJING - Zheng Qinwen became the first home winner of the China Open on Sunday as she beat Russian teenager Mirra Andreeva 7-5, 6-4 in the final.

The former world number four and reigning Olympic champion was a wildcard entry in Beijing, having struggled with form and fitness after elbow surgery in 2025.

It was the 54th-ranked Zheng's first title in nearly two years, and tears filled her eyes as she fell to the court in celebration.

"The feeling was incredible to win here in Beijing... in front of my home crowd is one of my dreams," she said during the trophy ceremony.

"I've been through a very, very tough year," she added.

She congratulated Andreeva on her French Open win from earlier this year before serenading the crowd with a song about chasing the "light of dreams".

Zheng, 24, is the first Chinese player to win the prestigious tournament since its inception in 2004.

Andreeva, ranked fifth, was more consistent to start with, but Zheng grabbed back a break and stayed with her 19-year-old opponent as they battled on the baseline.

Zheng saved three set points to level at 5-5 and won every single point after that, sending down an ace to take the first set.

A crowd desperate to see their homegrown talent crowned champion was at times disruptive as cheers erupted before points ended and shouts for Zheng punctuated serves on both sides of the net.

But the players kept their focus, holding serve until Zheng found a way through in the ninth game of the second set, firing brilliantly against the line to break and go up 5-4.

A double-fault threatened to derail an imminent triumph until Zheng, defiant, sent down an ace to win on her first match point.

- 'Want to give everything' -

It is Zheng's first trophy since October 2024 when she beat Sofia Kenin in Tokyo, and her first-ever title at the WTA 1000 level.

Ending the title drought was not easy.

"I felt like I just forgot how to compete after coming back from injury," she told reporters.

Concerns with her elbow forced her to retire from last year's China Open in the third round, which preceded a string of disappointing results.

"Finally, after so many losses, I (found) my fire again," she said.

The finalists' only previous meeting was in the 2024 China Open quarter-finals, where Zheng beat Andreeva in three sets.

Andreeva, playing in her first China Open final, said it was "a very nice week" despite falling just short.

With her run, Andreeva is set to move up to a career-high ranking of third.

Both players are scheduled to compete this week at the 1000-level tournament in Wuhan, with Zheng facing American Ann Li in the first round and Andreeva starting in the second.

"I'm so hungry, honestly, for what's gonna come next," Zheng added on Sunday. "I just want to give everything."
