World.title: From the archive: The songs that all Mexicans magically know
World.content:
I’ve been living in Mexico for a very long time. When I first came, I was barely an adult, and I’ve “grown up” here in the sense that I grew into an adult here. In lots of ways, I feel like Mexico has raised me from the age of 21 on, which I think most of us can agree is the age of just a baby.

I also love karaoke. A lot. I have a pretty average voice but can mostly hit the notes, and that’s enough for me. Really, there are few things more fun than pretending to be a rockstar, and Mexico is where I first honed my rockstar-pretending skills.

It’s at these parties, though, that I remember: actually, I’m not Mexican.

What makes this obvious? Song choices, mostly. And also this sad fact: Everyone seems to know every single word to lots of songs I’ve never heard in my life. They belt them out with the passion and pain of recently jilted lovers while I stand awkwardly by.

How and when did they learn them? Is there a secret Mexican kids club where they learn all the mariachi classics in elementary school?

Basically, the answer is yes, there is. Really, though, it’s mostly just from them listening to the music their parents listened to growing up. Remember too that children are included at parties here just as much as adults. They might be running around and playing, but Juan Gabriel’s music is subliminally making its way to their memory centers while they do.

I did not grow up with Mexican parents, so I’m still playing catch-up. It’s hard not to feel second-rate at these moments. I mean, what are the songs that Americans universally know? “She’ll Be Comin’ Round the Mountain?” Give me a break.

I know plenty of songs in Spanish, but I really just want to sing “I Want to Break Free” and other favorites at karaoke that fall within my limited voice range. If only I could comfortably hit Shakira’s high notes!

At least I can do fellow Tejana Selena’s Como la Flor, right? Alas, I am still far behind. Luckily, I am surrounded by Mexicans who can help me learn them, or at the very least what they are.

Some are ballads, and some are pop hits. But they all seem to have a magical effect on all Mexicans’ party time. They’re keys that unlock something inside the Mexican psyche, making them close their eyes, tilt their heads back, and position their hands in a way that can only be described as a gesture of anguish born from a deep well of heartbreak and passion.

So I have gone on a deep well expedition for you all, my friends, and have returned! Here are some of the songs that Mexicans know — completely, by heart — and love.

‘El Rey’ by Vicente Fernández

Vicente Fernández - El Rey (En Vivo)

Watch this video on YouTube

You might actually recognize this song, or at least some parts.

“Con dinero y sin dinero, hago siempre lo que quiero…” and “Llorar, y llorar…” are two of its most recognizable lines.



Vicente Fernández, like many of the great Mexican acts of the 20th century, had a real rags to riches story. Born in Jalisco, he spent his teenage years doing odd jobs, including working as a cashier at an uncle’s restaurant. Eventually, he started singing at restaurants and weddings, and the rest is history.

‘ Rata de Dos Patas’ by Paquita la del Barrio

Paquita la del Barrio - Rata De Dos Patas (En Vivo)

Watch this video on YouTube





Now, this song has some seriously sick burns. Here’s the chorus: “Rata de dos patas / Te estoy hablando a ti / Porque un bicho rastrero / Aún siendo el más maldito / Comparado contigo / Se queda muy chiquito.”

“Two-legged rat / I’m talking to you / Because a creeping bug / Even the worst kind, Compared to you / Is nothing.”

As you might guess, Paquita is known for her fearless teasing of, and anger at, Mexican misogyny. “¿Me estás oyendo, inútil?” — “Do you hear me, you good-for-nothing? — often makes its way into her live performances, and honestly, who can get enough of it? Someone’s got to stand up to all those cheating machistas!

‘Bésame Mucho’ by Consuelo Velázquez

Consuelo Velazquez — Besame Mucho

Watch this video on YouTube

You’ve probably heard this song before — it seems every artist has a version of it.

This is a recording of the original composer, who, if Wikipedia is to be believed, had never been kissed when she wrote this song at the age of 16. Check out this video to see her chops on the piano. Wow!

‘Amor Eterno’ by Juan Gabriel

Juan Gabriel - Amor Eterno (En Vivo [Desde el Instituto Nacional de Bellas Artes])

Watch this video on YouTube

Juan Gabriel, like many of the artists mentioned, is a Mexican institution. He sang passionately and often, accompanied by a full orchestra and mariachi singers.

I’m almost certain that most Mexicans know every single word to every one of his songs, but have not proved this scientifically.

‘El Triste’ by José José

José José - El Triste en vivo

Watch this video on YouTube

This is another one of those singers whose every song has essentially been memorized by a sizable portion of the population. Rumor has it that his singing voice completely left him after years of drinking.

Thankfully, he recorded quite a bit before that point.

‘Mis Ojos Lloran por Ti’ by Big Boy

Mis Ojos Lloran Por Ti

Watch this video on YouTube

This is a more contemporary song than the ones above, and it is a fun one! Whoever can sing this one at karaoke, in fact, pretty much wins the night.

Why? There’s a lot of really fast rapping woven throughout the song, and it is a major challenge.

‘Que Bello’ by Sonora Dinamita

La Sonora Dinamita - Que Bello (letra)

Watch this video on YouTube

This song cracks me up, and it’s one that I actually know! Sometimes I try to sing it at karaoke, but usually start laughing when I hear a line like “Pero me arrepiento, en el piso o donde sea y tómame” — “But I change my mind, on the floor or wherever, take me.”

Um, I’m sorry, a cold, hard floor? When there’s a nice, comfy bed available? Who are these people? In any case, it’s a fun little cumbia and a major classic.

‘Si No Te Hubieras Ido’ by Marco Antonio Solís

Marco Antonio Solís - Si No Te Hubieras Ido | Lyric Video

Watch this video on YouTube

This is the newest song on the list, having come out in 1999, the year I graduated high school. It’s a beautiful and heartbreaking ballad, with one of my favorite lines of any song: “El frío de mi cuerpo pregunta por ti.” “The cold of my body asks for you.”

See? Super romantic.

Sarah DeVries is a writer and translator based in Xalapa, Veracruz. She can be reached through her website.

World.title: Mexico’s week in review: An unauthorized police academy stirs a security row with US as triple storm threat keeps coasts on alert
World.content:
Listen to this article

Storms swirled around and within Mexico this week as a political misstep by Governor Mauricio Kuri in Querétaro became a national controversy.

Simon, currently located off the Pacific coast of Jalisco and Colima, is now a Category 4 hurricane and will make landfall this weekend. Hurricane Isaias swept past the Yucatán Peninsula and landed near Destin, Florida, on Friday evening. Far out in the Pacific, Tropical Storm Rachel, which briefly reached hurricane strength, stayed clear of the Mexican coastline on Saturday but was expected to weaken and send its remnants toward Baja California and the U.S. Southwest.

On land, President Claudia Sheinbaum reacted swiftly to the surprise inauguration in Querétaro of a binational security institution that received direct support from the United States. According to the federal government, the project was never disclosed to or authorized by the corresponding Mexican authorities.

In Nayarit, searching mothers helped authorities uncover an alleged “extermination center” near Tepic, where investigators found a makeshift burner and a pit containing the remains of recently cremated bodies. Officials haven’t said how many people died or tied the site to a criminal group. The discovery underscored Mexico’s disappearance crisis, with more than 130,000 people registered as missing.

Didn’t have time to catch this week’s top stories? Here’s what you missed.

Police academy controversy

Sheinbaum opened the week by questioning an “International Police Training Academy” in central Mexico, whose cornerstone Gov. Mauricio Kuri and U.S. Ambassador Ronald Johnson laid Oct. 2. She said such a project can’t exist without federal authorization and asked why the military, the Security Cabinet and the Foreign Ministry weren’t invited.

A leaked letter then showed Kuri had told Foreign Affairs Minister Roberto Velasco only that Johnson would visit Querétaro, calling the interactions ceremonial and never mentioning the academy. The Foreign Affairs Ministry replied that any security training project with a foreign government needs prior approval from the High-Level Security Group (GANSEG), which hadn’t been granted. It also offered to help Querétaro seek it.

On Tuesday, Sheinbaum said federal officials had approved nine Querétaro–U.S. cooperation projects since December 2021, but not this one. She cited the state’s security minister, who said the facility would bring specialized training from U.S. agencies. Johnson had called it a “State Interdiction Academy” and noted more than US $10 million in U.S. support for Querétaro police over the past decade. The episode drew parallels to April’s alleged CIA involvement in a Chihuahua drug lab raid. Both states are governed by the opposition National Action Party (PAN).

On Thursday, Sheinbaum met with U.S. business leaders at the National Palace, with Johnson in attendance, but said security would be handled separately. She said Johnson had agreed to meet Velasco soon, and Security Minister Omar García Harfuch told legislators that bilateral cooperation is subject to Mexican law.

Hurricane Simon threatens Jalisco and Colima

Simon strengthened into a Category 4 hurricane on Saturday morning, with sustained winds of 230 km/h (145 mph). The U.S. National Hurricane Center (NHC) said the eye could pass near or over Mexico’s west-central coast late Saturday or Sunday, though its track remained uncertain. Civil Protection chief Laura Velázquez said the impact zone could be Cihuatlán, La Huerta, Tomatlán, Cabo Corrientes or Puerto Vallarta in Jalisco, or Manzanillo, Colima.

A hurricane warning covers Punta San Telmo, Michoacán, to Punta Mita, Nayarit. Rainfall could reach 20 to 38 centimeters, with isolated totals of 64 centimeters. Authorities set up command centers in Puerto Vallarta, Cihuatlán and Manzanillo, began evacuations in the flood-prone Jalisco community of El Rebalse and suspended classes in 22 Jalisco municipalities Friday and Monday. Simon could be the second hurricane to make landfall in Mexico this Pacific season, after Polo.

On the Atlantic side, Isaias became the season’s first hurricane Wednesday night, the latest first hurricane in the 60-year modern era. It was forecast to make U.S. landfall Friday evening, with no Mexico landfall expected, though it dumped heavy rain on the Gulf coast and Yucatán Peninsula states. It followed Mexico’s first hurricane-free Atlantic September since 1994, a contrast with a Pacific that had produced nine hurricanes by Wednesday. Experts point to a “super” El Niño, which warms Pacific waters and raises wind shear in the Atlantic.

Sheinbaum presents presidential decrees regarding nationality and social media

On Wednesday, Sheinbaum signed a decree formalizing a constitutional reform that requires exclusive Mexican nationality for presidential, gubernatorial and Mexico City mayoral candidates. The ban takes effect from 2028, after gubernatorial elections in 17 states next June. Citizens Movement (MC) Sen. Luis Donaldo Colosio Riojas criticized the reform for creating “two categories of Mexicans.”

On Friday, after a fatal machete attack at a Torreón school, the government presented a decree on “safe digital environments” for minors. It bars platforms from showing or recommending content that promotes hate speech, violent extremism, sexual exploitation, suicide, self-harm, eating disorders, cyberbullying and illegal conduct. Sheinbaum said it would be published in the official gazette next Tuesday or Wednesday after legal review to ensure it doesn’t exceed the executive branch’s authority.

Border deployment and gunfire incident

Mexico sent 500 Army and National Guard troops to the Tamaulipas border after U.S. Coast Guard personnel were fired upon from the Mexican side Sept. 26 and returned fire. The U.S. ordered 500 soldiers to the Texas side.

The Foreign Affairs and Defense ministries described the twin deployments as part of a “Concurrent Operation,” backed by two UH-60 helicopters, drones and anti-drone equipment in five Tamaulipas municipalities. The Navy is also participating through “Operation Saber.” No injuries or damage were reported in the shooting.

Mazatlán gets elite reinforcements as violence persists

The federal government formed a Special Operations Group of 29 Defense Ministry soldiers to work within Mazatlán’s municipal police after repeated troop deployments failed to stem the violence. The unit follows a wave of homicides, armed attacks and explosive assaults that led officials to urge caution between 3 and 10 p.m. The city also bought 50 bicycles for soldiers and National Guard members.

Then came Thursday’s shooting at El Castillo prison, which killed nine inmates and a 2-year-old boy and injured 16 prisoners. Alleged Sinaloa Cartel figure “El Owen” was reportedly among the dead. Sheinbaum said the Security Cabinet is working with interim Sinaloa Governor Graciela Domínguez to strengthen the state’s prisons.

Inflation edges up

Annual headline inflation rose to 3.45% in September from 3.26%, the highest since May but well below March’s 4.59% peak. Core inflation eased to 3.75% from 3.88%. Fruit and vegetable prices jumped 8.78% annually, while meat prices fell 4.46%. The Bank of Mexico held its benchmark rate at 6.50% two weeks ago and meets again Nov. 5.

Investment news

Fixed capital investment grew 6% annually in July, the fastest pace in two years, driven by construction. Private sector investment growth hit a 30-month high, though the total remains 2.35% below its July 2024 record. Spending on Mexican-made machinery and equipment fell 8% from January to July, while imported equipment rose 3.5%.

In Nuevo León, Gov. Samuel García announced US $600 million for industrial infrastructure, mainly data centers in Apodaca and Pesquería. That brings 2026 foreign investment in the state to $136.6 billion by his count.

Bárcena says ‘not yet’ to fracking in Mexico

On Tuesday, Environment Minister Alicia Bárcena told lawmakers the conditions for fracking “do not exist” and that Sheinbaum hasn’t authorized pilot tests. Only testing for deep saline water has been approved. Government scientists identified the Sabinas-Burro-Picachos basin as the only viable site, but nonprofit CartoCrítica says all the fresh water needed there would come from basins lacking available supply.

4 economy headlines to know

Mexico’s trade surplus with the U.S. rose 21.2% to US $155.87 billion from January to August, as exports hit a record $419.34 billion. Only Vietnam posted a larger surplus. The government faces a tough negotiating backdrop, with the U.S. having declined to renew the USMCA trade agreement in its current form, in part due to its deficit with Mexico, which the Trump administration views as an unacceptable imbalance.

The International Monetary Fund raised its growth forecasts to 1.5% for 2026 and 1.8% for 2027, citing a strong second quarter, but urged fiscal consolidation.

Auto parts output hit a record US $10.85 billion in July, up 7.15%. Vehicle production, however, fell 15.1% in September, its steepest drop since 2021, and car exports declined 11.85%.

Finally, a Citi survey of Mexico-based analysts sees the peso at 18 per dollar at the end of 2026 and 18.50 at the end of 2027, after the currency fell 6% in September.

World.title: São Paulo Nightlife Tonight: Mr. Dan, Os Cabides — October 12, 2026
World.content:
Save Share In short Contents Listen Aa

São Paulo · Nightlife

Tonight, Monday 12 October 2026, São Paulo has a national holiday and a small but varied list: pagode (relaxed, sing-along samba) at Bar Templo in Mooca from 8 p.m., indie rock at Casa Rockambole in Pinheiros and a forró dance party at Canto da Ema, also in Pinheiros. Rain is likely early in the evening and the chance falls sharply after 8 p.m. All times are São Paulo time.

Tonight at a Glance — Date Monday, 12 October 2026, a national holiday (Our Lady of Aparecida). Banks, public schools and government offices are closed. All times São Paulo time (UTC-3).

— Weather Rain early, then drier. Open-Meteo shows 20.5°C (69°F) at 6 p.m., 18.5°C (65°F) at 8 p.m. and 18.0°C (64°F) at 11 p.m. The chance of rain falls from 88 per cent at 6 p.m. to 38 per cent at 8 p.m. and 5 per cent at 11 p.m.

— Top pick Mr. Dan (pagode) at Bar Templo in Mooca, opening slot at 8 p.m. General entry R$30 plus a R$4.50 fee (about US$7 in total).

— Neighborhood in focus Pinheiros and Mooca. Pinheiros holds two of tonight’s three picks, a short ride apart, while Mooca is the old working-class east side of the city.

— Entry prices From R$30 plus fee (about US$7) at Bar Templo. We could not confirm the prices at Casa Rockambole and Canto da Ema. Rate: US$1 = R$4.99 (EODHD, 9 October close).

— Safety note Use a rideshare for Mooca and for the trip home from Pinheiros, wait inside the venue for the car, and keep phones out of sight on the street, especially in the rain.

Planning more nights? Read our São Paulo Nightlife Guide 2026, with neighborhoods, costs, safety and how the scene works.

If You Only Go to One Place Mr. Dan, pagode at Bar Templo, Mooca The most complete night on offer: live pagode, a bar and a holiday crowd.

Tonight’s Top 3

1. Mr. Dan, pagode, at Bar Templo Pagode is a relaxed, communal form of samba, played with cavaquinho (a small four-string guitar), a banjo-style instrument and hand percussion, in which the audience sings along. Tonight the singer Mr. Dan plays an opening slot at Bar Templo in Mooca. Tonight Monday 12 October 2026, opening slot at 8 p.m. For ages 18 and over.

Genre Pagode.

Entry General entry costs R$30 plus a R$4.50 fee (about US$7 in total). Tables are sold too: R$170 for two (about US$34) and R$260 for four (about US$52), plus fees. The premium bistro area is sold out.

Address Bar Templo, Rua Guaimbé 322, Mooca.

Verdict The easiest pick for a holiday night out. For foreigners: standing entry is cheap, the crowd sings every chorus, and the music is easy to follow even without Portuguese. Book a table if you want a seat.

2. Exclusive Os Cabides, indie rock, at Casa Rockambole Os Cabides is a rock band playing a night billed as “Exclusive” at the Casa Rockambole, a small music house in Pinheiros. Tonight The ticket page lists the event from 7 p.m. to 11:59 p.m., and one agenda gives 8:30 p.m. for the band. For ages 16 and over; 16 and 17-year-olds need a notarised guardian’s authorisation.

Genre Indie rock.

Entry We could not confirm the price. The ticket page does not show tonight’s sold-out status.

Address Casa Rockambole, Rua Belmiro Braga 119, Pinheiros. The nearest Metro station is Fradique Coutinho.

Verdict A small-room rock night for visitors who want to see how the local scene works. For foreigners: arrive early, buy online before you go, and expect a crowd that knows the songs.

3. Trio Dona Zefa, forró party, at Canto da Ema Forró is a dance music from north-east Brazil, played with accordion, triangle and a zabumba drum, and São Paulo has a long-standing forró scene. Tonight the Trio Dona Zefa plays at the Canto da Ema, a forró house in Pinheiros. Tonight Doors at 7 p.m., with the show at about 9 p.m. according to the Sympla listing.

Genre Forró.

Entry We could not confirm the price. The Sympla listing shows no sold-out notice.

Address Canto da Ema, Avenida Brigadeiro Faria Lima 364, Pinheiros.

Verdict The best option to dance. For foreigners: forró is a couples’ dance with simple steps, and the crowd is welcoming to beginners, so a short lesson early in the evening is enough to join in.

Also Tonight

— Marina Íris, “Sorriso de Criança”, Sesc Bom Retiro A children’s samba show at 6 p.m. in the theatre, part of the ỌmỌdé festival of Black arts and culture. Tickets cost R$15 to R$50 (about US$3 to US$10), and children up to 12 enter free.

— Barbatuques, Sesc Pompeia A children’s music show, “Toca Aqui”, at 6 p.m. on Children’s Day. One agenda lists it as sold out, so check the Sesc site.

— Blue Note São Paulo, Avenida Paulista No show is listed for tonight. Its next shows are on Tuesday 13 October, at 8 p.m. and 10:30 p.m.

The Night in Context

Monday is normally the quietest night in São Paulo, because most big venues rest after the weekend. The holiday changes that only a little: the programme we could confirm is made up of mid-size bars, clubs and Sesc cultural centres.

That is a good moment to see the city’s everyday music. Pagode and forró are not tourist shows. They are the two styles that residents of Mooca and Pinheiros dance to, and a small ticket gets you into the same room as the locals. The two Pinheiros venues are close enough to compare in a single night.

Brazil also votes in the presidential runoff on 25 October, 13 days from tonight. Visitors need no papers for tonight’s events, but queues and road closures around polling day can affect transport later this month. Prices in this guide come from ticket pages and agendas checked on 12 October and can change at the door.

Practical Notes

— Transport Use Uber or 99 for Mooca. For Pinheiros, the Fradique Coutinho Metro station is the nearest to Casa Rockambole. Public transport may run on a holiday timetable, so check the Metro and CPTM apps before you leave and keep a rideshare as a back-up.

— Tickets Buy the Bar Templo ticket in advance on the Clube do Ingresso site. Check the Casa Rockambole and Canto da Ema pages again in the afternoon for prices and availability.

— Rain Rain is most likely before 8 p.m. Plan to arrive after 8 p.m., or take a car to the door, and bring a light rain jacket.

— Safety Keep phones out of sight on the street, and avoid waiting at the kerb in the rain. Wait inside the venue for the car.

World.title: Rio de Janeiro Nightlife Tonight: Pedra do Sal, Samba do Trabalhador — October 12, 2026
World.content:
Rio de Janeiro · Nightlife

Tonight, Monday 12 October 2026, is a national holiday in Rio de Janeiro (Our Lady of Aparecida and Children’s Day), and the city’s best Monday habit is samba: the free roda at the Pedra do Sal from about 6 p.m. and the Samba do Trabalhador at the Renascença Clube in Andaraí, from 5 p.m. Rain is likely early, then clears by 11 p.m. All times are Rio de Janeiro time.

Tonight at a Glance — Date Monday, 12 October 2026, a public holiday. Banks and government offices are closed, and bars and venues set their own hours. All times Rio de Janeiro time (UTC-3).

— Weather Warm, with rain early. Open-Meteo shows 22.8°C (73°F) at 6 p.m., 8 p.m. and 11 p.m. The chance of rain falls from 82 per cent at 6 p.m. to 50 per cent at 8 p.m. and 10 per cent at 11 p.m.

— Top pick Samba do Trabalhador, the Monday samba circle led by the composer Moacyr Luz, at the Renascença Clube. Samba from 5 p.m. We could not confirm that it runs on the holiday, so check before you go.

— Neighborhood in focus Saúde and Andaraí. The Pedra do Sal is a stone slope in the old port district where samba took root, and the Renascença Clube is a social club in the north of the city.

— Entry prices The Pedra do Sal is free. The Samba do Trabalhador is listed from R$30 (about US$6). Rate: US$1 = R$4.99 (EODHD, 9 October close).

— Safety note Stay with the crowd around the Pedra do Sal, keep phones out of sight, and use a rideshare for the trip home. Do not walk the empty streets of the port district after the roda ends.

Planning more nights? Read our Rio de Janeiro Nightlife Guide 2026, with neighborhoods, costs, safety and how the scene works.

If You Only Go to One Place Pedra do Sal samba roda, Saúde Free and outdoors, with Rio’s oldest samba tradition.

Tonight’s Top 3

1. Pedra do Sal samba roda, in Saúde The Pedra do Sal is a rock slope in the old port area, in the region known as Pequena África, where, according to local listings, some of Rio’s first samba circles took place in the 19th century. A roda de samba (a circle of musicians playing around a table) takes place there every Monday. Tonight Weekly series, starting about 6 p.m. (one listing says 7 p.m.). We could not confirm this week’s line-up, and rain is likely at the start.

Genre Samba, played acoustically with voices, guitars, cavaquinho (a small four-string guitar) and percussion.

Entry Free. You pay for drinks and food from the street vendors and bars nearby.

Address Pedra do Sal, Largo João da Baiana, Saúde.

Verdict The best-value night in Rio. For foreigners: arrive before 7 p.m. to find a spot, go with a group, and keep to the crowded part of the roda, because the quieter streets around it empty fast.

2. Samba do Trabalhador, with Moacyr Luz, at the Renascença Clube The Samba do Trabalhador (“the Worker’s Samba”) began in May 2005 at the Renascença Clube in Andaraí and is now one of the best-known samba circles in Rio. It is led by the composer Moacyr Luz and is held every Monday. Tonight Samba from 5 p.m., ending between about 9 p.m. and 9:45 p.m., depending on the listing. We could not confirm that tonight’s session goes ahead on the holiday.

Genre Traditional samba, sung by the whole room.

Entry Listed from R$30 (about US$6) by Time Out and Catraca Livre. We could not confirm tonight’s price or whether it is sold out.

Address Renascença Clube, Rua Barão de São Francisco 54, Andaraí.

Verdict The more organised alternative to the street. For foreigners: it is a seated club night with tables and a bar, so it is easier in the rain, and the crowd mostly sings along in Portuguese.

3. Palavra Cantada, “30 Anos”, at the Vivo Rio Palavra Cantada is a Brazilian children’s music duo, created by Sandra Peres and Paulo Tatit, and its “30 Anos” (“30 Years”) show is listed for 12 October, Children’s Day. This is a family show, not a late-night event. Tonight Monday 12 October 2026, 5 p.m. according to the Vivo Rio website.

Genre Children’s music.

Entry We could not confirm the price or whether tickets remain.

Address Vivo Rio, Avenida Infante Dom Henrique 85, Parque do Flamengo.

Verdict A useful holiday option for visitors with children. For foreigners: lyrics are in Portuguese and simple, so younger children follow them easily.

Also Tonight

— Showroom, the drag show, Teatro Rival Petrobras Listed for 12 October at the theatre on Rua Álvaro Alvim 33 in Cinelândia. We could not confirm the time or price.

— Blue Note Rio, Copacabana We found no show listed for 12 October on the club’s website, so ask the club before you go.

The Night in Context

Monday is a quiet night in Rio’s big halls, and yet it is a night when samba is very local. The crowd at a Monday roda is largely made up of residents, not visitors. That is the reason the Pedra do Sal and the Renascença Clube are on this list, and it is why they are a better introduction to Rio than a tourist show.

A holiday may change the mood. With the day off, more families could be out, and the late-afternoon sessions may fill earlier than on an ordinary Monday. We could not confirm whether tonight’s sessions follow their usual hours, so check before you travel.

Brazil also votes in the presidential runoff on 25 October, 13 days from tonight. Visitors need no papers for tonight’s events, but street closures and queues around polling day can affect transport later this month. Prices in this guide come from listings checked on 12 October and can change at the door.

Practical Notes

— Transport The holiday timetable applies to the Metro, buses and trains, so services run less often than on a normal Monday. Use Uber or 99 for the Pedra do Sal and the Renascença Clube, and wait inside a bar or club for the car.

— Rain The chance of rain is highest at the start, at 82 per cent at 6 p.m. The Pedra do Sal is outdoors, so bring a light rain jacket, or go to the Renascença Clube first and walk over later.

— Cash and cards Street vendors around the Pedra do Sal often prefer cash or Pix (Brazil’s instant payment system), so carry a small amount of cash.

— Safety Keep phones out of sight, stay in the crowded part of the roda, and avoid the empty streets of the port district late at night.

Musicians at a samba roda in Rio de Janeiro. File photo. Photo: Lgjunior/Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0

GABON · POLITICS

Key Facts — The country Gabon is a small, oil-producing nation on Central Africa’s Atlantic coast, ruled by President Brice Clotaire Oligui Nguema since a 2023 coup.

— What happened On Sunday 11 October, the presidency announced a reshuffle on television: five ministers left the government and eight newcomers joined.

— Who stays Oil and gas minister Clotaire Kondja, mines minister Sosthène Nguema Nguema and finance minister Thierry Minko all keep their posts.

— New energy minister Olivier Mouckocko, a geologist who was director of infrastructure and equipment at Eramet Comilog Manganese, replaces Philippe Tonangoye at water and energy.

— The numbers The new team has 32 members besides Vice-President of the Government Hermann Immongault, according to the state news agency AGP.

— What it means for you Investors in Gabon’s oil, including New York-listed VAALCO Energy, keep the same oil and finance ministers to deal with.

— Still open The presidency gave no reason for the changes, and the planned flared-gas tax has no rate or start date yet.

A Gabon reshuffle announced on Sunday 11 October brought eight new ministers into the government of President Brice Clotaire Oligui Nguema and removed five. The secretary general of the presidency read the list on television, according to the Libreville news site Gabonreview and the state news agency AGP.

For foreign investors, including US oil producer VAALCO Energy, the Gabon reshuffle keeps the oil, mines and finance ministers in place. The water and energy minister is out after months of water shortages and power cuts.

Who Leaves and Who Joins in the Gabon Reshuffle

Oligui Nguema led the August 2023 coup that ended more than five decades of Bongo family rule. He won the presidential election of 12 April 2025, and a new constitution abolished the post of prime minister.

The five ministers dropped in the Gabon reshuffle held water and energy, national education, institutional reform, industry, and social affairs.

Gabonreview listed the eight newcomers. They take over energy, fisheries, trade, social affairs, public works, tourism, the environment and a deputy post at the interior ministry.

Emmanuel Eyeghe Nze becomes minister of trade, industry and processing, and also government spokesman. Jacqueline Ilogue, previously labour minister, moves to national education.

Edgard Moukoumbi moves from public works to the interior ministry, which runs the police and local government. His predecessor there, Adrien Nguema Mba, takes over labour.

Hermann Immongault keeps his post as vice-president of the government, the official who coordinates the cabinet for the president. Defence minister Brigitte Onkanowa and transport minister Ulrich Manfoumbi Manfoumbi remain ministers of state, the senior rank.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on Africa Email address Follow Free. One email a day at most, and only when there is news. This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, Africa Intelligence. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

A Mining Executive Takes Over Power and Water

The Gabon reshuffle also replaces the minister for universal access to water and energy. Philippe Tonangoye, appointed in May 2025, leaves after months of water shortages and power cuts, according to the news site Gabon Media Time.

The outlet cited repeated blackouts at SEEG, the state water and power utility, along with sabotage, equipment theft and a fire at its headquarters. Those problems strained households and fed public discontent, it wrote.

His successor, Olivier Mouckocko, is a geologist trained in groundwater science. Before Sunday he was director of infrastructure and equipment at Eramet Comilog Manganese, according to AGP.

Comilog, controlled by the French mining group Eramet, runs the large manganese mine at Moanda in southeastern Gabon. Manganese is a metal used to harden steel and in some electric-vehicle batteries.

Oil, Mines and Finance Stay in the Same Hands

Clotaire Kondja remains minister of oil and gas, and Sosthène Nguema Nguema remains minister of mines, according to the full list published by Gabonreview. Marie-Edith Tassyla-Ye-Doumbeneny stays on as foreign minister.

Thierry Minko keeps the economy and finance ministry, which also handles debt and state shareholdings. On Thursday 8 October, the cabinet noted his ministry’s plan for an environmental tax on gas that oil companies burn off.

In September alone, keeping pump prices stable cost the state 30 billion CFA francs (about US$51 million), according to the official communiqué of that meeting. The communiqué blamed the jump on the crisis in the Middle East.

Before the war in Ukraine, the monthly bill ran at 7 billion to 9 billion CFA francs (about US$12 million to US$15 million). These amounts are converted at about 586 CFA francs to the US dollar on 12 October 2026.

The cabinet also approved Gabon’s attendance at the World Bank and International Monetary Fund annual meetings in Bangkok, from 12 to 18 October. The World Bank estimates that Gabon’s public debt passed 80% of gross domestic product in 2025.

What It Means for US Readers

Gabon pumps oil on land and off its Atlantic coast, and a US company is among the operators. Houston-based VAALCO Energy, listed in New York, operates the offshore Etame Marin block with a 58.8% working interest, according to the company.

For oil companies, the Gabon reshuffle leaves the same ministers in charge of licences, taxes and the planned levy on flared gas.

Gabon, the world’s second-largest manganese producer, supplied 63% of US manganese ore imports from 2020 to 2023, according to the US Geological Survey. Washington lists manganese as a critical mineral, and Gabon’s mines minister keeps his post.

The Gabon reshuffle does not change who runs the country. Power remains with Oligui Nguema, who decided the new line-up, according to Gabonreview.

What Is Not Known

The presidency has given no official reason for the Gabon reshuffle, and AGP noted only that the new team faces major challenges. The new list also drops the budget title of Marc Abeghe, the junior minister at the finance ministry.

Whether Abeghe still controls the budget is unclear, Gabonreview noted. It is also unclear when the gas-flaring tax will take effect or what rate companies will pay.

The cabinet communiqué gave neither, and Gabonreview wrote that both remain to be set in later legal texts, in its report on the tax.

More: Africa news in English, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

What happened in the Gabon reshuffle?

On Sunday 11 October, the presidency announced that five ministers were leaving and eight were joining. The new team has 32 members besides the vice-president of the government.

Who is Gabon’s new energy minister?

Olivier Mouckocko, a geologist who was director of infrastructure and equipment at Eramet Comilog Manganese. He replaces Philippe Tonangoye, whose time in office saw months of water shortages and power cuts.

Did Gabon change its oil or finance minister?

No. Clotaire Kondja stays at oil and gas, Thierry Minko at economy and finance, and Sosthène Nguema Nguema at mines.

Why does the Gabon reshuffle matter to US investors?

Houston-based VAALCO Energy, listed in New York, operates an offshore oil block in Gabon. The same oil and finance ministers stay in charge of licences, taxes and a planned tax on flared gas.

Who leads Gabon?

President Brice Clotaire Oligui Nguema, who led an August 2023 coup and won the presidential election of 12 April 2025. Hermann Immongault coordinates the cabinet as vice-president of the government.

World.title: Bolivia Morales Backers Plan La Paz March
World.content:
Save Share In short Contents Listen Aa

A blockade on a rural road to Tiwanaku, near La Paz, in an archive photo; road blockades are among the protests Bolivia's state of exception is meant to prevent (Photo: BlackNose, CC BY 3.0 via Wikimedia Commons)

POLITICS · BOLIVIA

Key Facts — The country Bolivia, a landlocked South American country with large lithium and gas reserves. President Rodrigo Paz has governed since 8 November 2025.

— Why it matters Groups including those loyal to former president Evo Morales blocked roads for 53 days in May and June, El Día reported, cutting supply routes and hurting the economy.

— Why now On Sunday 11 October, Morales-aligned leaders confirmed staggered protests and a march on La Paz from Tuesday 13 October, despite a state of exception.

— What happened Police deployed at four points on Cochabamba’s highways. President Paz said on Sunday that people who call for blockades are “traitors”.

— The numbers The march starts on 13 October. The COB union federation meets on 15 October. A state of exception, extended for 90 days in September, restricts road blockades.

— What it means for you Travellers and shippers on routes linking La Paz, Cochabamba and Santa Cruz should expect checkpoints and possible delays from Tuesday.

— Still open Where the march starts, how many people join, and whether the main union federation or peasant unions add their own protests.

Supporters of former Bolivian president Evo Morales will start a Bolivia march on the seat of government, La Paz, on Tuesday 13 October. They confirmed the plan on Sunday 11 October, despite a state of exception that bans road blockades. For US investors and travellers, it is the first big test of whether Bolivia can avoid a repeat of this year’s long highway shutdowns.

Police have already taken up positions on key highways in Cochabamba department, Morales’s political base. President Rodrigo Paz, who took office on 8 November 2025, said on Sunday that anyone who calls for a blockade “is asking for death”.

The protest targets Paz’s economic measures. These include a decree that removes the diesel subsidy and a plan to close or sell loss-making state companies, Visión 360 and Red Uno reported.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Bolivia ranks 12th of 14 with 28.4 points. Strongest pillar: military means (55); weakest: diplomatic & cultural influence (13). Alignment group: Hedging. WatchRating below investment grade (CCC+); economy contracting (-1.2%); inflation of 20%. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

What the Morales Camp Announced

Franco García, president of the Coordinadora Urbana Popular and a leader of the Evo Pueblo movement in Cochabamba, said the government’s deadline had expired. “We will see each other in the streets,” he said, according to Visión 360. He said peasant federations from all nine departments would join.

Jerson Murillo, a peasant union leader aligned with Morales, ruled out talks. “We are marching from the 13th. We are not going to greet or talk with the government. I already warned, we are going to remove it,” he said, according to Los Tiempos and Unitel.

Murillo did not say where the Bolivia march will begin. He named Caracollo, Patacamaya and La Huachaca as possible starting points on the Altiplano highway to La Paz. Organisers told Red Uno the protests would be staggered and peaceful.

Morales, Bolivia’s president from 2006 to 2019, has his base in the Chapare coca-growing region of Cochabamba. He faces an arrest order linked to earlier protests, which he rejects, Unitel reported. For background, see Bolivia Seeks Regional Help on 2 Evo Morales Warrants.

This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

How the Government and Police Responded

In an interview with state media published on Sunday, Paz said blockades starve hospitals of oxygen, push up food prices and stop exports. “Those are not compatriots, those are traitors,” he said, according to Unitel.

Henry Ontiveros, the police commander for Cochabamba department, said officers were posted on all bridges and access roads to the city. Police deployed at Parotani, Suticollo, the Vacas junction and the Huayllani bridge, on the routes west to La Paz and east to Santa Cruz, Visión 360 reported.

The state of exception was first declared after the May and June blockades. It was extended for 90 days in September with the support of the Legislative Assembly, El Día reported. It lets the armed forces help the police keep roads open. For background on police equipment, see Bolivia Police Get US Riot Gear on 9 October.

The Altiplano beside Route 4 between Cahuasi and Caracollo, one of the possible starting points named for the march (file photo, 2019) (Photo: Eshko Timiou, CC0, via Wikimedia Commons)

Other Groups Weigh Their Own Protests

The Morales camp is not the only group unhappy with the diesel price rise. The Central Obrera Boliviana (COB), the country’s main trade-union federation, called a national meeting in Cochabamba for Thursday 15 October to analyse “the current situation”, El Día reported.

A faction of the CSUTCB, the main peasant confederation, met on Saturday night. It rejected the diesel price rise and called for unity among rival leaders before deciding on any action, El Día reported, citing a Vos TV report.

At a weekend meeting of Runasur, a regional network of left-wing movements, in Villa Tunari, Morales also attacked the Shield of the Americas. That is the anti-drug cooperation alliance promoted by US President Donald Trump. Morales compared it to Plan Condor, the campaign of repression run by South American military regimes in the 1970s and 1980s, Visión 360 reported.

What It Means for You

Anyone travelling overland in Bolivia this week should check road conditions daily. The highways linking La Paz, Oruro, Cochabamba and Santa Cruz are the most exposed. Flights between the main cities avoid the roads if protests grow.

For investors, the Bolivia march is a test of Paz’s reform plan, which includes ending the diesel subsidy. A short, peaceful march would suggest the state of exception is working. Weeks of blockades would hit exports, food supply and fuel distribution again. For the fuel context, see Bolivia Keeps Petrol Subsidy Until January Review.

The government has warned it will not allow new pressure measures, Los Tiempos reported, and police say they will keep the main roads open.

What Is Not Known

It is not known how many people will join, or from which town the march will leave. Organisers have not given an expected turnout.

It is unclear whether the COB or the peasant unions will join on Thursday or later. The government has not said how it would respond if roads are blocked, beyond enforcing the state of exception. A US statement on the blockades reported by Bolivian media could not be checked against the original.

Frequently Asked Questions

When does the Bolivia march by Morales supporters start?

Groups loyal to former president Evo Morales say staggered protests and a march on La Paz begin on Tuesday 13 October. The starting point has not been confirmed.

What does Bolivia’s state of exception allow?

It restricts road blockades and lets the armed forces support the police in keeping roads open. It was extended for 90 days in September, El Día reported.

Is it safe to travel by road in Bolivia this week?

Delays and checkpoints are possible on highways linking La Paz, Oruro, Cochabamba and Santa Cruz. Travellers should check road conditions daily and consider flights.

Sources: Visión 360, 11 October; Los Tiempos, 11 October; Unitel, Paz interview; Unitel, police deployment; El Día; Red Uno; Visión 360, Runasur; Teleamazonas, Paz inauguration.

World.title: Peru Says US, China Eye US$800 Million Port
World.content:
Save Share In short Contents Listen Aa

The beach at La Punta de Bombón in Islay province, Arequipa, the district where the Corío port is planned, in January 2006 (Photo: Robertnura, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons)

ECONOMY · PERU

Key Facts — The country Peru is a major copper and farm exporter. Its biggest new port, Chancay, north of Lima, is run by China’s state-owned Cosco Shipping.

— Why it matters A second deep-water port in the south would decide whether US or Chinese capital shapes Peru’s Pacific trade routes to Brazil and Bolivia.

— Why now Arequipa’s governor, Rohel Sánchez, said in an RPP radio interview reported on Sunday 11 October that groups from four countries are interested. Officials pitch the port to investors in Lima on Monday 12 October.

— What happened Sánchez named groups from the United States, China, India and the Netherlands. The project’s official master plan prices it at more than US$800 million.

— The numbers The site covers 34,596 hectares, with 1,127 hectares for the port core. Natural depth is 19 to 29 metres, regional outlets reported.

— What it means for you US port operators, shippers and grain or mineral traders may get a chance to bid. Nothing is tendered yet, and no investor is committed.

— Still open Which companies are interested, when ProInversión, the state investment agency, opens a process, and who would finance the port.

Business groups from the United States, China, India and the Netherlands have shown interest in the planned Corío port in southern Peru, Arequipa’s regional governor said. The Corío port would sit in Islay province, on the Pacific coast of the Arequipa region in Peru’s far south. For US readers, it is a test of whether American capital competes with China for Peru’s next big gateway.

Rohel Sánchez, the elected governor of Arequipa, made the claim in an interview with RPP, a national radio network. Perú Informa and Evidencia, two Peruvian outlets, reported it on Sunday 11 October.

No company has been named, no tender exists and no money is committed. The project is still at the stage where the state decides how to offer it to private investors.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Peru ranks 5th of 14 with 54.7 points. Strongest pillar: military means (71); weakest: future resources (37). Alignment group: Closer to Washington. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

What the Governor Said

Sánchez said he had met business groups from the four countries, all interested in taking part in the port. He also said the chief executive of Hyundai, the South Korean carmaker, had shown interest in green hydrogen and car industry projects there.

According to Evidencia, Sánchez said the project would now enter a phase of talks with bidders. He said the land had been registered in the name of the Peruvian state.

Perú Informa reported that 34,596 hectares are registered to the state. Of these, 1,127 hectares are set aside for the port core, and the rest for industrial, technology and urban zones.

The governor stressed the site’s natural depth, which outlets put at 19 to 29 metres. That would let it handle very large ships. He said it could carry cargo from southern Brazil and link with the southern railway towards Bolivia and Argentina.

This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

Where the Corío Port Stands

The official process is slower than the governor’s words suggest. On Thursday 3 September, the National Port Authority (APN), the state port regulator, approved the master plan for the Corío terminal.

The plan foresees a multipurpose terminal for containers, break-bulk and dry bulk cargo, built in three stages. It puts the investment at more than US$800 million, according to PortalPortuario, a regional shipping news site.

That is far below the figure of about US$7 billion that promoters of the project had cited. They had pitched Corío as a hub bigger than Chancay.

.8 billion with the US billion figure promoters had cited" data-lazy-src="https://www.riotimesonline.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/rt-chart-peru-corio-port-us-china-interest-2026-1.png" /> .8 billion with the US billion figure promoters had cited" /> Corío port investment: APN master plan versus the figure earlier cited by promoters (Chart: The Rio Times; data: APN via PortalPortuario, Perú Informa)

On 29 September, the APN asked ProInversión, the state agency that runs public-private partnerships, to assess the project and, if it agrees, start promoting it. The Arequipa regional government published that request on Tuesday 6 October.

The APN letter was signed by its board chairman, Abel Alvarado Huertas. Under the master plan, the terminal will be publicly owned, open to all users and of national scope.

Andina, the state news agency, reported that officials and business leaders meet for an investment presentation on Monday 12 October from 9 a.m. (10 a.m. ET) at the Hilton hotel in Lima’s Miraflores district. Sánchez, ProInversión and the APN are due to speak, and Mediterranean Shipping Company (MSC), the Geneva-based container line, is listed among the expected panel guests. ProInversión’s executive president, Luis Del Carpio Castro, is due to present the next steps.

What It Means for You

For US investors and port operators, Corío is an early chance to look at a large Pacific project before terms are set.

For Washington, the question is strategic. Chancay, which opened in 2024, gave China a major foothold on South America’s Pacific coast, and US officials have criticised that. Our earlier report, Peru Chancay Port: US Pressure Has Not Moved China, covers that dispute.

For traders in soya, minerals and other bulk goods, a southern port could shorten routes from Brazil and Bolivia to Asia. That depends on roads and railways that are not yet finished.

The risk is that interest does not become investment. Peru has announced large ports before that took years to start, and the project has no operator, no financing and no secured cargo.

What Is Not Known

Sánchez did not name the companies or say how firm their interest is. None of the groups has commented publicly, and their interest has not been independently confirmed.

It is not known whether ProInversión will formally take on the project, or when. The APN request is subject to the agency’s own evaluation.

It is not known what, if anything, officials will commit to at Monday’s presentation in Lima, or whether any of the interested groups will attend.

The timeline is long. Estimates by the consultancy Infraplan, cited by Perú Informa, suggest five to six years of structuring, promotion and building before the Corío port opens.

Frequently Asked Questions

Where is the Corío port planned?

In the district of La Punta de Bombón, in Islay province, Arequipa region, on Peru’s southern Pacific coast. The National Port Authority approved its master plan on 3 September 2026.

How much would the Corío port cost?

The official master plan puts the investment at more than US$800 million over three stages. Promoters had earlier cited a figure of about US$7 billion.

Are US companies investing in the Corío port?

Not yet. Arequipa’s governor says groups from the United States, China, India and the Netherlands are interested, but no company has been named and no tender has opened.

Sources: Gobierno Regional de Arequipa, APN request to ProInversión (6 October 2026); Perú Informa; Evidencia; Andina, 12 October presentation (9 October 2026); PortalPortuario, APN master plan.

World.title: Egypt Eyes US$5 Billion Trade With Indonesia
World.content:
Save Share In short Contents Listen Aa

RT Ask Rio Times 17 years of Latin America reporting, on demand. Ask Answers are generated from Rio Times reporting only — every claim links to its source article. Open the full Ask Rio Times → RT Ask Rio TimesCost of living, safety, visas across Latin America › RT Ask Rio Times 17 years of Latin America reporting, on demand. × Best for expats Cost of living Safest places Easy visas Tap a question, or type your own — the answer appears right here. Ask Open the full Ask Rio Times →

EGYPT · TRADE

Key Facts — The country Egypt is a close US security partner in North Africa and controls the Suez Canal, a main Asia–Europe shipping route.

— What happened In Jakarta on Sunday 11 October, Egypt’s President Sisi said he and Indonesia’s Prabowo Subianto agreed to aim for US$5 billion in trade by 2030.

— The starting point Indonesian figures put bilateral trade at US$2.38 billion in 2025, so the goal means more than doubling it in five years.

— The agreements The presidents witnessed four memoranda on fisheries, statistics, a strategic partnership action plan and visa exemption for official passports.

— The investment angle Indonesia’s sovereign wealth fund Danantara and an Egyptian state agency are asked to widen work on palm oil, phosphate fertilisers, energy and logistics.

— Still open Neither side has published a timetable, sector targets or financing for the US$5 billion goal.

Egypt and Indonesia want their bilateral trade to reach US$5 billion by 2030, more than double last year’s level. President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi set the target in Jakarta on Sunday 11 October after talks with Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto, the Egyptian presidency said.

For US readers, the visit shows a close American security partner building ties with the world’s most populous Muslim-majority country. Egypt is pitching itself as a factory floor for Arab and African markets, and it wants Indonesian money to help build it.

What Sisi and Prabowo Agreed in Jakarta

Sisi flew to Jakarta from Malaysia on Saturday 10 October for a two-day official visit. Talks at the Merdeka Palace, the Indonesian president’s official residence, followed on Sunday.

At a joint press conference, Sisi said in Arabic both sides would work to raise trade volume “to reach five billion dollars by 2030”. He added that Egypt wants Indonesian companies to increase their investments in the Egyptian market.

The two presidents then witnessed the signing of four memoranda of understanding, presidential spokesman Mohamed El-Shenawy said. They cover fisheries and maritime affairs, statistics, a strategic partnership action plan, and visa exemption for diplomatic, service and special passports.

A memorandum of understanding is a statement of intent rather than a binding treaty. Over lunch, Sisi told his host that the two countries had written “another new page” in their relations.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on Egypt Email address Follow Free. One email a day at most, and only when there is news. This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, Africa Intelligence. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

How Much the Two Countries Trade Today

Bilateral trade reached US$2.38 billion in 2025, according to Indonesian trade figures reported by Investor Trust, a Jakarta business outlet. Indonesia sold goods worth US$1.94 billion to Egypt and bought US$439.8 million in return.

That left Indonesia with a surplus of about US$1.5 billion. In the first half of 2026, bilateral trade already reached US$1.74 billion, almost three-quarters of the 2025 total.

Reaching US$5 billion by 2030 would still need growth of about 16% a year from the 2025 level. Over the five years to 2025, trade grew by about 6% a year, the same figures show.

In August, Indonesian Trade Minister Budi Santoso proposed talks on a preferential trade agreement and a free trade agreement with Egypt. A preferential deal cuts tariffs on a short list of goods, while a free trade agreement covers most trade.

Palm Oil, Fertilisers and a Sovereign Wealth Fund

The joint statement welcomes “tangible progress” between Danantara and the Future of Egypt for Sustainable Development agency. Danantara is Indonesia’s sovereign wealth fund, launched in February 2025 to hold the state’s stakes in large state-owned companies.

Future of Egypt is a state development authority that began under the armed forces and runs the New Delta land reclamation scheme. Egypt’s parliament voted in July 2026 to make it independent of the defence ministry.

The presidents pointed to openings for the two bodies in crude palm oil and its products, and in phosphate fertilisers and their raw materials.

They also asked the two bodies to look at infrastructure, energy, logistics and agribusiness. Indonesia is the world’s largest palm oil producer, while Egypt mines phosphate, a key raw material for fertiliser.

Sisi also pitched joint manufacturing in priority sectors. According to Daily News Egypt, both sides want Egypt to become a production and export hub for Arab, African and international markets.

Security, the Nile and Gaza

The joint statement commits both sides to deepen defence and security ties to strengthen their national capabilities. No arms contracts or values were announced.

On the Nile, Prabowo backed Egypt’s efforts to protect its water rights, the Egyptian spokesman said. Egypt has long opposed Ethiopia’s large hydropower dam on the Blue Nile, the river’s main tributary.

Sisi also recalled Prabowo’s presence at the Sharm el-Sheikh peace summit in October 2025, where a Gaza ceasefire document was signed. He called for full, safe and sustained humanitarian access to the Gaza Strip.

On the Gulf, the two presidents voiced deep concern about the continued escalation and widening hostilities. They called for immediate de-escalation and restraint.

What It Means for US Readers

Egypt is one of Washington’s closest Arab partners and a key mediator on Gaza. The joint statement backs full implementation of US President Donald Trump’s comprehensive plan to end the conflict in Gaza.

Trump attended the October 2025 ceasefire signing in Sharm el-Sheikh, the same event Prabowo joined. Indonesia also praised Egypt’s central role in getting humanitarian aid into Gaza.

For US investors, the trade target matters less as a number than as a signal of where Cairo seeks capital. Indonesian state money could join Gulf and Western investors in Egyptian farming, fertiliser and logistics projects.

Egypt is also opening state companies to outside investors. The state-owned Banque du Caire plans to sell 30% of its shares in November, another test of foreign appetite for Egyptian assets.

What Is Not Known

Neither government has published a timetable, sector targets or financing behind the US$5 billion bilateral trade goal. The full texts of the four memoranda have not been released.

In August, Indonesia proposed a second joint trade committee meeting before the end of 2026. No date has been announced.

It is also unclear whether the defence talks will lead to any arms purchases. Prices, volumes and company names for the palm oil and fertiliser projects have not been disclosed.

More: Egypt news in English, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

How much do Egypt and Indonesia trade now?

Bilateral trade reached US$2.38 billion in 2025, according to Indonesian figures. Most of it was Indonesian exports to Egypt, worth US$1.94 billion.

What did the two presidents sign in Jakarta?

On Sunday 11 October, they witnessed four memoranda of understanding. These cover fisheries, statistics, a strategic partnership action plan and visa exemption for official passports.

What is Danantara?

Danantara is Indonesia’s sovereign wealth fund, launched in February 2025 to hold the state’s stakes in large state-owned companies. The joint statement asks it to expand work with an Egyptian state agency on palm oil, fertilisers, energy and logistics.

Does the visa deal help tourists or business travellers?

No. The memorandum covers only diplomatic, service and special passports, which officials carry. Ordinary travellers still follow each country’s normal visa rules.

Why does a bilateral trade target between Egypt and Indonesia matter to Americans?

Egypt is a key US partner on Gaza and controls the Suez Canal. Its growing Asian ties shape where investment flows and which partners Cairo can lean on.

World.title: Peru Starts 119 Recounts in Lima Mayor Race
World.content:
Save Share In short Contents Listen Aa

The headquarters of the Jurado Nacional de Elecciones (JNE), Peru’s electoral jury, in central Lima (Photo: Ovruni, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons)

POLITICS · PERU

Key Facts — The country Peru, a major copper exporter, voted for mayors and regional governors on Sunday 4 October. Lima, the capital, has no runoff: the list with most votes wins.

— Why it matters The narrow race for the capital pits conservative Rafael López Aliaga’s party against Francis Allison’s. A legal fight over whether López Aliaga may take office again is building.

— Why now Special electoral courts begin public vote recounts on Monday 12 October, and a jury adviser has signalled the López Aliaga question may wait until January.

— What happened The National Elections Jury (JNE) lists 119 recount hearings from Monday 12 to Friday 16 October. The first starts at 8:30 a.m. Lima time (9:30 a.m. ET).

— The numbers With 92.919% of Lima tally sheets counted, Renovación Popular has 27.714% and Avanza País 26.833%, a gap of 0.881 points.

— What it means for you Nothing changes for visitors. City services run as normal while courts finish the count. The new city government takes office in January 2027.

— Still open Whether the recounts move the Lima result, and whether the jury hands López Aliaga the credentials to serve as mayor.

— Prediction markets Polymarket gives López Aliaga an 80% chance of winning the Lima mayor race, down from about 97% a week earlier (12 October, 2:28 a.m. ET).

Peru’s electoral courts start recounting disputed ballots on Monday 12 October, eight days after local elections. The recounts come as the race for Lima mayor stays too close to call. For foreign readers, the capital’s result also tests whether Peru’s ban on re-electing mayors can be sidestepped.

The National Elections Jury (JNE), Peru’s electoral court, lists 119 public recount hearings for the week on its website. The first is set for 8:30 a.m. at the court for southern Lima, on a polling table in Villa El Salvador. More hearings follow in Callao, Cusco, Ayacucho, Puno and Piura.

Correo reported on Sunday that 105 hearings had been scheduled by midday. The number grew overnight. The hearings are streamed on the JNE’s website and its TV channel.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Peru ranks 5th of 14 with 54.7 points. Strongest pillar: military means (71); weakest: future resources (37). Alignment group: Closer to Washington. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

Why the Lima Mayor Count Is Not Finished

The Lima Metropolitan count is the one most watched abroad. With 92.919% of the 26,351 tally sheets counted, the Renovación Popular list had 27.714% of valid votes on Sunday morning, Trome and Gestión reported. Avanza País, whose candidate is Francis Allison, had 26.833%.

Renovación Popular is the conservative party led by López Aliaga, who won the Lima mayoralty in 2022. Allison is a former mayor of the Lima district of Magdalena del Mar.

The rest of the sheets went to the special electoral courts, known as JEE. On 9 October the electoral office ONPE said 1,886 Lima sheets were still awaiting a ruling. Courts first compare each sheet with their own copy. Only when that fails do they order a recount.

Nationwide, the courts reviewed 6,964 flagged sheets and sent 421 to recount, Gestión reported on Saturday, citing a JNE statement. Another 70 were reported lost or destroyed. Jury president Roberto Burneo said recounts must end by 28 October.

The JNE schedule does not say whether any of this week’s hearings concern the capital’s mayoral race. Fifteen are before the Lima Centro court, with no polling table listed.

Peru's special electoral courts have scheduled 119 public recount hearings for 12 to 16 October. (Chart: The Rio Times; data: Jurado Nacional de Elecciones hearing schedule, read 12 October 2026, 06:20 UTC)

This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

The Credentials Question

The bigger dispute is legal. Peru’s Constitution bars mayors from immediate re-election. López Aliaga is registered on his party’s list as first councillor, not as the candidate for mayor.

“Running is prohibited, but being is not,” he told reporters on election night, Trome reported. “I am not running for mayor.”

On Sunday, Jorge Valdivia, who coordinates the JNE’s advisers, told Ojo Público that the courts would proclaim winners for the posts they ran for. The new council would then apply the municipalities law and ask the jury for credentials, he said. That points to January 2027, when councils take office.

Fernando Tuesta, a former ONPE chief and electoral expert, told La República the jury was “postponing” and “evading” a decision it should have made earlier. With no mayor, the first councillor would normally step in, he said, but the jury cannot give credentials to someone who is barred.

Ojo Público reported that Renovación Popular does not rule out a constitutional complaint against jury members. Allison has said he can still overturn a gap of less than one point. “We are fighting vote by vote,” he said, Trome reported, adding that he will accept the result.

What It Means for You

For travellers and residents, nothing changes this week. Lima’s city government keeps running, and the hearings are public court sessions, not street events.

For investors, the question is institutional. Peru has held national and local votes in 2026, and runoffs for regional governor are due on 6 December. A clear, lawful outcome in the capital would remove one source of dispute.

The risk runs the other way too. If the jury leaves the credentials decision to January, the capital could start 2027 with a legal fight over who is its mayor.

What Is Not Known

It is not known how many of the flagged Lima sheets will be recounted, or whose votes they hold. Burneo has said results could be proclaimed in the first week of November. Ojo Público reports mid-November.

It is also unclear whether the jury will rule directly on López Aliaga’s eligibility, or leave it to the new council. No formal JNE decision on that question has been published.

Background: Lima Mayor Race Lead Stays Under One Point and Peru Pushes Regional Runoff Back a Week to 6 December.

What Prediction Markets Say

On Polymarket, bets on the “Lima Mayoral Election Winner” gave López Aliaga an 80% chance at 2:28 a.m. ET on 12 October. That is down about nine points in a day and 17 points in a week. Allison stood at 4%. About US$525,000 has been traded on the market.

On Kalshi, which is regulated in the US by the CFTC, López Aliaga last traded at 84% and Allison at 15%, with about 25,500 contracts traded on López Aliaga.

Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

Frequently Asked Questions

When do Peru’s vote recounts start?

Public recount hearings start on Monday 12 October 2026. The JNE lists 119 hearings through Friday 16 October, and recounts must end by 28 October.

Who is leading the Lima mayor race?

With 92.919% of tally sheets counted, Rafael López Aliaga’s Renovación Popular list had 27.714% and Francis Allison’s Avanza País 26.833%.

Can López Aliaga become Lima mayor again?

It is not settled. Peru bars mayors from immediate re-election, and he ran as first councillor. A JNE adviser said the new council may have to decide in January 2027.

World.title: Guatemala Hosts US Scouts for Cartel Drills
World.content:
Save Share In short Contents Listen Aa

Rainforest around the ancient Maya city of Tikal in Petén, northern Guatemala (Photo: Rebecca Wilson, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons)

SECURITY · GUATEMALA

Key Facts — The country Guatemala borders Mexico, Belize, Honduras and El Salvador. Petén, its northernmost department, is largely rainforest along the Mexican and Belizean borders.

— Why it matters US military planners are preparing joint anti-cartel training on Guatemalan soil, part of Washington’s regional campaign against drug cartels.

— Why now The US Embassy announced the Petén reconnaissance mission on Sunday 11 October. It linked it to an anti-cartel initiative launched in March.

— What happened Chargé d’affaires Jorgan Andrews, Joint Task Force-Bravo and the defence attaché toured Petén. They gathered data for future combined training, the embassy said on 11 October.

— What it means for you No change to travel advice for Petén or the Tikal area has been announced. The mission signals deeper US security ties with Guatemala.

— Still open When the training will take place, how many US troops would take part, where exactly in Petén, and for how long.

A US team led by the embassy’s top diplomat has carried out a reconnaissance mission in Petén, Guatemala’s northern jungle department. The US Embassy said on Sunday 11 October that the Petén reconnaissance mission gathered data for future combined training against drug cartels. For US readers, it shows Washington’s anti-cartel campaign moving from conference declarations to planning on the ground in Central America.

The trip was led by Jorgan Andrews, the chargé d’affaires who heads the US Embassy in Guatemala City. He was joined by members of Joint Task Force-Bravo and by the embassy’s defence attaché, Colonel Rubiano.

Prensa Libre, a Guatemala City daily, reported that personnel from the Guatemalan Army also took part. It said the combined training planned for Petén would focus on the fight against drug trafficking.

What the Embassy Said

The embassy announced the mission in a post on X. “This operation gathered data for future combined training under the Americas Counter Cartel Conference (A3C) initiative,” it wrote in Spanish.

“United for regional security and to combat transnational threats,” the post added. The embassy did not give the date of the visit or name the places the team inspected.

Radio station La Red 106.1 reported that the Guatemalan Army described the United States as a key strategic partner and ally. The army said the relationship helps consolidate a shared commitment to regional security.

Joint Task Force-Bravo is a US military command based at Soto Cano Air Base in Honduras. Its US Army and Air Force units fly helicopter, medical and relief missions with partner countries across Central America.

In recent months its aircrews have supported a Honduran-led medical mission and delivered water tanks to remote villages in Panama, according to US military releases.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on Guatemala Email address Follow Free. One email a day at most, and only when there is news. This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

How the Anti-Cartel Push Began

The A3C label refers to the Americas Counter Cartel Conference. US Secretary of War Pete Hegseth hosted the conference at US Southern Command headquarters in Doral, Florida, on 5 March 2026.

Guatemala’s Defence Minister, Henry Sáenz, attended, according to the state news agency AGN. Sáenz heads the Defence Ministry in the government of President Bernardo Arévalo.

“Guatemala is present as a state committed to the defence of the Western Hemisphere,” Sáenz told the meeting, AGN reported. He said cartels erode sovereignty, distort economies and infiltrate state institutions.

Prensa Libre reported that the United States and nearly 20 Latin American and Caribbean countries signed a joint security declaration there. Mexico, Colombia and Brazil did not send delegations, the paper said.

Sáenz used the event to showcase Operation Cinturón de Fuego (“Belt of Fire”). It is a military deployment to tighten control of Guatemala’s border with Mexico, which he called the most porous and dangerous.

On 9 March, La Hora quoted Sáenz as saying in a radio interview that Washington had lifted a 50-year block. It had barred Guatemala from buying US military equipment. He said the army had about Q400 million (about US$52 million) for such purchases in 2026.

That conversion uses the Bank of Guatemala’s reference rate of 7.64157 quetzales per US dollar for Monday 12 October.

The purchases have since begun. On 21 September, AGN reported that Sáenz had received a shipment of US weapons after what the agency called a 47-year embargo.

A Guatemalan Kaibil soldier at a machine-gun range led by US Army Green Berets of the 7th Special Forces Group in Poptún, Petén, on 17 March 2026 (Photo: 1st Lt. Sarah Morgan, US Army, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons)

Why Petén Matters

Petén covers Guatemala’s far north and borders both Mexico and Belize. Its large forested areas and long, thinly guarded frontier make it hard to patrol.

Pressure on the border rose in February. Nemesio Oseguera Cervantes, known as “El Mencho”, leader of the Jalisco New Generation Cartel, died in a Mexican security operation in Jalisco.

Prensa Libre reported at the time that Guatemala then reinforced San Marcos and Huehuetenango, its western border departments, under the same operation. Sáenz said no Mexican armed groups had been detected inside Guatemala.

US forces already train in Petén. US Army photos show Green Berets of the 7th Special Forces Group training Guatemalan Kaibil special forces in Poptún, Petén, in March.

Guatemala is not alone in this shift. For related coverage, see Peru Sets 19 October Hearing on Shield of the Americas and US and 13 Nations Back Bolivia’s Antidrug Effort.

What It Means for You

For travellers, nothing changes for now. No authority has announced restrictions around Tikal, Flores or other visitor areas of Petén. Anyone heading there should still follow the latest US State Department advice.

For people tracking US policy, the Petén reconnaissance mission shows how the anti-cartel agenda is being put into practice. Planning teams on the ground usually come before exercises, equipment deliveries and longer cooperation deals.

For investors and businesses, closer security ties may strengthen Guatemala’s standing in Washington. Better control of the northern border could also help trade and tourism.

There is a counterweight. Foreign military activity is a sensitive subject in the region. In Chile and Peru, critics have questioned what US-led security pacts mean for national sovereignty.

What Is Not Known

The embassy has not said when the visit took place or which sites the team visited. Neither government has published a date for the training.

It is not known how many US personnel would take part or which Guatemalan units would join them. Nor is it known how long they would stay. No budget for the exercises has been disclosed.

The colonel’s full name has not been published. Nor have the exact terms of Guatemala’s commitments under the March declaration.

The sources reviewed by early Monday 12 October include no separate Defence Ministry statement detailing the mission.

Frequently Asked Questions

What was the US reconnaissance mission in Petén?

A US team led by chargé d’affaires Jorgan Andrews gathered data in Petén. Its aim was to plan future combined training with Guatemala’s army.

What is the A3C initiative?

It stems from the Americas Counter Cartel Conference, hosted by US Secretary of War Pete Hegseth in Florida on 5 March 2026. Guatemala joined its joint security declaration there.

Will US troops be based in Guatemala?

Neither government has said so. The embassy described the trip as data gathering for future combined training, with no dates, troop numbers or locations announced.

Sources: US Embassy Guatemala post of 11 October as published by Prensa Libre; La Red 106.1; AGN; Prensa Libre (5 March); La Hora; Prensa Libre (24 February); AGN (21 September); Joint Task Force-Bravo (DVIDS); Banco de Guatemala.
