NEW DELHI: Jantar Mantar on Monday was denotified as a designated protest site, with three alternative venues designated for demonstrations in Delhi.In a notice issued by Delhi Police commissioner Anurag Kumar, the police said the ministry of home affairs had constituted a committee to examine suitable alternative venues for citizens to exercise their right to organise protests and demonstrations.The decision was taken based on the committeeâs recommendations."Ministry of home affairs, Government of India, had constituted a Committee to examine alternative proper venues for citizen's right for organizing protest/demonstrations in place of the existing designated site. Based on the Committee's recommendations, Jantar Mantar as a protest venue has been de-notified," the notice reads.The three venues designated for organising protests and demonstrations are Ramlila ground in Central Delhi, Burari Ground in North Delhi and CBD Ground in East Delhi. The Delhi Police said a detailed and revised standard operating procedure (SOP) governing protests at the three venues would be issued separately.The order partially modifies the earlier Standing Order No. L&O/48/22, dated April 28, 2022."Detailed and revised SOP for organizing protest/demonstrations at these three venues will be issued separately. This is in partial modification of earlier Standing Order No.L&O/48/22 dated 28.04.2022," the notice reads further.The move comes amid ongoing massie protests in the national capital demanding the resignation of chief election commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

World.title: How India travels: A tale of two wheels and many divides
World.content:
File image of urban traffic

India on the move

Rural-urban divide

Two Indias, Two Ways to Travel

Students take the bus, workers take the bike

Men ride, women walk

The Gender Divide in Indiaâs Commute

Short commutes, steeper city bills

City Travel Comes at a Price

The work clock

For long trips, the bus still rules

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

A quarter-century ago, an advertising campaign presented the two-wheeler as a symbol of âNaye Bharat ki Nayi Tasveerâ. But is the India of 2026 still commuting mainly on two-wheelers, has it moved to cars, or are more people walking? The answer depends a great deal on which states people live in, whether they are in a village or a city, and on their gender. All three, in varying degrees, shape how people get around and how much they pay for it.Among some of the extremes featured in Indiaâs National Household Travel Survey, in Puducherry, 92.7% of workers use a two-wheeler as their primary mode. In Nagaland, more than seven in ten walk. West Bengal has the highest published bicycle share, Ladakh stands out for buses, and Sikkim for cars. Conducted from July 2025 to June 2026, the survey covered 4,92,023 households and 18,44,179 people aged six and above.At the national level, the old two-wheeler image still rings true, though the averages hide big regional differences. Among workers who travel at least 1km to work, 42.6% mainly use a two-wheeler, 28.3% walk and 10.7% cycle. The average one-way trip to a fixed workplace takes 25 minutes, and travel costs about â¹785 a month per worker.Between India and Bharat, the numbers shift substantially. In rural India, workers are split almost evenly between two-wheelers at 37.1% and walking at 36.6%.In cities, the balance tips firmly towards the engine, presumably because of longer distances. Two-wheelers rise to 52.3% and walking falls to 13.5%. Autos, buses and cars all carry a bigger share too.The metro and local-train story is overwhelmingly urban. The surveyâs Train/Monorail/Tram category, which includes metro rail and suburban or local trains, carries 5% of urban workers but just 0.4% of rural ones. In urban Maharashtra, home to Mumbaiâs suburban railway, the share is 20.7%. It is 16.5% in urban West Bengal and 14.4% in Delhi, known for its metro network.The survey reports Rail separately. That category accounts for just 0.2% of workers nationally, 0.2% in rural India and 0.3% in urban India.Students and workers commute very differently. In villages, 40.5% of students walk and 18.9% cycle. In cities, buses at 33.7% and autos at 14.4% play a bigger role. Nationally, 37% of students walk, 29.5% take a bus and 15.8% cycle, while only 6.7% use a two-wheeler. Among workers, buses account for just 6.7%, exactly the share two-wheelers have among students.The contrast is sharpest in Kerala, where buses carry 72% of students but 24.9% of workers. Age changes the picture too. Students aged 15 to 29 walk far less than those aged 6 to 14, 22.2% against 47.3%, and cycle more, 21.4% against 11.9%.Among workers, 47.1% of men use a two-wheeler to get to work. Among women, it is 18.4%. About half of female workers, 50.6%, walk, against 24.1% of men. Women are also much more likely to take the bus, 14% against 5.3%.It would be easy to put this down to rural India, where more people walk. But the divide holds in cities too. There, 57% of male workers use two-wheelers, against 25.8% of women, while women are twice as likely as men to walk, 24% against 11.6%. The bicycle divide is even starker in relative terms. Among workers, 12.3% of men cycle to work but only 1.7% of women do.Yet among students, the sexes are much closer. Some 17.7% of male students cycle, against 13.4% of female students. Odisha makes the contrast particularly striking. Female students there cycle almost as often as male students, 32.8% against 34%. Among workers, though, the Odisha gap opens up. Some 25.5% of men cycle to work, against 5.8% of women.Most work commutes are under half an hour. Some 83.4% of workers travelling to a fixed workplace get there within 30 minutes. Students do even better, with 87.6% reaching school or college within half an hour.However, travelling in cities is much costlier. The average urban trip to work takes 27 minutes, just four more than in villages, but costs â¹1,044 a month against â¹612, about 71% more. Urban students pay about 71% more too, even though their average trip is a shade shorter, 22 minutes against 23 in villages.Even within cities, there are stark differences. Workers in urban West Bengal and urban Delhi spend about the same time getting to work, 36 and 35 minutes on average. But the urban West Bengal worker spends about â¹825 a month, while the urban Delhi worker spends about â¹2,081, roughly two and a half times as much.Urban West Bengal also has a much bigger long-commute tail. Some 13% need over an hour to commute, against 4.1% across urban India. Hence, lower monthly spending there does not necessarily mean a quicker journey.Across India, 56.5% leave for work between 8am and 10am. In Mizoram and Ladakh, some 97.1% and 95.1% of commuters leave between 8am and 10am.Evenings vary even more. Across India, 31.1% leave work at 6pm or later. In Tamil Nadu it is nearly half, 48.9%, with Gujarat at 45.2% and Delhi at 44.6%. Men are more than twice as likely as women to be leaving that late, 34.1% against 16%.Take work and study out of the picture and far fewer people step out at all. On a given day, 18.7% of people aged six and above travelled at least 1km for some other reason, 23.8% of males and 13.3% of females.They also get there differently. Among men making such trips, 40.1% use a two-wheeler, against 17.6% of women. Among women, 30.4% take an auto or e-rickshaw, against 12.7% of men. For women, autos and e-rickshaws play much the same role that two-wheelers do for men.In the 28 travel days before the survey, 11.3% of households made an overnight trip of 50km or more that kept a member away from home for more than 24 hours. More than half of these households, 55.8%, used the bus as their primary mode.The separately reported Rail category comes next at 17.7%. Cars account for 15.1% and two-wheelers 8.8%. Another 3.3% fall under Train/Monorail/Tram. Just 0.6% travelled by air.Few of these trips were about work. Some 70.2% of households making overnight trips travelled for socialising, communication or religious purposes.How far are people travelling? The answer is not provided in the details released so far. The survey collected trip distances, as well as information on licences, household vehicles and bus or rail passes, but none of these appears in the released estimate tables.A quarter-century after the âNaya Bharatâ pitch, the two-wheeler still leads the national picture. But the survey shows how much that picture hides, and the big missing piece is how far India travels. At a time when there is demand for metros in every Tier 2 city and road and rail connectivity is better than ever, the full data, when released, will help policymakers make more informed decisions about how to prioritise Indiaâs transport needs.

World.title: Delhi protests: SC on Tuesday to hear pleas on attacks on protesters, lawyers
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Monday agreed to hear two separate pleas on Tuesday concerning the October 10 and 11 protests in Delhi, including allegations of attacks on lawyers and protesters and disruptions to the functioning of courts.

A bench comprising Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mahadevan said it would not allow the court to become a political battleground while agreeing to list a plea seeking action against alleged hooligans accused of attacking lawyers and protesters.

âPrivate hooligans are not being stoppedâ: Senior advocate seeks action

Senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan mentioned a plea seeking action against alleged hooligans who, he said, were attacking lawyers, young people and other protesters without facing police action.

He also raised concerns over videos purportedly showing the alleged attackers recording their actions and proudly displaying them.

âPrivate hooligans are not being stopped. They are making videos and proudly proclaiming what they have done. I am shocked. Iâve never seen a senior advocate being dragged on the streets. At some point, the Bench will have to come to the rescue of the Bar and young children,â Sankaranarayanan said.





Referring to restrictions imposed under Section 163, he urged the court to ask the police to exercise restraint.

âAt a time when our senior advocates are being dragged through the streets, at such times I must urge the Court to convey to the police to exercise restraint,â he said.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

SCBA seeks protection for lawyers

Separately, the SCBA mentioned its plea seeking directions to ensure that lawyers can move freely and court proceedings are not disrupted during protests.

SCBA president and senior advocate Pradeep Rai said political parties should not interfere with lawyersâ work or affect the functioning of courts.

CJI Surya Kant said he had already appealed to the authorities to ensure there was no impediment to court functioning or the movement of lawyers amid the restrictions imposed during the protests.

The matters are now scheduled to be heard on Tuesday.

World.title: 'Keep getting messages': Rahul Gandhi's big claim, and a message for CEC Gyanesh Kumar
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha

on Monday levelled serious allegations against chief election commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar and the Narendra Modi-led Centre, claiming that around 200 government officials were in touch with the opposition and sharing information, including officials from the Enforcement Directorate (ED), Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) and the ministry of external affairs.

Speaking at a press conference ahead of the INDIA bloc's planned march to the

, Rahul said, "I want to tell

that 200 officials of your government are in touch with us and informing us, including those in the ED, CBI, foreign ministry..."

Stepping up his attack on the poll body chief, Rahul claimed Kumar was having "sleepless nights" amid the opposition's campaign against alleged electoral irregularities.

Responding to a reporter's question on whether he had communicated with the CEC, Rahul claimed that he had been "getting messages".

When asked if he had a message for Gyanesh Kumar, Rahul said, "You have done a crime, and you are not the main criminal. You made a mistake and you are not the mind behind the mistake. We are after the people who are behind what you did. It is very easy for you, resign and get out of the way. We know that you have been forced by the Prime Minister, Amit Shah, Ajit Doval," Rahul Gandhi said

The former Congress president also questioned why Kumar had not resigned, claiming that the opposition was receiving information from several sources.





"Why is all this happening? Because we are only asking the question raised by two Election Commissioners: why is Gyanesh Kumar not resigning? These days, we are receiving information from everywhere. Gyanesh Kumar, we know your situation. We know you are unable to sleep at night, and do not worry, we will not spare you. I am telling you directly that you will not escape as Election Commissioner because of what is happening.

"

Rahul also accused the Centre of turning Delhi into a fortress to protect the CEC, as INDIA bloc leaders prepared to march towards the Supreme Court to demand Kumar's removal over alleged "vote chori" and concerns surrounding the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

He said a public movement against alleged electoral irregularities had been under way in Delhi for the past four to five days, with protesters demanding Kumar's removal.

"Since last 4-5 days, public movement is on in Delhi against 'vote chori', seeking CEC removal," the Raebareli MP said.

Referring to the police action during the October 10 protests, Rahul alleged that authorities were preventing people from reaching the national capital by stopping trains and buses and forcing passengers to get off.

"People are being stopped from reaching Delhi. Trains and buses are being stopped, and people are being made to get off.

Delhi has been turned into a fortress, with 20,000 to 30,000 police personnel deployed everywhere. Now, think about how powerful this is. But our strategy is different," the former Congress chief said.

Questioning the security arrangements, Rahul accused the government of making a "grave mistake" by protecting Kumar. He argued that the heavy police deployment would only help the opposition draw attention to its allegations against the CEC and the Centre.

"We want 20,000 to 30,000 police personnel deployed on the streets. The government is committing a grave mistake, because we want to show the country that Modi ji wants to ensure the security of Gyanesh Kumar... The more he is protected, the more we will ultimately reach his controller... We are receiving reports that police personnel are distressed because they are being ordered to beat up young people, while instructions are being issued to give RSS members a free hand.

"

Rahul further claimed that some police personnel supported the opposition's campaign and wanted it to continue.

"I am happy to tell you that 50% of the police personnel, and I am counting them, are telling us that what you are doing is right and that we should continue..."

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

He also alleged that security personnel and ordinary citizens were increasingly opposed to the government's handling of the protests.

"Police, ITBP, CRPF, the people of India are on one side and Narendra Modi, Amit Shah, Ajit Doval, Gyanesh Kumar, and 4-5 members of the Election Commission who are facilitating 'vote chori' and hijacking the country are on the other side.

We are increasing this divide..."

Rahul said the opposition's resistance had been building for years and was now taking a more concrete form.

"There was resistance from 12 years but it is getting crystallised now," he said.

He also announced that INDIA bloc leaders would approach the Supreme Court on Monday with a petition against the CEC over alleged "vote chori".

The press conference came ahead of the INDIA bloc's planned march to the Supreme Court, with opposition leaders seeking Kumar's removal amid mounting criticism of the SIR exercise.

World.title: ‘Salt rubbed into wounds’: 3 men allege electric shocks, torture at BJP MLA’s house in UP
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Police in Uttar Pradeshâs Moradabad are investigating allegations that three men were illegally confined and tortured at the residence of BJP MLA Sushant Singh over a missing gold bracelet belonging to the legislatorâs son, PTI reported citing officials.

The complainants have sought the registration of an FIR against six named persons, including the MLAâs aides, and nine unidentified individuals. However, no case had been registered so far, Moradabad SP (Rural) Kunwar Akash Singh said, adding that action would be taken after an investigation.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

According to the victimsâ family, Atul and Lavesh, who worked as domestic help at the legislatorâs house, and their friend Ramu were held captive and tortured over the suspected theft of the gold bracelet.

Ramuâs mother, Omwati, alleged that an aide of the MLA took her son from their home on October 7, while Atul and Lavesh were already being held at the residence.

She claimed that the three men were hung upside down, beaten with belts, subjected to electric shocks and had salt rubbed into their wounds.

All three were admitted to a hospital in Kashipur. Officials said Ramuâs condition was critical.

Sushant Singh dismissed the allegations as baseless, maintaining that the domestic workers had only been questioned about the missing bracelet and had not been assaulted.

Moradabad MP and Samajwadi Party leader Ruchi Veera demanded immediate justice for the victims and strict action against those responsible.

Police said further action would follow the investigation.

World.title: 'They are inconveniencing common public': Yogi Adityanath slams INDIA bloc for 'blaming EC when they lose'
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Uttar Pradesh chief minister

on Monday slammed the

and the INDIA bloc amid their planned protest march against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation, saying "it is surprising that if they win elections, it is their capability, but if they lose, they blame EVMs, EC.

"

Speaking to ANI, Adityanath urged the opposition to change its conduct and leadership, alleging that its response to election results reflected a lack of trust in constitutional bodies.

"They are inconveniencing the common public by creating anarchy. They are also attempting to question the constitutional institutions of the country. It is surprising that if they win elections, it is their capability. But if they lose, they blame EVMs, EC," he said.

"Such conduct has become part of Congress' intent. They should change their corrupt conduct and their distrustful leadership. They should not spread anarchy in India or attempt to question the constitutional bodies in India," he added.

The UP chief minister further warned that people would not tolerate such actions for long and said the Congress could face political consequences if it continued with the same approach.





"People will not accept this anarchy, they will not tolerate this for long. If they continue like this, they will have to lose whatever they are left with," he added.

Adityanath's remarks came as the INDIA bloc prepared to hold a protest march to the

on Monday. Leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha

Rahul Gandhi

called on students, civil society organisations and opposition parties to join the march.

"12th October, India marches peacefully as one to the Supreme Court.

Students, civil society organisations, opposition parties: Please join us to defend our democracy," Rahul had earlier said.

The Congress MP had announced the protest alleging that Delhi Police personnel and BJP workers had used violence against students and women during a protest led by CJP. The protest had demanded the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

The entry and exit gates of six metro stations: Patel Chowk, Janpath, Rajiv Chowk, Mandi House, Central Secretariat and Barakhamba Road, were scheduled to remain closed from 6 am to 4 pm on October 12 for security reasons.

World.title: Anti-CEC row LIVE: Delhi Police denotify Jantar Mantar as protest site; suggest three new locations
World.content:
Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant on Sunday (October 11, 2026) declined a request by the Leader of the Opposition, Rahul Gandhi, for a meeting on Monday (October 12, 2026). Sources said the meeting was declined as the issues likely to be raised were already sub judice in the Supreme Court. Besides, the court cannot intervene in matters of governance and functioning of the state on its administrative side.

Also read: Protests in Delhi: What are the rules and processes in place? | Explained
